rows.topic: Did Christ have a biological father?
rows.claude_r1:
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Jesus had no biological father

**Position.** On the KJV text, the child Jesus had a mother, Mary, and no human biological father. Joseph was her husband and the child's legal and caring guardian, but not his begetter. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost."

## 1. The conception is stated as a conception without a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** The Greek is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου), "out of the Holy Spirit." *Ek* (G1537) marks source or origin. The source of the conception is named, and it is not Joseph. *Synelthein* (συνελθεῖν, G4905, "to come together") is the word for the couple's coming together, and the text puts the pregnancy *before* it.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek *gennēthen* (γεννηθέν, "begotten, conceived") is joined to *ek pneumatos*. The same verb that elsewhere names a father's act is here assigned to the Holy Ghost.
**[L4]** From the *ek* of source in Matthew 1:18 and the repeated *gennēthen ek pneumatos* in Matthew 1:20, the conceiving is assigned to the Holy Ghost and to no man. The text names only Mary and the Holy Ghost as the two terms of the conception.

## 2. Mary's own question and the answer she was given

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (γινώσκω, G1097) is "to know," used here of sexual knowledge. It is present tense: she is presently knowing no man. *Parthenos* (παρθένος, G3933) in Luke 1:27 means "virgin," and Mary is called "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." *Episkiazō* (ἐπισκιάζω, G1982) means "to overshadow." It is not the word of marital union. "Therefore" (*dio*, διό) makes the divine conception the ground of the title "Son of God."
**[L4]** Mary's question, which asks how conception can occur when she knows no man, is answered by naming the Holy Ghost's coming and not any man's. The answer excludes a human begetter because the answer supplies a different cause for the birth.

## 3. Joseph's conduct shows that he was not the father

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
**[L2]** *Apolysai* (ἀπολῦσαι, G630) is "to dismiss, to put away." Joseph was minded to dismiss a wife already found with child, so he knew the child was not his.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." *Ginōskō* (G1097) is imperfect (*eginōsken*): he was not knowing her, and "till" (*heōs*, G2193) runs to the birth.
**[L4]** Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph acting as a man who knew he was not the father. Matthew 1:25 shows that he had no relations with Mary through the time of the birth. Together these two verses close off Joseph as biological father.

## 4. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
**[L2]** The verb *egennēsen* (ἐγέννησεν, G1080, "begat") runs through Matthew 1:2-15 as "A begat B." At the last step the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē* (ἐγεννήθη, "was born"). The relative pronoun *hēs* (ἧς, "of whom") is feminine singular, so it refers to Mary and not to Joseph. Joseph is called *ton andra Marias* (τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, "the husband of Mary").
**[L3]** Matthew 1:20 calls Joseph "thou son of David" and Matthew 1:25 says he "called his name JESUS." Joseph's role is given as taking Mary and naming the child, not begetting him. Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." *Enomizeto* (ἐνομίζετο, G3543) means "was thought, was supposed," so the Joseph connection is marked as a supposition, not a fact.
**[L4]** The text carries the line to Joseph, switches from active "begat" to passive "was born," and shifts the pronoun to the feminine. This gives Joseph legal standing in the line and Mary the only birth-giving relation.

## 5. Prophecy and the body prepared

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
**[L2]** *Almah* (עַלְמָה, H5959) is a young woman of marriageable age, unmarried. The sign is that she *conceives* (*harah*, הָרָה, "is with child") and *bears*.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." Matthew uses *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") for the same prophecy. Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." The phrase is *genomenon ek gynaikos* (γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός, "come to be out of a woman"). Only the woman is named as source.
**[L4]** Isaiah 7:14 as Matthew 1:23 applies it, together with Galatians 4:4, presents the birth as from a woman and a prophetic virgin with no human father named. This matches the "seed of the woman" language of Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed" (*zera*, זֶרַע, H2233, "seed").

## 6. Jesus' own speech

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
**[L3]** Luke 2:49: "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Mary says "thy father" of Joseph, and the child answers by pointing to "my Father" in the temple. Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him."
**[L2]** In Luke 2:49 *Patros* (πατρός, G3962) is "father" and the possessive is "my." The child redirects the title from the household to God.
**[L4]** Luke 2:48 uses "thy father" in the sense of the household's recognised father, and Luke 2:49 corrects the direction of the title. Together these show the title in Luke 2:48 is the ordinary one for a guardian. This sense is the one Luke 3:23 qualifies with "as was supposed."

## Anticipated objections

- John 6:42, "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" is what the crowd said. It reports the people's understanding, which is the "supposed" of Luke 3:23.
- Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh," names David's descent and does not name Joseph as begetter. Matthew 1:20 calls Joseph "son of David," and Luke 1:32 says the Lord God "shall give unto him the throne of his father David," which speaks of the throne.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. The conception is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost" with a named source and no human agent. Footing: Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], *ek pneumatos hagiou* and *gennēthen* [L2], *synelthein* "before they came together" [L3].
2. Mary was a virgin who knew no man, and the angel's answer supplies a divine cause. Footing: Luke 1:34 [L1], *ginōskō* and *parthenos* [L2], Luke 1:35 "overshadow" and "therefore" [L3].
3. Joseph knew the child was not his, and he did not know Mary until the birth. Footing: Matthew 1:19 [L1], *apolysai* [L2], Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till" [L3].
4. The genealogy shifts from "begat" to "was born" with a feminine "of whom," and Luke 3:23 calls the connection "supposed." Footing: Matthew 1:16 [L1], *egennēsen / egennēthē / hēs* [L2], Luke 3:23 *enomizeto* [L3].
5. Scripture traces the birth to a woman, a virgin, and her seed. Footing: Isaiah 7:14 [L1], *almah* [L2], Galatians 4:4 and Matthew 1:23 [L3].
6. Jesus had no human biological father; he was conceived by the Holy Ghost in Mary, and Joseph was her husband and his guardian, not his begetter. Footing: links 1-5 [L4] resting on Matthew 1:18, 1:20, Luke 1:34-35, Matthew 1:25 [L1/L3] and *ek*, *ginōskō*, *egennēthē* [L2].

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# Challenge: the seed is David's according to the flesh, and the named father is Joseph

The defender's keystone, **D6**, says "Jesus had no human biological father." I answer from the rows. The promise names a seed that comes out of a man's body. The text names one man as father: Joseph, of the house of David. Each of the defender's links D1 to D5 reads a verse past what it says.

## My declared chain

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's body.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12 says: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." The seed comes from David's own body.
- [L3] Acts 2:30 says: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- [L3] Romans 1:3 says: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- [L2] *Osphys* (G3751) means "loins." It is the word in Acts 2:30. It is also the word of Hebrews 7:10, "he was yet in the loins of his father," where a man's descendants are counted in a father. *Sperma* (G4690, "seed") in Romans 1:3 carries *kata sarka*, "according to the flesh."
- [L4] The loins-word and the seed-word, both marked "according to the flesh," require a flesh seed out of David's line through a man's loins.

**C2. Descent is counted by the father's house, and the text names the father.**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14 says: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L3] Numbers 1:18 says the tribes "declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Ezra 2:59 shows the other side: those who "could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel," were left out.
- [L3] The man of that house is named. Luke 2:4 says Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David." The angel says in Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David." Mary herself says in Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The disciple says in John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
- [L3] Mary's kin is given as Elisabeth, "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36), and Elisabeth "was of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5).
- [L4] Descent that is "evident," counted by the father's house, is made evident through the man the rows name, Joseph of David's house. It is not made evident through Mary, whose stated kin is of Aaron.

**C3. Knowing is the canon's stated means of begetting, and Joseph and Mary were husband and wife.**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1 says: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L3] They were husband and wife from the espousal. Matthew 1:19 calls him "Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20 says "Mary thy wife." Deuteronomy 22:24 calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife."
- [L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is the same verb in Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25.
- [L4] Joseph, of David's house, knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins. This rests on C1's seed, C2's named father, Genesis 4:1's means, and the husband-and-wife rows.

## Against the defender's links

**D1 ("no human agent")**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20 says: "that which is conceived [Gr. begotten] in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] John 1:13 says of believers: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." 1 John 5:1 says: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."
- [L2] These rows join the same verb, *gennaō* ("beget"), to the same *ek* ("out of"), with God as the source. They are said of men who had human fathers.
- [L4] So "begotten ... of" God is covenant origin, and it stands beside a human father. Romans 1:3 adds *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh") when flesh descent is meant. Matthew 1:20 does not add it.
- [L3] The angel's "for" (*gar*, "for, because") gives the reason for the command "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." The child is the seed God claims: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14).

**D2 (Mary "knew no man," so the answer excludes a begetter)**
- [L1] Luke 1:34 says: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *Ginōskō* here is present tense. It states her condition when the angel spoke.
- [L3] The angel's verbs show presence and power, not begetting. *Eperchomai* ("come upon") is the verb of Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses." *Episkiazō* ("overshadow"; G1982: 5 verses) is the cloud of Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them," and Peter's shadow in Acts 5:15.
- [L3] The title "Son" already stands with the throne before her question. Luke 1:32 says: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The same pairing appears in 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him to be my son." Solomon had a father, David.

**D3 ("he knew the child was not his")**
- [L1] Matthew 1:19 says he was "minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] *Eboulēthē* means "was minded," a word of intent. Its stated grounds are "being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example." It contains no verb of knowing.
- [L3] Matthew 1:25 says "knew her not till she had brought forth." *Heōs* ("till") marks the span up to the birth, and it comes after "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24). Deuteronomy 20:7 names that taking as its own step: "betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- [L4] So Matthew 1:18's "before they came together" dates the finding before the taking into his house. Matthew 1:25 covers the pregnancy after the taking. Both fit C3.

**D4 (the passive verb and "supposed")**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16 says: "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- [L2] *Egennēthē ex hēs* means "was born of her." It names the mother of the birth and does not narrate the begetting.
- [L3] Luke uses *enomizeto* in Luke 3:23. It is the verb form of Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made." Luke 3:23 stands with Luke's own narration: "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27) and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41).

**D5 ("woman ... her seed")**
- [L1] Galatians 4:4 says "made of a woman."
- [L3] Matthew 11:11 says: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13).
- [L3] "Her seed" (Genesis 3:15) has the same form as Hagar's "thy seed" (Genesis 16:10). Hagar's son was Abraham's.
- [L2] Isaiah 7:14 uses *almah* (H5959, "young woman"; 7 verses). Its sign is bounded in Ahaz's day by Isaiah 7:16 and Isaiah 8:3-4. There, "I went unto [Heb. approached] the prophetess; and she conceived."

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

1. **LINK D1:** "the conceiving is assigned to the Holy Ghost and to no man."
   - PRESSED WITH: John 1:13; 1 John 5:1; Romans 1:3. *Gennaō ek* God is said of men who had fathers, and only Romans 1:3 carries "according to the flesh."
2. **LINK D2:** "The answer excludes a human begetter because the answer supplies a different cause."
   - PRESSED WITH: Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34; 1 Chronicles 28:6. These are the angel's verbs of power and presence, and a "my son" title that stands beside a named father.
3. **LINK D3:** "so he knew the child was not his."
   - PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:19 (*eboulēthē*, intent, with its two stated grounds); Matthew 1:24; Deuteronomy 20:7.
4. **LINK D5:** "Only the woman is named as source."
   - PRESSED WITH: Matthew 11:11 with Luke 1:13; Genesis 16:10.
5. **LINK D6:** "Jesus had no human biological father."
   - PRESSED WITH: 2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30; Hebrews 7:14 with Numbers 1:18; Luke 2:48.
   - The defender must show how a seed "out of thy bowels," "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh," is "evident" by the father's house while the father whom Mary names is set aside.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 2, RESPONSE

# Round 2: Jesus had no human biological father

The challenger's chain rests on one move: wherever the text says "seed of David," "loins," or "father," it must mean Joseph's body. I take C1 to C3 first, then the five pressed premises.

## A. Answer to C1: the seed "according to the flesh"

**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
**[L2]** *Osphys* (G3751, "loins") names descent in general. The challenger's own witness shows this. **[L1]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Levi was in Abraham's loins several generations back, so "loins" does not require the immediate father's body. *Sarx* (G4561, "flesh") is glossed on the sheet as "the body ... or as the means of kindred." The flesh of kindred is the body, and Mary supplies a body.
**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." *Genomenon ek gynaikos* (G1096, "come to be," with "out of a woman") says that Jesus' flesh came out of her. Romans 1:3 says "made of the seed of David according to the flesh," and the "made" is the same *ginomai* verb of Galatians 4:4.
**[L4]** Acts 2:30, Hebrews 7:10 and Galatians 4:4 make "fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" mean David's body-line reaching Jesus through the woman he was "made of." Flesh descent from David is therefore met by Mary. It does not need Joseph's begetting.

**[L1]** Luke 1:32, said to Mary before the conception: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
**[L2]** *Patros* (G3962, "father") is used here of David, many generations back. In the same message that announces the conception, "father" is lineal, not immediate.
**[L4]** So "thy father" in Luke 2:48, which the challenger presses, does not have to mean begetter. The word's range includes ancestor and household head.

**[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
**[L3]** Verse 14 gives the sonship in covenant terms: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son." The same promise reaches Solomon in 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son."
**[L2]** *Bachar* (H977, "choose") is election. Luke 1:35 differs: **[L1]** "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." *Dio* (διό, "wherefore") grounds the title in the cause just named, the Holy Ghost coming on her. For Solomon the title rests on God's choice. For the child in Luke 1:35 it rests on the conception.
**[L4]** The Solomon parallel therefore fails on its own wording. Solomon is "chosen," while Jesus is "therefore ... called the Son of God" because of how he is conceived.

## B. Answer to C2: "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda"

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." The verse names the tribe, not the begetter.
**[L3]** Ezra 2:61 gives the precedent for counting through a wife's line: "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name." Matthew 1:21 gives Joseph's act: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25 says "he called his name JESUS."
**[L2]** *Kaleō* (G2564, "to call, name") is the act by which Joseph owns the child into his house and line.
**[L4]** Ezra 2:61 shows the canon recognising a line through a naming legal head, and Matthew 1:21 and 1:25 give Joseph that act. Joseph's place in the register therefore rests on being the legal head and namer.

**[L3]** The challenger's use of Elisabeth is weak. Luke 1:36 gives "thy cousin Elisabeth," and Luke 1:5 says "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron." A cross-tribe kinship by marriage has precedent in 2 Chronicles 22:11: "the wife of Jehoiada the priest." The text does not state that Mary is not of David. It states only that her kin by marriage is of Aaron.

**[L1]** There is a barrier to Joseph as begetter. Matthew 1:11: "Josias begat Jechonias." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Matthew 1:16 puts Joseph in this line.
**[L3]** Jeremiah 22:30: "for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
**[L2]** *Zera* (H2233, "seed") in the Jeremiah verse is the same word the challenger relies on in the promise to David.
**[L4]** Matthew 1:12 and 1:16 place Joseph in Jechonias' line, and Jeremiah 22:30 withholds the throne from his seed. A son begotten by Joseph would be of that seed. The text that carries Joseph in the line also keeps the throne from the seed that line produces, so Joseph is legal head and not begetter.

## C. Answer to C3 and to the D3 press: no window for Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *Synerchomai* (G4905, "to come together") is the couple's union. The pregnancy is found before it.
**[L1]** Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife."
**[L2]** *Paralambanō* (G3880, "receive near, associate with oneself") is the taking into his house.
**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is the verb of Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." *Heōs* (G2193, "until") runs to the birth.
**[L4]** The three verses close the timeline. The conception was found before the coming together (1:18). After the taking, he knew her not until the birth (1:25). The challenger proposes that Matthew 1:25 covers only the pregnancy after the taking, with Deuteronomy 20:7 as the separate step. That concedes my point, because by the challenger's own account no moment remains in which Joseph's knowing could have preceded the conception. The challenger's husband-and-wife rows (Matthew 1:19, 1:20, Deuteronomy 22:24) show the legal bond, not the act. Genesis 4:1 makes the act, not the bond, the means, and Matthew 1:25 denies the act through the birth.

**On Joseph's mind:** I rest the weight on the angel's answer. **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *Gar* (G1063, "for") gives the reason. The reason is the source of the conception. If Joseph were the source, there would be nothing for the angel to explain.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:19 shows the case that needed explaining: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man] ... was minded to put her away privily." *Apolyō* (G630, "dismiss, divorce") is what a husband does to a wife found with child by another.
**[L4]** The "fear not ... for" structure of Matthew 1:20 only makes sense if Joseph was not the father.

## D. Pressed premise 1: John 1:13, 1 John 5:1, Romans 1:3

**[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
**[L2]** *Haima* (G129, "blood"), *thelēma* (G2307, "will") and *anēr* (G435, "man") are set against *theos* (G2316, "God"). The verse offers "of man" and "of God" as alternatives, not as co-causes of the one birth. **[L2]** *Gennaō* (G1080) is glossed on the sheet: "figuratively, to regenerate." The believers' birth is a regeneration, and the verse itself says it is "not of blood."
**[L3]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." The believing in this verse marks the birth as spiritual.
**[L4]** John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1 mark their "of God" as figurative by the believing and by the contrast with blood. Matthew 1:20 marks its "of the Holy Ghost" as literal by its object: "that which is conceived in her," which is in the womb. Matthew 1:18 confirms it with "found with child." The same preposition does not carry the same sense when the objects differ. I answer the Romans 1:3 press in section A: the "flesh" is met through the woman.

## E. Pressed premise 2: Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, 1 Chronicles 28:6

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
**[L2]** *Andra* (G435, "man, husband") is the word for the husband in Matthew 1:16. She is already espoused (Luke 1:27) and expects to be married.
**[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son."
**[L4]** If the angel's promise meant a conception to come through marriage, her question would have an obvious answer. The angel's reply in Luke 1:35 names the Holy Ghost coming upon her and not a husband. Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34 show the verbs *epercomai* (G1904, "come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "overshadow") can describe presence and power. Here they stand as the answer to "How shall this be?" and the cause for the "therefore." That cause is stated. The challenger's alternative has no verse in Luke 1:35.

## F. Pressed premise 3: Matthew 1:19, 1:24, Deuteronomy 20:7

The challenger is right that *boulomai* (G1014, "be minded") is a word of intent, and that Matthew 1:19 has no verb of knowing. I rest D3 instead on section C, which is the chain of Matthew 1:18, 1:20, 1:24 and 1:25. **[L3]** Deuteronomy 20:7 distinguishes "betrothed" from "taken." That distinction is exactly what Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 use to close the timeline.

## G. Pressed premise 4: Matthew 11:11, Genesis 16:10

I concede that "made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4), "born of women" (Matthew 11:11), and "her seed" (Genesis 3:15 beside Genesis 16:10) do not by themselves exclude a father. **[L4]** That sub-claim floats alone. It stands only together with Matthew 1:18-20 and Luke 1:34-35, which name the source. Matthew 11:11 and Luke 1:13 say "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son," with the father addressed. Luke 1:31 says "thou shalt conceive in thy womb," with no father in the promise.

**On Isaiah 7:14.** **[L1]** Isaiah 7:11: "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above." **[L2]** *Oth* (H226, "sign") is a wonder. **[L3]** Isaiah 7:13: "Hear ye now, O house of David." Isaiah 8:3 names the prophetess's son "Mahershalalhashbaz," not Immanuel. **[L4]** The sign of 7:14 is not the birth of 8:3, which has a different name. Matthew 1:22-23 applies the passage to the birth of Jesus with *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin").

## H. Pressed premise 5: the "father whom Mary names"

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
**[L1]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

### 1. What held at L1–L2–L3?

A point is listed here only where no charge in either side's lists contests the textual, lexical, or cross-reference record:

*   **The marriage status at the espousal:** Both sides cite that Joseph and Mary were husband and wife in law from the espousal: Matthew 1:19 names *"Joseph her husband"*, Matthew 1:20 names *"Mary thy wife"*, and Deuteronomy 22:24 terms a betrothed woman *"his neighbour's wife"*.
*   **The grammar of Matthew 1:16:** Both sides recognize that *egennēsen* (ἐγέννησεν, G1080) governs the preceding genealogy up to Joseph, and that Matthew 1:16 uses the passive verb *egennēthē* (ἐγεννήθη) with the feminine singular pronoun *hēs* (ἧς, *"of whom"*), denoting Mary.
*   **The lineage of Joseph:** Both sides acknowledge that Luke 2:4 states of Joseph that *"he was of the house and lineage of David"*, and Matthew 1:20 addresses him as *"Joseph, thou son of David"*.
*   **The absence of an explicit tribal row for Mary:** Both sides accept that scripture does not record Mary’s father or assign her house by name; her stated kinswoman is Elisabeth, who is *"of the daughters of Aaron"* (Luke 1:5, 36).
*   **The vocabulary of the overshadowing:** Both sides record that Luke 1:35 uses *eperchomai* (ἐπέρχομαι, G1904) and *episkiazō* (ἐπισκιάζω, G1982), the latter appearing also in Luke 9:34 (*"there came a cloud, and overshadowed them"*) and Acts 5:15.
*   **The bounded span of *heōs* in Matthew 1:25:** Both sides agree that *heōs* (ἕως, G2193) in Matthew 1:25 (*"And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"*) marks a period that runs up to the birth.
*   **The signet rows:** Both sides record that the signet plucked in Jeremiah 22:24 (*"though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence"*) is set upon Zerubbabel in Haggai 2:23 (*"will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee"*).

### 5. Most Vulnerable Points in the Debate

*   **Vulnerability in the Defender's Chain:**
    *   *Flesh descent through Mary without a tribal row:* Defender’s link D6 relies on Romans 1:3 (*"Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh"*), arguing that this flesh descent was provided through Mary. However, defender formally conceded: *"I concede that no row states Mary's house"* and *"No row names Mary's father."* Scriptural attribution of Davidic lineage in the nativity accounts is given to Joseph: Luke 1:27 (*"a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David"*), Luke 2:4 (*"Joseph also went up... because he was of the house and lineage of David"*), and Matthew 1:20 (*"Joseph, thou son of David"*).
    *   *The biological reading of 'of the Holy Ghost':* Defender rests D1 on Matthew 1:20 (*"for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"*). Challenger pressed this with passages where *gennaō ek* God is predicated of individuals who have human biological fathers: John 1:13 (*"Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God"*) and 1 John 5:1 (*"Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God"*). Defender is forced to argue an inferential distinction between spiritual regeneration and physical conception without a distinct lexical marker in the verb itself.
*   **Vulnerability in the Challenger's Chain:**
    *   *The absence of an explicit verse narrating Joseph's act of knowing:* Challenger’s link C2 (and C6) concludes: *"So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins."* To construct this, challenger relies on Genesis 4:1 (*"And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived"*), the legal marriage status in Matthew 1:19–20, and the bounding preposition *heōs* in Matthew 1:25 (*"And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"*). The text of Matthew 1:18, however, reads: *"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost"*. Challenger interprets *"came together"* (*synerchomai*, G4905) as the public taking into the home under Matthew 1:24 (*"took unto him his wife"*), but no explicit L1 verse narrates an act of marital union between Joseph and Mary prior to that finding.
    *   *The passive construction in Matthew 1:16:* While challenger notes that passive verbs do not exclude a human father, Matthew 1:16 breaks the continuous active formula (*"Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob..."*) used throughout Matthew 1:2–16, switching to *"Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."* Challenger must treat this switch as non-narration of the begetting rather than an intentional exclusion of Joseph from the begetting verb.

**ANSWER: Jeremiah 22:24, Jeremiah 22:30, Haggai 2:23, Matthew 1:12, Jeremiah 18:8 -- D6 --** (C3, narrowed). Haggai 2:23: "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet." Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."

It does not state that Joseph begat the child, so it does not meet D6.

**Close.** Every link stands on the verses of Matthew 1:18-25 and Luke 1:34-35, where the conception is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost" and the cause of the birth is the Holy Ghost's coming. Every witness the challenger pressed gives either a household title (Luke 2:48; John 6:42), a covenant title (1 Chronicles 28:6; Acts 13:33), or a line that ends at Joseph (Matthew 1:12, 1:16). None of them states a human begetting, and I have granted what they say.

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 4, CLOSE ROUND

# ROUND 4: CHALLENGER'S CLOSE

The question is whether Christ had a biological father. The record's reading, from the case already made: **yes.** The promised seed comes out of a man's loins. The one man the text names beside the mother is Joseph, of the house of David, her husband from the espousal. The rows about the Holy Ghost name God's covenant claim and his empowering presence. They do not name a begetter. My links stand under their own numbers, as follows.

---

**C1: SUPPORTED.** The promise requires seed out of the body of David's line, according to the flesh.
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." The seed comes out of the body.
- [L2] *sperma* (G4690), "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring," stands in Romans 1:3. *osphys* (G3751), "loins," stands in Acts 2:30 and Hebrews 7:10.
- [L3] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." Psalms 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne" (margin "Heb. belly"). Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L4] Footed on the [L1] row, the [L2] words and the [L3] rows: the oath is a flesh seed out of loins, and Hebrews 7:14 calls it "evident." Hebrews 7:10, "he was yet in the loins of his father," shows that loins carry seed down a chain of fathers. That carrying is the chain C1 points to, and it runs through a father's loins at every step.

**C2: SUPPORTED.** The father is named, in the mother's mouth, the narrator's, the town's, a disciple's and the angel's.
- [L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Mary, who received the angel's word, names Joseph "thy father."
- [L2] *huios* (G5207), "son," stands in John 6:42 and John 1:45. *Iōsēph* (G2501) stands in Luke 2:33.
- [L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." Luke 2:27: "the parents brought in the child Jesus." Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year." Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- [L4] Footed on [L1], [L2] and [L3]: the father named in every register is Joseph. Luke 2:49, "I must be about my Father's business," does not take the word "father" from Joseph. It sets the covenant Father beside him, the same pairing 1 Chronicles 28:6 shows: "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him [to be] my son." In that verse the son David begat and the son God claims are one man.

**C3: NARROWED TO:** The signet plucked from Coniah (Jeremiah 22:24) is set again on Coniah's grandson (Haggai 2:23), and Coniah's seed runs on in the line Matthew writes down to Joseph (Matthew 1:12).
- [L1] Jeremiah 22:24: "though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence."
- [L2] *chotham* (H2368), "signet," stands in Haggai 2:23.
- [L3] Haggai 2:23: "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel... and will make thee as a signet." 1 Chronicles 3:17: "the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." Jeremiah 18:8: "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them."
- [L4] Footed on these rows: the sentence on Coniah is answered by the LORD's own signet word to his grandson. Jeremiah 22:30 therefore lays no bar against the line that runs by "begat" to Joseph.

**C4: SUPPORTED.** Israel reckons a man by his father's house.
- [L1] Numbers 1:2: "by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names, every male by their polls."
- [L2] *bayith* (H1004), "a house... family," stands in Numbers 1:2.
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed" (margin "or, pedigree"). Ezra 2:61-62 records those "called after their name," the wife's house: "as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- [L4] Footed on [L1], [L2] and [L3]: the register runs by the father's house, and a line carried by the wife's house was struck. Joseph is "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). Mary's kinswoman is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5, 36). The Davidic house the rows give is Joseph's.

**C5: SUPPORTED.** "Of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" are words of covenant origin and empowering presence. They are not words of begetting.
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904), "come upon," and *episkiazō* (G1982), "overshadow," both stand in Luke 1:35.
- [L3] Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." Acts 5:15: "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them." 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."
- [L4] Footed on [L1], [L2] and [L3]: these two verbs are used of the apostles, of a cloud and of a shadow. The "of God" family is used of believers. The title comes with the throne before Mary's question: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32). The title is crowned at the raising: "he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee" (Acts 13:33).

**C6: SUPPORTED.** A man was involved: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.
- [L1] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." This is the canon's stated means of begetting.
- [L2] *yada'* (H3045), "to know," stands in Genesis 4:1. *heōs* (G2193), "until," stands in Matthew 1:25.
- [L3] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20: "Mary thy wife." Deuteronomy 22:24 calls the betrothed "his neighbour's wife." Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L4] Footed on [L1], [L2], [L3] and the C1 chain: the seed must come out of a man's loins, knowing is the stated means, and Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal. So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and "till" bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy.

The timing rows stand as written and are read inside this chain:
- "before they came together, she was found with child" (Matthew 1:18) dates the finding before the taking, "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24).
- The law names the same step: "betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her" (Deuteronomy 20:7).
- "seeing I know not a man" (Luke 1:34) uses the present indicative *ginōskō*. It is her state when the angel spoke.

"Of whom was born Jesus" (Matthew 1:16) names the mother and does not narrate the begetting. "Made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) is the phrase of birth itself. Matthew 11:11 uses it of John, whose father is named: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13). The father acts as fathers act. He names the child: "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:21), done at Matthew 1:25, as Zacharias wrote "His name is John" (Luke 1:63).

---

**Close.** Precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10), the rows interlock:
- the seed is out of David's loins according to the flesh (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30);
- the father is named Joseph in every register (Luke 2:48; John 6:42);
- reckoning runs by the father's house (Numbers 1:2);
- the Holy Ghost comes upon and overshadows, as he does the apostles and the cloud (Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34);
- the title is the covenant son's (1 Chronicles 28:6).

Christ had a biological father, Joseph, his named Davidic father, and the oath to David stands kept in the flesh.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Terms.** A "biological father" is a human male whose seed contributed to conception. I hold that Christ had none. Mary conceived by the Holy Ghost. Joseph was her husband and the child's reputed, legal father. [L4, resting on the verses below]

## 1. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at the end

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren."
[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] Every link from verse 2 to verse 16 uses *gennaō* (G1080, "to beget," of the father). At the last step the text does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." It calls Joseph *anēr* (G435, "husband, man") of Mary. It then says *ex hēs* (ἐξ ἧς, "out of whom"). The relative pronoun is feminine singular, so it refers to Mary alone. The verb *egennēthē* (ἐγεννήθη, "was born") is passive.

[L3] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." This again names Joseph by his relation to Mary.

[L4] The text keeps "begat" for every male link and drops it at the one place where Joseph and Jesus meet. It then assigns the birth to the woman by a feminine pronoun. Together the lexical shift and the cross-reference show that Matthew withholds a father-son begetting between Joseph and Jesus.

## 2. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] *To gennēthen* (τὸ γεννηθέν, "that which is begotten or conceived") is followed by *ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου, "out of Holy Spirit"). The preposition *ek* names the origin. The only origin given is the Spirit.
[L3] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The word *andra* (ἄνδρα, "a male person") shows Mary excludes any male as the means. The angel does not correct her premise.
[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] *Dio kai* (διὸ καί, "for which reason also") ties the title to the conception. *Episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow") describes divine power, not a husband's union.
[L4] Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy "before they came together." Luke 1:34 says Mary knows no man. Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 name the Spirit as the source. These four verses leave no place for a male contribution.

## 3. Joseph's fatherhood is only reputed

[L1] Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
[L2] *Enomizeto* (ἐνομίζετο, "was reckoned, was supposed by custom or opinion") marks an opinion held by people, not a fact.
[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know"), as in Luke 1:34, is used of marital relations. Matthew 1:25 says Joseph had no such knowledge of Mary up to the birth.
[L3] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49 answers: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The speaker is Mary, in household language. The child's reply points to a different Father.
[L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" These are the words of a crowd. They are the opinion that Luke 3:23 labels "supposed."
[L4] Luke's "as was supposed" and Matthew's "knew her not till" give two footings. Statements that call Joseph the father are reports of what people thought or of household speech, and they do not describe the conception.

## 4. The royal line does not run through Joseph's seed

[L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
[L1] Matthew 1:11: "Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel."
[L2] In Jeremiah 22:30 the Hebrew *zera'* (H2233, "seed, offspring") names the descendants of the man being cursed. Joseph, in Matthew's chain, is of that seed.
[L1] Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
[L3] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The word *sarx* (G4561, "flesh") names the bodily descent.
[L4] The seed of Jechonias is barred from the throne (Jeremiah 22:30), and Joseph is in that seed (Matthew 1:11-12). Yet the throne is promised to Jesus (Luke 1:32), and he is of David "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). So Jesus' flesh is not drawn from Joseph's seed. It comes through the woman, and Joseph supplies legal standing as "son of David" (Matthew 1:20).

## 5. The pattern of Scripture is "her seed" and "a body prepared"

[L1] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head."
[L2] *Zera'* (H2233, "seed") is ordinarily traced through the man. Here it is "her seed."
[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son."
[L2] *'Almah* (H5959, "a young woman of marriageable age, unmarried"). It is the word used of Rebekah before her marriage. [L3] Genesis 24:16 describes her as "a virgin, neither had any man known her," and Genesis 24:43 calls the same woman *'almah*.
[L1] Matthew 1:23 quotes the prophecy with *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin"). [L3] Luke 1:27 uses it of Mary: "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
[L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
[L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
[L4] Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 name only the woman. Isaiah 7:14, read with Genesis 24:16 and Matthew 1:23, names a virgin. Hebrews 10:5 says the body was prepared. These agree with Section 2 that no human male's seed formed the child.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Matthew 1:16 breaks the "begat" (*gennaō*, "beget") pattern of Matthew 1:2-15, calls Joseph "husband" (*anēr*, "husband, man"), and assigns the birth to Mary by the feminine *ex hēs* ("out of whom"); footing: Matthew 1:2, 1:16 [L1], *gennaō* / *ex hēs* [L2], Matthew 1:20 [L3].
2. The only stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, and Mary knew no man; footing: Matthew 1:18, 1:20 [L1], *ek pneumatos hagiou* ("out of Holy Spirit") and *andra* ("a male person") [L2], Luke 1:34-35 [L3].
3. Joseph's fatherhood is reputed, not biological; footing: Luke 3:23 [L1], *enomizeto* ("was supposed") [L2], Matthew 1:25 and Luke 2:48-49 [L3].
4. Jesus' Davidic flesh does not come from Joseph's seed, which lies under Jeremiah 22:30; footing: Jeremiah 22:30 and Matthew 1:11-12 [L1], *zera'* ("seed") [L2], Luke 1:32 and Romans 1:3 [L3].
5. Scripture's pattern is "her seed," a virgin conceiving, a woman-born son and a prepared body; footing: Isaiah 7:14 and Galatians 4:4 [L1], *'almah* ("young woman") and *parthenos* ("virgin") [L2], Genesis 3:15, Genesis 24:16 and Hebrews 10:5 [L3].
6. Therefore Christ had no biological father; Joseph was his husband-of-Mary guardian and legal father only, and the conception was by the Holy Ghost; footing: Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 [L1], *ek* ("out of") and *dio kai* ("for which reason also") [L2], Luke 1:34 and Galatians 4:4 [L3].

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# Challenge: Joseph, the named father of the seed of David

**Terms.** I accept the defender's definition: a biological father is the man whose seed contributed to the conception. I hold that Christ had one, Joseph. The chain the defender declared has to make the Davidic seed "according to the flesh" pass around the only man the text names in that line, and the rows do not let it.

## MY DECLARED CHAIN

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's body.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- [L2] *osphys* (G3751, "loins"). It is the same word as Hebrews 7:10, "he was yet in the loins of his father." In Hebrews 7:10 the loins are the father's.
- [L3] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne" (margin: "Heb. belly").
- [L4] David's flesh is promised out of his bowels and loins (2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30). The loins-word belongs to a father in Hebrews 7:10. So the seed "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3) runs through male loins, father to son, down to the child.

**C2. Descent is counted by the father's house, and it is "evident" by that count.**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L3] The opposite case: Ezra 2:61-62. The priests who "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name" were "as polluted, put from the priesthood." Being reckoned through the wife's house cost them their standing.
- [L4] A tribe is "evident" by the house of the fathers (Numbers 1:18). Being called after the wife's house was struck from the register (Ezra 2:62). So "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" rests on a father's house.

**C3. The one man the text names in that house is Joseph, and the text names him father.**
- [L1] Luke 2:4: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David."
- [L1] Luke 2:48: Mary says, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L3] The narrator speaks the same way: "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27) and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41). A disciple says, "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
- [L2] *goneis* ("parents," Luke 2:27, 41) is Luke's own narration. It is not a crowd's opinion.
- [L4] Luke speaks of Joseph as father in four voices: the narrator, the mother, a disciple and the town. The only house of David he gives is Joseph's (Luke 2:4).

**C4 (keystone). Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L1] Matthew 1:19-20: "Joseph her husband" and "Mary thy wife."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24 calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife." Matthew 1:25 says "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L4] The canon's stated means of begetting is a husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1). Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal (Matthew 1:19-20; Deuteronomy 22:24). The seed must come out of a man's loins (C1). "Till" (Matthew 1:25) limits the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking. So, as an inference on those rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

## PRESSES AGAINST THE DEFENDER'S LINKS

## 6. The remaining links

- **C1** stands on 2 Samuel 7:12, Acts 2:30 and Hebrews 7:9-10.

# SYNTHESIS

Scope note: chain-scoped debate (Isaiah 28:10). Both sides declared numbered chains and both ran a link round and a close round. Below, quotations are words of the transcript above or of the KJV with book, chapter and verse.

---

## 1. HELD AT L1-L2-L3 — points no charge on either list contests

1. **Romans 1:3 — "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."** Both sides affirm the row. The challenger's C1 rests on it; the defender's close round narrows D4 to it: "Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 state that Jesus is David's seed according to the flesh." Neither list charges the affirmation itself.
2. **[L2] The angel's two verbs do not denote begetting.** The challenger asserted it in [CR1] and pressed it with Acts 1:8 ("after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you") and Luke 9:34 ("there came a cloud, and overshadowed them"); the defender states the same in [DR2] and does not rest D2 on them. No list contests the lexical point.
3. **[L1-L2] Luke 1:34's "seeing I know not a man" is present indicative of Mary's state at the hour of the angel's word.** Both sides say so ([DR3]: "present indicative, as the challenger says"). The dispute is what follows from it, which is charged and stands in section 2.
4. **[L2] *gennaō* with *ek theou* is used of persons who have human fathers (John 1:13; 1 John 5:1, "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God").** The defender does not deny the usage; he distinguishes its scope (regenerate adults versus a womb-event at Matthew 1:20). The transference is charged and stands under D2.
5. **[L1-L2] The grammar of Matthew 1:16 as both sides describe it:** active "begat" with the father as subject through the chain, then "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ" — passive verb, feminine relative. The challenger's own description: "the passive *egennēthē* ("was born") states the birth and does not narrate the begetting." The inference drawn from the change of verb and relative is charged by both lists and stands under D1.

---

## 2. CONCESSIONS AND LINK RESULTS — both link rounds and both close rounds

### A. Defender's declared chain (D1–D6)

- **D1 — CITED-WITH-FOOTING.** Link round: "LINK 1: SUPPORTED." Close round: "D1: KEPT." The challenger pressed it with Matthew 1:3 ("Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar"), 1:5, 1 John 5:1, and the naming rows (Matthew 1:21, 1:25; Luke 1:62); the defender answered each with the row and with Exodus 2:10 ("he became her son"). Nothing withdrawn; the pressed point stands unresolved.
- **D2 — CITED-WITH-FOOTING, with one limb dropped and the link kept (narrowing).** The verb-limb was withdrawn in the defender's own words: "The verbs are not what carries my claim." Link round: "LINK 2: SUPPORTED." Close round: "D2: KEPT." Within D2 the defender also granted the challenger's reading of the timing clause: "The challenger's reading of "came together" as the taking into the house is granted (Matthew 1:24)."
- **D3 — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE in the link round, restored to KEPT in the close round.** [DR3]: "LINK 3: NARROWED TO: the father-rows are the voice of the household and the people." A limb was dropped in that same round: "I drop the claim that Luke 2:4 says anything of the flesh." Close round: "D3: KEPT."
- **D4 — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE, twice.** [DR3]: "LINK 4: NARROWED TO: Jesus' flesh is not from Joseph's seed, and the Davidic seed in his flesh comes through Mary." [DR4]: "D4: NARROWED TO: Matthew's line through Jechonias lies under Jeremiah 22:30, and no verse names Joseph as the begetter of the seed of David in Jesus," and, in the answer on Romans 1:3, "I narrow D4 to this: Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 state that Jesus is David's seed according to the flesh. They do not say it came by Joseph's begetting." The close-round form of the link does not carry the "comes through Mary" limb that the link-round form stated.
- **D5 — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE, three times.** [DR2]: "These two rows are cumulative support. They are not independent proof, and I rest nothing alone on them." [DR3]: "I rest nothing on "her seed", "made of a woman" or "a body hast thou prepared" as separate proof." [DR4]: "D5: NARROWED TO: Isaiah 7:14 as Matthew 1:23 applies it," with "I concede that Genesis 3:15 ("her seed"), Genesis 24:16 and Hebrews 10:5 ("a body hast thou prepared me") do not prove the point alone."
- **D6 — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE, link kept.** "I concede the challenger's point. "Of a woman" is said of every man, and of John, whose father is named. Galatians 4:4 carries no weight for D6 alone, and I drop it." Close round: "D6: KEPT on Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 and *dio kai*. Galatians 4:4 is dropped as proof."
- **Defender's other stated grants in the close round:** "I grant the narrowed C4: divine work in a womb can stand beside a named father. My claim does not rest on that point"; "I grant C6: the phrase rests on Joseph"; "I grant that "fruit of his loins" is David's."

### B. Challenger's declared chain (numbered as its close round numbers it)

- **C1 (the seed out of a man's body) — CITED-WITH-FOOTING.** Footing: 2 Samuel 7:12 ("I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels"), Acts 2:30 ("of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh"), Hebrews 7:10 ("he was yet in the loins of his father"). Close round: "C1: KEPT. The promised seed comes out of a man's body, and the one man the text names beside Mary is Joseph."
- **C2 (husband and wife; the timing rows read inside the union) — CITED-WITH-FOOTING, and the one link its own hand files at [L4]:** "So I hold, at [L4] on those rows, that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal." Close round: "C2: KEPT. Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal, and the timing rows are read inside that union."
- **C3 (the sign) — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** The broader [CR2] form, "The sign the angel gives Mary for "how shall this be" is a conception by a named husband, made possible by God," was narrowed in both later rounds to: "NARROWED TO: The sign the angel gives for "how shall this be" is Elisabeth's conception, a wife bearing a son to her husband, made possible by God. Luke joins Mary's conception to it with "also.""
- **C4 (divine work in a womb beside a named father) — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** "I drop "the same act as Luke 1:35."" and "NARROWED TO: In these rows, divine work in a womb is written beside a named father. So the Holy Ghost named at Matthew 1:20 does not by itself displace a father."
- **C5 (the loins are a man's) — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** "I drop the universal form and keep the positive rows."
- **C6 (the house of David rests on Joseph) — CITED-WITH-FOOTING and conceded by the opposing side.** Pressed with Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4, Numbers 1:18 and Ezra 2:61-62; the defender's close round answers: "I grant C6: the phrase rests on Joseph," limited there to "Joseph's legal and house standing."
- **Challenger's own withdrawal on the genealogy:** "'Heli was a father-in-law' is a construct no row states. Its only offered warrant is the Ezra 2:61 practice that Ezra 2:62 struck." This is the challenger refusing a construct, not conceding one.
- **Challenger's method declaration:** "The chain is the proof. The method is Isaiah 28:10, "precept upon precept; line upon line.""

### C. Charged points, both answers on the record, unresolved

1. **Matthew 1:16.** Challenger: *ek* + the woman stands beside an active "begat" at 1:3, 1:5 (twice) and 1:6, so *ex hēs* marks the mother. Defender: the active verb is the father's throughout, and at the one link where Joseph and Jesus meet it is passive with a feminine relative.
2. **Matthew 1:19 "was minded to put her away privily."** Challenger: "Matthew gives *dikaios* ("just") and *mē thelōn… paradeigmatisai* ("not willing to make a public example")… Matthew names no suspicion and no other man." Defender's [DR2] read the intent as a wrong done by another man; the close-round answers on Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 state Matthew's written grounds and the abstinence rather than restating that motive.
3. **Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."** Challenger: *heōs* bounds the abstinence after the taking in Matthew's order (1:18 finding, 1:24 taking, 1:25 not-knowing), and "It does not reach back across the espousal before the finding." Defender: "The text closes the account on abstinence, not on a husband's begetting," and the union is a supplied step.
4. **Luke 1:34-35.** Challenger: the present tense dates her state; the answer names the Spirit and the power, and those verbs are not begetting. Defender: the question is "how," the reply supplies the Holy Ghost and the power, and *dio kai* grounds the title in that coming.
5. **Luke 1:36-37 ("she hath also conceived a son in her old age"; "For with God nothing shall be impossible").** Challenger: the sign is a wife's conception by her named husband, and "also" joins the two. Defender: "The text does not make Mary's like Elisabeth's in every detail," and points at the wording difference between Luke 1:13 ("thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son") and Matthew 1:21 ("she shall bring forth a son").
6. **Hebrews 7:14 "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."** Challenger: *anatellō* as a shoot out of stock (Isaiah 11:1), with Numbers 1:18's reckoning "by the house of their fathers," Exodus 2:10 read against Exodus 2:1 (Moses kept of Levi), and Ezra 2:62's exclusion. Defender: the verse does not use *gennaō*; a tribe is entered by taking and naming (Genesis 48:5, "which were born unto thee"; Exodus 2:10), and Ezra 2:62 is a missing register.
7. **Jeremiah 22:30 ("no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David") with Haggai 2:23 ("will make thee as a signet") and Jeremiah 18:8.** Challenger: the plucked signet is set again on Coniah's grandson, and Jeremiah's own rule shows pronounced sentences turned. Defender: Haggai 2:23 "says nothing of him sitting on the throne of David," chapter 22 states no condition, and a throne claim resting on Joseph's seed sits under the curse.
8. **Luke 3:23 "which was the son of Heli" and the two named fathers of Joseph.** Defender's [DR3] construct (one begetter, one father-in-law, on the Ezra 2:61 practice) against the challenger's charge that the practice was struck at Ezra 2:62; the close round's narrowed D4 no longer rests on the construct.
9. **Luke 1:27 and Mary's house.** Challenger: the house phrase follows the man's name, Luke 2:4 repeats it of Joseph, and the only kin named for Mary is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5, 1:36). Defender: the clause also governs the virgin, Exodus 6:23 shows Levi-Judah kinship by marriage — and then grants C6.
10. **Luke 3:23 "as was supposed."** Challenger: *nomizō* carries no verdict of its own (Acts 16:13 true custom; Acts 21:29 false supposition). Defender: the *hōs* parenthesis is Luke's own hedge at the one link, and Luke writes "Joseph and his mother" (Luke 2:33, 2:43).
11. **Matthew 1:20's margin "Gr. begotten."** Both hands lean on the same margin in opposite directions: challenger (1 John 5:1's *gennaō* + *ek* of believers with fathers); defender (the father-verb with the Holy Ghost as its stated source).

---

## 3. DRIFT GUARD VIOLATIONS — CHALLENGER SEAT ONLY

Tested the challenger's assertions **and** its grants and concessions in every round and in the link round. **No violation found on any guard the transcript reaches.** The tests, with the seat's own words:

- **DG-8 (a) — no "no human father / without Joseph" and no flesh routed through Mary alone.** No such statement appears. When the Mary-line was offered against it, the seat answered from rows: "The one kin Luke names for Mary is Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth," who is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5)." The seat never conceded a Mary-only flesh route.

- Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar". Here "of Thamar" follows an active "begat" with a father as subject. Matthew 1:5: "Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth". The same pattern holds there. In both, the father's verb is written. In 1:16 it is withheld, so the witnesses show the very pattern that 1:16 departs from.
- Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". [L2] *gennaō* is "begotten" here, with *ek* ("out of") the Holy Ghost. It stands in the womb of Mary, with no male named.

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

**LINK ROUND: CHALLENGER**

---

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

*Premise: "Matthew names no suspicion and no other man."*

Footing:
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] *thelō* (G2309, "to determine ... choose or prefer") stands negated in this verse: "not willing." The main verb is "was minded" (*boulomai*, G1014, to will or intend). Matthew writes an intent, "to put her away privily," and two grounds: "being a just [man]" and "not willing to make her a publick example."
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The angel answers a fear about *taking* her. He names her "thy wife" (*gynē*, G1135, "a wife").
- [L4] From these three: the verse gives Joseph's intent and two grounds of character. It gives no verb of knowing or suspecting and names no second man. The angel's answer speaks to the taking, "fear not to take unto thee." I read the row at its own words and supply no ground it does not give.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:
- **Matthew 1:18**, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
  - [L2] *heuriskō* (G2147, to find) dates a finding. What is found carries its origin in the same clause: "with child of the Holy Ghost." The finding itself names no other man.
  - [L3] Matthew sets "came together" by what follows: Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife." The law names the same step in Deuteronomy 20:7: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
  - So "before they came together" dates the finding before the taking into his house. It does not supply a suspicion Matthew never writes.
- **Matthew 1:25**, "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
  - [L2] *heōs* (G2193, "until") bounds a span. That span stands after Matthew 1:24's taking, in Matthew's own order.
  - It speaks of Joseph's conduct with the wife he took. It adds no ground to Matthew 1:19's intent.
- **Matthew 1:20**, quoted above. The "for" grounds the command to take her, and the angel calls her his wife. This agrees with my premise: the text answers Joseph's fear about taking her, not a charge against her.

---

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

*Premise: "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins."*

Footing, set out as a chain:

1. **The seed is out of a man's body.**
   - [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
   - [L3] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
   - [L3] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
   - [L2] *sarx* (G4561, flesh, "the means of kindred") stands in both Acts 2:30 and Romans 1:3.
2. **The canon's stated means of begetting is knowing.**
   - [L1] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
3. **Joseph is of David's house and Mary's husband from the espousal.**
   - [L1] Luke 2:4: "he was of the house and lineage of David."
   - [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
   - [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband," where *anēr* (G435) means "husband."
   - [L3] The law calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
4. **[L4], footed on rows 1 to 3:** Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.
   - The seed must proceed out of a Davidic man's bowels.
   - Knowing is the stated means.
   - The one Davidic man the text joins to Mary as husband is Joseph.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:
- **Matthew 1:18**, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
  - [L2] *heuriskō* (G2147, to find) dates the finding.
  - [L3] "Came together" is set by Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife," and by Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
  - The finding comes before the taking. It does not come before the espousal, in which she is already "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
  - "Of the Holy Ghost" uses *ek* (out of) with God as origin. 1 John 5:1 uses the same language of men with fathers: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."
  - [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 gives "Solomon thy son" and "my son" in one verse. So God's claim on a son stands beside a begetting father.
- **Matthew 1:25**, "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
  - [L2] *heōs* (G2193, "until") bounds the abstinence to the birth.
  - [L3] In Matthew's order, the finding (1:18) comes before the taking (1:24), and 1:25 follows the taking. The "till" therefore covers the pregnancy after she came into his house.
  - It does not reach back across the espousal before the finding.
- **Luke 1:34**, "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
  - [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, to know) is present indicative here: her state at the hour the angel spoke.
  - [L3] Luke 1:31 puts the conceiving ahead in time: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."
  - A present state answered with a future conception does not close the espousal after that hour.

---

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** The sign the angel gives for "how shall this be" is Elisabeth's conception, a wife bearing a son to her husband, made possible by God. Luke joins Mary's conception to it with "also."

Footing:
- [L1] Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age ... who was called barren."
- [L3] Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."

- [L4] From these: the sign is a barren wife's conception by her husband, made possible by God. Mary is told her conception is "also" of that kind. The power of God works where the woman is barren, and a husband is still named.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:
- **Luke 1:35**, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
  - [L2] The verbs are *eperchomai* (G1904, "to supervene ... come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "to cast a shade upon").
  - [L3] Acts 1:8 uses the first verb of the apostles: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you."
  - [L3] Luke 9:34 uses the second of the cloud: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them."

- **Luke 1:34**, "seeing I know not a man." This is her present state (*ginōskō*, present indicative), answered with the future "thou shalt conceive" (Luke 1:31).

  - [L2] *adynateō* (G101, to be impossible).

- **Luke 1:13**, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
  - The "thee" is the hearer, Zacharias. Luke 1:31 speaks to the hearer Mary: "thou shalt conceive."
  - [L3] The father's act in Luke 1:13 is "thou shalt call his name John." Matthew 1:21 gives the same act to Joseph: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Joseph does it at Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."
  - [L2] *tiktō* (G5088, to bring forth) stands in both Luke 1:13 and Matthew 1:21. The two announcements carry one shape.

---

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** In these rows, divine work in a womb is written beside a named father. So the Holy Ghost named at Matthew 1:20 does not by itself displace a father.

Footing:
- [L1] Luke 1:15: "he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb."
- [L3] Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- [L1] Jeremiah 1:5: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee."
- [L3] Jeremiah 1:1: "The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah."
- [L4] From these two pairs: the Spirit's filling in a womb stands with a father, Zacharias. God's forming in the belly stands with a father, Hilkiah. Divine agency in a womb and a named father are written together. I drop "the same act as Luke 1:35."

Answers to the pressed witnesses:
- **Luke 1:13** and **Matthew 1:21**, "And she shall bring forth a son."
  - [L2] *tiktō* (G5088, to bring forth) is in both verses.
  - Matthew 1:21 is spoken to Joseph and carries the father's naming command: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Luke 1:13 has the same command: "thou shalt call his name John." The rows match in the father's act.
- **Luke 1:15** and **Matthew 1:20**, "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
  - [L2] The margin of Matthew 1:20 reads "Gr. begotten." The verb is *gennaō* (G1080) with *ek*.
  - [L3] 1 John 5:1 uses the same verb and preposition of believers, who have fathers: "is born of God ... him also that is begotten of him."
  - "Of the Holy Ghost" names God as origin. It stands beside a father as Luke 1:15 does.

---

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** The loins named in the seed rows are a man's. Acts 2:30's "fruit of his loins" is David's, in the loins-word Hebrews 7:10 uses of a father.

Footing:
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- [L2] *osphys* (loins) is the noun of Acts 2:30. It stands again in Hebrews 7:10.
- [L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
- [L3] Genesis 35:11: "kings shall come out of thy loins."
- [L3] 2 Samuel 7:12: "which shall proceed out of thy bowels."

Answers to the pressed witnesses:
- **Romans 1:3**, "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh," with **Galatians 4:4**, "made of a woman, made under the law."
  - [L2] *ginomai* (G1096, "to become ... be made") stands twice in Galatians 4:4, and the second use is "made under the law." It is a verb of becoming, not a lineage marker.
  - [L3] "Born of a woman" is said of every man: Job 14:1, "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days." It is said of John, whose father is named: Matthew 11:11, "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." The defender grants it carries no weight.
  - Romans 1:3's seed is "of David," and Acts 2:30 places that seed in David's loins.

  - [L2] *patēr* (G3962) means "father (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)." So David is the remote father.

  - [L2] *gennaō* is glossed "properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother." So "born of thee" names the mother's bearing, as Matthew 1:16 does. It does not take the father from the line.

---

**LINK 6: SUPPORTED**

*Premise: "Luke 1:27 attaches 'of the house of David' to 'a man whose name was Joseph.'"*

Footing:
- [L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary."
- [L2] *anēr* (G435, "a man ... husband") is followed by Joseph's name and then *ex oikou David* (*oikos*, G3624, house). The phrase stands after the man's name, before the clause turns back to "the virgin's name."

- **Luke 1:27**, quoted above.
  - [L2] *parthenos* (virgin) opens the verse. But the house-phrase follows the man's name, and Luke 2:4 confirms its holder.
  - [L3] The one kin Luke names for Mary is Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth," who is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5).
