- **D5:** NARROWED TO: Isaiah 7:14 as Matthew 1:23 applies it. Genesis 3:15, Genesis 24:16 and Hebrews 10:5 support it but are not independent proof.
- **D6:** KEPT on Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 and *dio kai*. Galatians 4:4 is dropped as proof.

## ANSWERS TO THE WITNESSES

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:18 -- D2 -- "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." (answers C1, C2)**

- [L1] The one stated source of the pregnancy sits in the same clause as the finding: "found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *heuriskō* (G2147, to find) dates the finding. The source it gives is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of Holy Spirit). The verse names no man.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20 gives the same source as the angel's ground: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The margin reads "Gr. begotten," and *gennaō* (G1080) is "properly, of the father."
- [L4] Matthew 1:20's verb is the father-verb, and its source is the Holy Ghost. The challenger's chain needs a known husband inside the espousal. No row carries that. Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 give the Holy Ghost, and that is the source I hold.
- The challenger's reading of "came together" as the taking into the house is granted (Matthew 1:24). It does not change this, because the source is given in the same clause as the finding.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:25 -- D2 -- "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." (answers C2)**

- [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, to know) and *heōs* (G2193, until, "of time and place") tie the not-knowing to the birth.
- [L3] Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." Matthew 1:25 follows it.
- [L4] Matthew's closing line on the matter reads: she was found with child of the Holy Ghost, and he knew her not until she bore. The text closes the account on abstinence, not on a husband's begetting. The challenger's "knew Mary within the espousal" is a supplied step. My D2 asks only what Matthew 1:18, 1:20 and 1:25 state together.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:34 -- D2 -- "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" (answers C2, C3)**

- [L2] *ginōskō* is present indicative, as the challenger says. It states her condition at the hour of the question.
- [L3] Luke 1:35 answers the "how" with no man: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- [L4] The question is "how," given that she knows no man. The reply supplies the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, not a husband to be. The answer fits the question as I read it and does not fit the challenger's reading.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:35 -- D6 -- "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." (answers C3, C4)**

- [L2] *dio kai* (for which reason also) makes the conception the stated cause of the title "the Son of God."
- [L3] The challenger offers 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." There the sonship is by choice. In Luke 1:35 the cause is the Holy Ghost coming upon the mother.
- [L4] The challenger grants that *eperchomai* (G1904) and *episkiazō* (G1982) do not themselves mean "beget." The verbs are not what carries my claim. The "therefore" carries it, because the title follows from the coming of the Holy Ghost on Mary. The same verse then names no father alongside the Holy Ghost.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:36 and Luke 1:37 -- D2 -- "And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren." / "For with God nothing shall be impossible." (answers C3)**

- [L2] *adynateō* (G101, to be impossible) in Luke 1:37 answers the "how" by the power of God.
- [L3] Luke 1:13 and Matthew 1:21 differ in their words. Luke 1:13 reads "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son," with *gennaō* (G1080) and "thee." Matthew 1:21 reads "And she shall bring forth a son," with *tiktō* (G5088, "to produce ... as a mother") and no "thee."
- [L4] The sign in Luke 1:36 shows what God can do. The challenger's "also" joins the two conceptions as events God works. The text does not make Mary's like Elisabeth's in every detail. The one difference in wording is that Luke 1:13 names a husband as the one borne to, and Luke 1:31 and Matthew 1:21 do not.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:13 -- D2 -- "But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." (answers C3, C4)**

- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is "properly, of the father." It is spoken to the father, who is named.
- [L3] Matthew 1:21 gives the naming to Joseph: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25 shows him doing it: "he called his name JESUS."
- [L4] The challenger sets the two announcements side by side on the naming. I grant the parallel. A father's naming, like a legal father's, is the guardian's act. Exodus 2:10 shows this: "he became her son. And she called his name Moses." Naming does not prove begetting.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:15 -- D2 -- "For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb." (answers C4)**

- [L2] The verb in Luke 1:15 is "filled" (*pimplēmi*, to fill). The verb in Matthew 1:20 is *gennaō* with *ek*. They are different verbs.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Holy Ghost is the source of what is conceived.
- [L4] Luke 1:15 says the Holy Ghost fills a child already conceived. Matthew 1:20 says the Holy Ghost is the origin of the conception. Both can stand with a father named elsewhere. I grant the narrowed C4: divine work in a womb can stand beside a named father. My claim does not rest on that point. It rests on the verb and preposition of Matthew 1:20 and on the "how" answered in Luke 1:35.

**ANSWER: Jeremiah 1:5 -- D5 -- "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, [and] I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations." (answers C4)**

- [L2] The verbs are forming (*yatsar*, to form) and knowing, not begetting.
- [L3] Jeremiah 1:1: "The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah." The father is named in the opening verse, and Jeremiah 1:5 is spoken of the forming in the belly.
- [L4] I grant that God's forming in the belly stands with a named father in Jeremiah. D5 does not claim that divine agency excludes a father. It claims that Matthew 1:23 sets the sign of Isaiah 7:14 on a virgin who conceives, and Jeremiah 1:5 uses no virgin.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:16 -- D1 -- "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." (answers C1, C2)**

- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) appears twice. In the active it is "begat," with the father as subject. In the passive it is "was born," with the mother as source. *anēr* (G435) is "a man ... husband."
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." The pattern is father begat son. Matthew 1:3 and 1:5 add the mother ("of Thamar," "of Rachab," "of Ruth") but keep the father as the subject of "begat."
- [L4] In the 1:2-15 pattern the father is subject of "begat." In 1:16 the line gives "Jacob begat Joseph." Then Joseph is "the husband of Mary," and the birth of Jesus is "of whom," in the feminine, and is passive. The father is the one who begat in every earlier link and is not named as the begetter in the last. I keep D1.

**ANSWER: Luke 3:23 -- D3 -- "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli," (answers C2, C6)**

- [L2] *enomizeto* (G3543, was supposed) qualifies "the son of Joseph."
- [L3] Luke 2:48 puts "thy father and I" in Mary's mouth. Luke 2:49 gives the child's answer: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 4:22 and John 6:42 are the townsmen's words: "Is not this Joseph's son?" and "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" In Luke 2:33 and Luke 2:43 the narrator himself writes "Joseph and his mother."
- [L4] Everything in the reported speech is what the speakers took to be so. Luke 3:23 is the narrator, and he writes "as was supposed." In his own voice Luke writes "Joseph and his mother" (Luke 2:33, 2:43).

**ANSWER: Luke 1:27 -- D3 -- "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary." (answers C6)**

- [L2] *oikos* (G3624, house) follows Joseph's name in the clause.
- [L3] Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David." Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David."
- [L4] I grant C6: the phrase rests on Joseph. That is Joseph's legal and house standing, which is what D3 asserts. The house phrase does not state who begat Jesus. Genesis 48:5 ("thy two sons ... are mine") and Exodus 2:10 ("he became her son") show a son reckoned to a house without being begotten into it.

**ANSWER: Exodus 6:23 -- D3 -- "And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar." (answers C6)**

- [L2] *lāqach* (H3947, to take) is the taking of a wife.
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L4] I granted the reckoning by the father's house in the previous answer. The row does not alter D3, because D3 holds that Joseph is Jesus' father in the house reckoning. It does not hold that he begat him. Exodus 6:23 says "she bare him," and that is the verse where begetting is stated. Matthew 1:16 names no such begetting of Jesus by Joseph.

**ANSWER: Romans 1:3 -- D4 -- "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" (answers C5)**

- [L2] *sarx* (G4561, flesh, "the means of kindred") and *ginomai* (G1096, to become).
- [L3] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." Hebrews 7:10 says of Levi: "he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Hebrews 7:9 adds "Levi ... payed tithes in Abraham."
- [L4] I grant that "fruit of his loins" is David's. Hebrews 7:10 shows loins-language reaching down through generations. Levi is in Abraham's loins, across the span between them. So the phrase carries David's descendant through his line and does not name Joseph as the begetter. I narrow D4 to this: Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 state that Jesus is David's seed according to the flesh. They do not say it came by Joseph's begetting.

**ANSWER: Jeremiah 22:30 and Matthew 1:11-12 -- D4 -- "Thus saith the LORD, Write ye this man childless, a man [that] shall not prosper in his days: for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah." (answers C5)**

- [L2] *zera'* (H2233, seed) is the word for "his seed."
- [L3] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." Matthew 1:16 puts Joseph at the end of that line. The challenger offers Haggai 2:23 ("will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant ... and will make thee as a signet") and Jeremiah 22:24 ("though Coniah ... were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence").
- [L4] Haggai 2:23 sets Zerubbabel as a signet. It says nothing of him sitting on the throne of David and ruling in Judah, which is what Jeremiah 22:30 withholds. I do not claim the sentence is broken. I claim only that a claim to the throne resting on Joseph's seed alone sits under Jeremiah 22:30. That is the footing of D4 as narrowed, and the unnamed premise in Luke 1:32 is the throne given "unto him."

**ANSWER: Luke 1:32 -- D4 -- "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:" (answers C5)**

- [L2] *patēr* (G3962) is "father (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)."
- [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- [L4] I grant that "father David" can be a remote father. The throne is "given" (*didōmi*, to give) to him by "the Lord God." It is not said to descend by a begetting. That keeps D4 within what the verse states.

**ANSWER: Isaiah 7:14 and Isaiah 8:3 -- D5 -- "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." / "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son." (answers C4)**

- [L2] *'almah* (H5959, young woman) is the word in Isaiah 7:14. The challenger notes its range. *parthenos* (G3933, virgin) is the word Matthew 1:23 uses for it.
- [L3] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." Isaiah 8:3 gives the prophet's going to the prophetess with a named father in the near context.
- [L4] I narrow D5 to the verse the text itself applies. Matthew 1:23 renders Isaiah 7:14 with *parthenos* and sets it beside Matthew 1:20 and 1:18. I concede that Genesis 3:15 ("her seed"), Genesis 24:16 and Hebrews 10:5 ("a body hast thou prepared me") do not prove the point alone. Genesis 16:10 and Genesis 24:60 use "thy seed" of women with husbands. D5 rests on Matthew 1:23.

**ANSWER: Galatians 4:4 -- D6 -- "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law," (answers C5)**

- [L2] *ginomai* (G1096, to become) stands twice in the verse.
- [L3] Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days." Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist."
- [L4] I concede the challenger's point. "Of a woman" is said of every man, and of John, whose father is named. Galatians 4:4 carries no weight for D6 alone, and I drop it. D6 stands on Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 and *dio kai*, together with Luke 1:34.

## CLOSING SUMMARY

- **D1:** Matthew 1:16 breaks the "begat" pattern of Matthew 1:2-15, and the birth is "of whom," in the feminine.
- **D2:** The source stated in Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 is the Holy Ghost. Luke 1:34-35 answers a question that excludes a man with an answer that names none.
- **D3:** Luke 3:23 qualifies the sonship with "as was supposed." The speeches that call Joseph father are what the speakers took to be so.
- **D4 (narrowed):** Nothing in the seed-of-David verses names Joseph as the begetter.
- **D5 (narrowed):** Matthew 1:23 applies Isaiah 7:14 to a virgin.
- **D6:** The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost. Joseph is Mary's husband and, in the house reckoning, Jesus' legal father.

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 4, CLOSE ROUND

# ROUND 4: CHALLENGER CLOSE

My links keep their link-round numbers. I press nothing new. These are my final words on my own position.

## STATUS OF MY LINKS

- **C1:** KEPT. The promised seed comes out of a man's body, and the one man the text names beside Mary is Joseph.
- **C2:** KEPT. Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal, and the timing rows are read inside that union.
- **C3:** NARROWED TO: The sign the angel gives for "how shall this be" is Elisabeth's conception, a wife bearing a son to her husband, made possible by God. Luke joins Mary's conception to it with "also."
- **C4:** NARROWED TO: In these rows, divine work in a womb is written beside a named father. So the Holy Ghost named at Matthew 1:20 does not by itself displace a father.
- **C5:** NARROWED TO: The loins named in the seed rows are a man's. Acts 2:30's "fruit of his loins" is David's, in the loins-word Hebrews 7:10 uses of a father.
- **C6:** KEPT. Luke's "of the house of David" rests on Joseph, and the record reckons sons by the house of their fathers.

## C1: THE SEED IS OUT OF A MAN'S BODY

- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." The seed comes out of David's own body.
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The son is David's seed in the flesh.
- [L2] *sarx* (G4561, flesh, "the means of kindred") in Romans 1:3 makes the descent a matter of kindred in the flesh, not of title. *zera'* (seed) in 2 Samuel 7:12 is what proceeds "out of thy bowels."
- [L3] Psalms 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." Genesis 35:11: "kings shall come out of thy loins." Hebrews 7:14: "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L3] The reckoned son stands apart from the begotten one. Exodus 2:10 says "he became her son," and Genesis 48:5 says "thy two sons ... are mine." Each is a son counted to a house, not seed out of the bowels.
- [L4] The oath names a seed out of David's bowels, fruit of his body, according to the flesh, and "evident." The canon's stated means of begetting is "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1). A seed that proceeds out of a man's body therefore stands on a man.

## C2: HUSBAND AND WIFE, AND THE TIMING ROWS READ INSIDE THE UNION

- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *anēr* (G435, "husband, man") in Matthew 1:19 and *gynē* (G1135, "a wife") in Matthew 1:20 name the pair as husband and wife before the taking. *paralambanō* (G3880, to take unto) in Matthew 1:20 and 1:24 names the taking into the house.
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24 calls the betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife." Deuteronomy 20:7 names the step still to come: "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?"
- The timing rows, held as written:
  - Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." This dates the finding before the taking.
  - Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." This is the taking.
  - Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." *heōs* (G2193, "until") bounds the not-knowing to the pregnancy after the taking.
  - Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" *ginōskō* (G1097) stands in the present tense. It is her state in the hour the angel spoke, not a vow.
- [L4] Footed on Matthew 1:19-20 with *anēr* and *gynē*, on Deuteronomy 22:24, and on Genesis 4:1, I hold this: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.
- "Of the Holy Ghost" is the angel's ground for the command to take her, joined to it by "for." John 1:13 says "born ... of God," and 1 John 5:1 says "is born of God." There the same "of" names an origin in God beside human birth, and it names no begetter in the flesh.

## C3: THE SIGN IS A WIFE BEARING TO HER HUSBAND

- [L1] Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age." Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
- [L3] Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called."
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080, "to procreate, properly, of the father") in Luke 1:13 is spoken to Zacharias.
- [L4] God's power makes possible a conception by a wife to her named husband. Luke then sets Mary's conception beside that one with "also."

## C4: DIVINE WORK IN A WOMB STANDS BESIDE A NAMED FATHER

- [L1] Luke 1:15: "he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb." Jeremiah 1:5: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee."
- [L3] Luke 1:13 names John's father. Jeremiah 1:1 reads "Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah."
- [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904, "come upon") in Luke 1:35 is the verb of Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." *episkiazō* (G1982, "overshadow") in Luke 1:35 is the cloud of Luke 9:34 and the shadow of Acts 5:15.
- [L4] In both rows the Holy Ghost's work and God's forming are written beside a named father. In every row I cited, the angel's verbs are coming-upon and presence, never begetting. The Holy Ghost at Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 therefore does not by itself displace the named father.

## C5: THE LOINS ARE A MAN'S

- [L1] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- [L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Genesis 35:11: "kings shall come out of thy loins."
- [L2] *sarx* (G4561) stands in Acts 2:30: "according to the flesh."
- [L4] In each row the loins-word is used of a father, so the line carries through men. The flesh of David's seed comes down that line of loins.

## C6: THE HOUSE OF DAVID RESTS ON JOSEPH, AND THE REGISTER IS THE FATHER'S

- [L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
- [L3] Numbers 1:2: "by the house of their fathers." Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L3] Ezra 2:61-62 shows the reverse. The priests who "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name" were "as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- [L2] *patēr* (G3962, "father") stands in Mary's own mouth, Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." *goneus* (G1118, "parent") is the narrator's word in Luke 2:27, "the parents brought in the child Jesus," and in Luke 2:41, "his parents went to Jerusalem."
- [L3] Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled." John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." Luke 4:22: "Is not this Joseph's son?"
- Luke 3:23, "(as was supposed) the son of Joseph," uses *enomizeto*, the verb form of "where prayer was wont to be made" (Acts 16:13). The word carries no verdict of its own. It stands with Mary's "thy father."

## THE TITLE AND THE THRONE, AS I HAVE HELD THEM

- [L1] Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title and the throne are given before Mary's question in Luke 1:34.
- [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- [L4] In one verse, 1 Chronicles 28:6, the son David begat bears God's covenant sonship. "Shall be called the Son of God" (Luke 1:35) is that covenant title, and it stands with a father in the flesh.
- On Jeconiah, 1 Chronicles 3:17 records "the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son." Haggai 2:23 sets "Zerubbabel ... the son of Shealtiel" as the signet plucked in Jeremiah 22:24. Jeremiah's own rule stands: "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil" (Jeremiah 18:8).

## FINAL WORDS

The record answers the question yes. Christ had a biological father, and his name is Joseph.

- **The seed.** It is David's "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). It proceeds "out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and is "of the fruit of his loins" (Acts 2:30).
- **The father, named.** Mary says "thy father" (Luke 2:48). The narrator writes "his parents" (Luke 2:41), a disciple says "the son of Joseph" (John 1:45), and the angel says "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).
- **The union.** They were "Joseph her husband" and "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:19-20). The canon's means of begetting is "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1). "Till" bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy (Matthew 1:25). So I hold, at [L4] on those rows, that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.
- **The Holy Ghost and the title.** "Of the Holy Ghost" names the origin in God, as "born of God" does in John 1:13. "Son of God" is the covenant title God gave Solomon while David was his father (1 Chronicles 28:6).

Precept upon precept, line upon line (Isaiah 28:10): the rows interlock, and they name the man.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** [L4] Christ had no human biological father. His conception in Mary was of the Holy Ghost, with no man's seed involved. By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed contributed to the conception. I rest this on the KJV text alone.

## 1. The conception is stated as "of the Holy Ghost," not of a man

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The preposition is *ek* (G1537, "out of," marking source). The source of the pregnancy is named as the Holy Ghost. The time is fixed as "before they came together," and *synerchomai* (G4905) means "to come together."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek *gennaō* (G1080, "to beget, to conceive") is in the passive, "that which is begotten in her." The source is again *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Ghost."
[L4] Matthew 1:18 gives the source as the Holy Ghost and the timing as before any union. Matthew 1:20 repeats the source with the same *ek*. No place is left for a man's seed as a contributing source.

## 2. Mary's question and the angel's answer

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is here used of marital knowledge. Mary states that she has had no man.
[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] *Episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow") is the word for the Highest's power covering her. *Dia touto* ("therefore") makes this act the reason the child is called the Son of God.
[L4] Mary's question asks how conception could occur without a man. The answer names no man. It names the Holy Ghost coming upon her and the power of the Highest overshadowing her. The answer stands on the verse that asks and the verse that replies.

## 3. Joseph's conduct shows he knew he was not the father

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L2] *Apolyō* (G630, "to release, put away") is the word for his intended action.
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

# Debate synthesis

**Classification rule:** “Cited-with-footing” reports that a side exhibited a chain in its link round. It is not a ruling that the chain establishes its conclusion.

## 1. Uncontested text and wording

- **[L1]** Galatians 4:4 says Christ was “made under the law.” Neither charge list contests that phrase.
- **[L2]** Both sides accepted the correction of the Greek wording in Luke 1:35 to *dio kai*, rendered “therefore also.” They disputed its application, recorded below.
- **[L3]** No substantive cross-reference chain is listed as uncontested: the parties’ charge lists contest the bearing of the chains on the question.

## 2. Link rounds, concessions, and close rounds

### Defender’s links

| Link | Link-round filing | Charge and both sides’ answers |
|---|---|---|
| **D6 — Davidic seed and Joseph’s status** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The challenger pressed Acts 2:30 and Romans 1:3 against the proposed legal reckoning. The defender cited Luke 3:23, Matthew 1:20 and Luke 2:4 for Joseph’s house, and Hebrews 7:5, 10 for loins-language across generations. The challenger answered that the chain of fathers reaches the final link; the defender answered that it does not establish that requirement. |
| **D1 — “of the Holy Ghost”** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The challenger pressed John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1 as language of divine origin applied to believers with fathers. The defender cited Matthew 1:18, 20 and Luke 1:34–35, distinguishing the conception in Mary from believers’ birth of God. |
| **D2 — Mary’s question and the answer** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The challenger linked Luke 1:35’s title to Luke 1:32 and 1 Chronicles 28:6. The defender linked the answer to the immediately preceding question and the Holy Ghost’s coming upon Mary. Both discussed the force of *dio kai*. |
| **D3 — Joseph and the time window** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The challenger distinguished betrothal, taking and abstinence, citing Deuteronomy 20:7 and Matthew 1:24–25. The defender cited Matthew 1:18, 20 and 1 Corinthians 7:5 for the timing and sense of “came together.” |
| **D4 — the sign** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The challenger pressed Isaiah 7:16 and 8:3–4 alongside Matthew 1:22–23. The defender distinguished the names in Isaiah 7:14 and 8:3 and cited Matthew’s application of Isaiah 7:14. |
| **D5 — “of whom” and the prepared body** | **NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE** | The defender kept Matthew 1:16 and Hebrews 10:5 but said: “I drop any rest on the ‘born of a woman’ idiom.” The challenger cited Genesis 4:25 and Matthew 11:11 to show that mother-language occurs where a father is named. |

### Challenger’s links

These labels follow the challenger’s **link-round numbering**, rather than the earlier declared-chain numbering.

| Link | Link-round filing | Charge and both sides’ answers |
|---|---|---|
| **C1 — abstinence and taking** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The defender pressed Matthew 1:18, 20 and Luke 1:34–35 against a union before the finding. The challenger cited Matthew 1:24–25 and Deuteronomy 20:7, reading the abstinence as beginning with the taking and “came together” as joining into one house. |
| **C2 — pedigree** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The defender pressed Matthew 1:16’s change from “begat” to “was born” and Ezra 2:62’s missing register. The challenger cited Numbers 1:18, the Hebrew verb *yalad*, and Ezra 2:59–62 for pedigree by the fathers’ house. |
| **C3 — loins and the line of fathers** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The defender cited Hebrews 7:5, 10 for descent across generations without establishing the last link. The challenger cited those same verses with Matthew 1:2 and Acts 2:30 for a succession of fathers. |
| **C4 — Joseph’s proposed action** | **NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE** | The challenger retained: “The exposure (G3856) that Joseph would not bring on her follows from the finding before the taking,” and expressly said: “The limb ‘whoever is the father’ leaves the link.” The defender pressed Joseph’s justice, proposed putting away and the angel’s explanation in Matthew 1:19–20. |
| **C5 — “as was supposed”** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The defender cited Luke 2:44–46 and Acts 14:19–20 for mistaken supposition, alongside Luke 1:34–35. The challenger cited Acts 16:13 for usage and Luke 2:41, 48 for the narrative context. Both said context bears on the word. |
| **C6 — God’s raising and a father’s begetting** | **CITED-WITH-FOOTING** | The defender cited Acts 13:23 and Luke 1:35. The challenger cited 2 Samuel 7:12, 1 Chronicles 28:6 and Acts 13:23 for God’s raising of David’s seed. |

### Express corrections, grants and withdrawals

- The defender corrected the Greek: **“The challenger is right that Luke 1:35 reads ‘therefore also’ and that the Greek is *dio kai*.”**
- The defender withdrew one use of Galatians 4:4: **“I withdraw Galatians 4:4 as an exclusion witness.”**
- The defender granted the comparison: **“‘born of women’ (Matthew 11:11) and ‘born of a woman’ (Job 14:1) are said of men who have fathers.”**
- The defender granted the ordinary means: **“Genesis 4:1 is the ordinary means of conceiving.”**
- The challenger narrowed C4 rather than conceding the entire link, using the words quoted in the table.

### What the close rounds did

The defender’s close restated D1–D6 and answered the challenger’s witnesses on the conception and timing, Mary’s question, the sign, the father-language and Davidic seed. The defender wrote: **“I narrow nothing and concede nothing.”** That statement did not erase the earlier express narrowing of D5 or the withdrawal of Galatians 4:4 as an exclusion witness.

The challenger’s close identified two alleged inconsistencies: the defender’s renewed use of “made of a woman” after withdrawing it as an exclusion witness, and its use to locate the Davidic flesh in the woman. Those are the challenger’s **charges**, not concessions by the defender.

The defender had no round after the challenger’s close. That is procedural and counts against neither side. The system-identified new close references—**1 Corinthians 1:18** in the defender’s close and **Isaiah 28:10** in the challenger’s close—are not counted.

## 3. Challenger: instruction compliance

The challenger maintained the required position that Joseph was the biological father and placed the proposed union within the espousal. Its grants that the conception preceded the taking and that betrothal and taking are distinct did not themselves grant a prohibited conclusion.

One **layer-label issue** appears in the challenger’s link round. Under **[L2]**, it wrote: **“The dio kai (‘therefore’) in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity.”** The parties contested that connection; presenting it as lexical grounding rather than an argued application conflicts with the instruction to distinguish lexical evidence from inference. No further violation is established merely by the challenger’s grants or by its disputed conclusions.

## 4. Engagement and defense

The challenger engaged the defender’s **chain**, not just isolated words: it pressed the seed, pedigree, conception, timing and title links, then answered the defender’s six listed premises. Its C4 filing narrowed a limb while keeping the link.

The defender filed footing for each charged link, narrowed D5, and gave a substantive close. It did not use the placeholder described in the request. Its final statement maintained D1–D6; that is its recorded position, not an independent ruling.

## 5. Most exposed questions in the record

- **D6:** Whether the Davidic seed texts and Joseph’s named house establish the proposed final link, or whether the defender’s reckoning accounts for the seed-language.
- **C1:** Whether Matthew 1:18’s “came together” and 1:25’s “knew her not till” permit the proposed sequence within the espousal.
- **D1/D2 and C6:** How Matthew 1:20’s “of the Holy Ghost” and Luke 1:35’s answer relate to the Davidic-seed chain.

The parties supplied competing chains and answers on each question.

--- ORACLE_DEBATE_V1 CONFIRMATION ---
(A review of the single judge's second opinion, which was HELD. The debate's verdict is the panel's.)
1. **Accurate in substance:** the synthesis records both chains, the narrowing of D5 and C4, and the corrected challenger count; the second opinion is not the panel’s verdict. 2. **Tension:** Matthew 1:18’s “came together” can carry a conjugal sense, but the comparison with 1 Corinthians 7:5 does not by itself establish that sense in Matthew. Matthew 1:25 and the timing of the taking remain central to the collision; the challenger’s proposed prior union is an **[L4] inference**, not a narrated event. Romans 1:3’s Davidic seed and Matthew 1:20’s “of the Holy Ghost” must both be accounted for. The reported contradiction over “born of a woman” also needs distinction: reusing the phrase is not necessarily reasserting it as an exclusion witness. 3. **New:** no new textual finding is established; the corrected count removes C1 from the *unexhibited* count while leaving the second opinion’s adverse fit ruling in place.

X1 LINK 5 | EARLIER [CR3] "I drop any rest on the "born of a woman" idiom, since I have granted that it is said of men with fathers." | CLOSING [CR4] "So the seed of David is "made" of a woman, as Matthew 1:16 "of whom" traces." | The closing rests the Davidic seed on the very idiom the defender dropped as said of men with fathers.

## MY CLOSE: the record's reading, from the case already made

My links stand as my link round numbered them: C1, C2, C3, C5 and C6 SUPPORTED. C4 stands only as narrowed: "The exposure (G3856) that Joseph would not bring on her follows from the finding before the taking (Matthew 1:18-19)." The limb "whoever is the father" stays out.

**1. The seed is out of a man's body (C3).**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- [L2] The word for "bowels" is mê'eh (H4578), which the lexicon glosses "of men, the seat of generation."
- [L3] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." The word for "loins" is osphys (G3751), "procreative power."
- [L3] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The word for "seed" is sperma (G4690), "seed (including the male 'sperm')."
- [L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
- [L4] The promise sets the seat of the seed in David's own generative body, and the canon carries seed down through the loins of a father. The defender granted the seed is David's "according to the flesh" (G17). On these rows, the flesh came by a father's loins.

**2. The pedigree is declared by the father's house.**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
- [L2] "Evident" is pródēlos (G4271), "plain before all men."
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Here bayith (H1004) means house or family, and 'âb (H1) means father.
- [L3] Ezra 2:59: "but they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel." Its margin reads "[seed: or, pedigree]."
- [L3] Ezra 2:62: "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- [L4] Under the law, descent is plain before all men only by the house of the fathers. The father the text names is Joseph: "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)" (Luke 2:4) and "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).

**3. The father is named, and "as was supposed" is a verb of usage (C5).**
- [L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L3] Luke 2:41: "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover."
- [L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"
- [L3] John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
- [L2] At Luke 3:23, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph," the verb is nomizō (G3543), "properly, to do by law (usage)... be wont." It is the verb of Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made," which the defender granted as a true usage (G15).
- [L4] Mary, Luke's narrator, the town and a disciple all name Joseph as the father. Luke's verb at 3:23 states how the law reckoned the son, and it stands with Mary's "thy father."

**4. Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal (C1).**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." The defender granted this is the ordinary means (G5, G8).
- [L3] Matthew 1:19 calls him "Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20 calls her "Mary thy wife." Deuteronomy 22:24 calls the betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife." The defender granted the betrothed is called wife (G9).
- [L3] The "coming together" of Matthew 1:18 is set by what follows. Matthew 1:24 reads "and took unto him his wife," and the law names that same step in Deuteronomy 20:7: "that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" The defender granted that betrothal and taking are two acts (G7).
- [L2] At Luke 1:34, "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?", ginōskō is present tense. The defender granted that it names her state when she asked.
- [L4] The seed rows require a man's loins, and knowing is the stated means of begetting. The husband and wife are joined in law from the espousal. Matthew 1:25, "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son," bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking (G6). So, footed on these rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.
- [L1] Luke 2:5 shows the two together as husband and expectant wife: "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."
- [L1] Joseph does the father's act of naming. Matthew 1:21 reads "and thou shalt call his name JESUS," and this is done at 1:25.
- [L3] It is the same act as Zacharias's: "And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called" (Luke 1:62).

**5. "Of the Holy Ghost" is covenant origin, and "Son of God" is the covenant title (C6).**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] The margin's verb is gennaō (G1080).
- [L3] The same verb is said of believers in 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God [is born: Gr. has been born]." Believers born of God still have fathers in the flesh.
- [L3] John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- [L1] The title comes with the throne before Mary's question. Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." Luke 1:34 comes after it.
- [L2] At Luke 1:35 the "therefore also" is dio kai. It connects back to v.32, not forward to a divine begetting of flesh: "shall be called the Son of God."
- [L3] The verbs of Luke 1:35 are empowerment and presence in their other rows:
  - Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you."
  - Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them."
  - Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."
- [L3] The title is the Davidic covenant title:
  - 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." In one verse the son is David's by begetting and God's by choosing.
  - 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
  - Psalms 2:7: "Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee." The New Testament applies it at three occasions:
    - the resurrection, Acts 13:33: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee";
    - the priesthood, Hebrews 5:5: "So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee";
    - beside the Davidic promise, Hebrews 1:5: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?"
- [L4] The title runs alongside a father in the flesh, as it did with Solomon. "Of the Holy Ghost" marks the seed God claims for his covenant, in a verse that names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife."

**6. "Made of a woman" names the mother, and the flesh is his brethren's.**
- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
- [L3] The same phrase is said of sons with fathers:
  - Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble. [few...: Heb. short of days]"
  - Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named in Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
  - Genesis 4:25: "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel." Seth is her seed, and Adam knew her.
- [L3] Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same."
- [L3] Hebrews 2:16: "For verily he took not on [him the nature of] angels; but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]"
- [L3] Hebrews 2:17: "Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren."
- [L4] The mother is named as Eve was named over Seth, and the flesh came "likewise," as his brethren's came. Matthew 1:16, "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ," names the mother of the birth and is held as written, beside "thy father" at Luke 2:48.

**Final word.** On these rows the record reads the topic this way:
- The seed is David's according to the flesh, out of bowels and loins.
- The pedigree is evident by the house of the fathers.
- The father is named: Joseph, son of David, husband of Mary.
- "Of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" are covenant origin and covenant title, given with the throne.
- Christ had a biological father, Joseph, who knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

Precept upon precept, line upon line (Isaiah 28:10).

rows.claude_r1:
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Thesis.** [L4] The KJV answers no. Jesus was conceived in Mary without any man's seed, by the power of the Holy Ghost. Joseph was his father only by legal standing and in common supposition, not by generation. By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed generated the child. The text excludes that.

## 1. The woman was a virgin when she conceived

**[L1] Luke 1:27:** "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
- **[L2]** The word is παρθένος (parthenos, "a virgin, a maiden who has not had relations with a man").

**[L1] Luke 1:34:** "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L2]** The verb is γινώσκω (ginōskō, "to know"), here in its sexual sense.
- **[L3]** Genesis 4:1 uses the same idiom: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- Mary's question rules out a human explanation. Gabriel's answer does not say "a man shall come." It names another source (see 3 below).

**[L1] Matthew 1:23:** "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."
- This quotes **[L1] Isaiah 7:14:** "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son."
- **[L2]** The Hebrew is עַלְמָה (ʿalmāh, "a young woman of marriageable age, unmarried").
- **[L3]** Genesis 24:43 uses the same word for Rebekah: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water."
- **[L3]** Genesis 24:16 describes her: "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
- So the word is used of a woman the text itself says no man had known.
- [L4] The chain is this. Matthew 1:22 introduces the quotation as fulfilment ("Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled"). The Greek parthenos in Matthew 1:23 fixes the sense. Genesis 24:16,43 shows ʿalmāh applied to a woman declared unknown by any man. Together these show the prophecy was of a conception without a man.

## 2. The source of the conception is stated as the Holy Ghost, not Joseph

**[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** "Of" translates ἐκ (ek, "out of, from the source of"). The source is πνεύματος ἁγίου (pneumatos hagiou, "Holy Spirit").
- The timing is "before they came together."

**[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** The participle is γεννηθέν (gennēthen, "begotten, brought into being"). It is again ἐκ πνεύματος (ek pneumatos, "out of the Spirit").
- The angel gives this as the reason Joseph should not fear to take Mary.

**[L1] Matthew 1:19:** Joseph was "minded to put her away privily."
- [L4] Joseph's own reaction shows he knew the child was not his. That is why the angel's explanation was needed.

**[L1] Matthew 1:25:** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L2]** The verb ἐγίνωσκεν (eginōsken, "was knowing") is in the imperfect, describing continued non-relations. Its limit is the birth ("till she had brought forth").
- Joseph had no union with Mary before the birth.

## 3. The power by which the child came to be

**[L1] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** The verb ἐπισκιάσει (episkiasei, "will overshadow") is not language of marital union. In the Greek Old Testament it is used of the cloud over the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35).
- **[L3]** Exodus 40:35 in the KJV reads: "the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle."
- The word marks divine power at work, not the act of a man.
- "Therefore" (διό, dio, "for which reason") ties the child's title to this origin.

**[L1] Galatians 4:4:** "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
- **[L2]** γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός (genomenon ek gynaikos, "coming to be out of a woman") names only the woman as the human source.
- **[L3]** Genesis 3:15 foretells this: "between thy seed and her seed." The Hebrew zeraʿ (seed) is attributed to the woman, which is unusual because seed is normally reckoned through the man.
- [L4] Two footings support the inference. Galatians 4:4 names only the woman as the human origin. Genesis 3:15 assigns the promised seed to the woman. So the deliverer's human origin is traced through her alone.

## 4. Joseph's fatherhood is legal and supposed, not generative

**[L1] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** Matthew 1:2–15 repeats ἐγέννησεν (egennēsen, "begat") for every link. At verse 16 the pattern changes. The text does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." It says ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη (ex hēs egennēthē, "out of whom was born"), with the relative pronoun ἧς (hēs) in the feminine singular. It refers to Mary alone.
- The same genealogy that gives Joseph's line breaks its formula at the one point where the generative claim would have been made.

**[L1] Luke 3:23:** "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L2]** ὡς ἐνομίζετο (hōs enomizeto, "as was thought, as was supposed") marks a popular belief, not a fact.

**[L1] Mark 6:3:** "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?"
- Here the townspeople name only the mother.

**[L1] Luke 2:48–49:** Mary says "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Jesus answers, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
- [L4] Two footings support the inference. Mary's phrase uses the speech of ordinary supposition, as in Luke 3:23. Jesus's reply redirects "father" to God. So the title "father" for Joseph is real in the household but is not the claim of generation.

## 5. Consistency with the royal line

**[L1] Jeremiah 22:30:** "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:11–12** records "Josias begat Jechonias" and "Jechonias begat Salathiel."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:16** names Joseph as in that royal line.
- **[L1] Luke 1:32** promises: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- [L4] The chain is this. Jeremiah 22:30 forbids Jechonias's seed from the throne. Matthew 1:11–16 puts Joseph in Jechonias's line. Luke 1:32 promises the throne to Jesus. If Joseph's seed generated Jesus, that promise would collide with Jeremiah 22:30. If Joseph is father only by legal standing, Jesus's right to the throne comes through the husband's line without his seed. This is a corroborating fit, not the main proof.

## Summary

[L4] Every verse that speaks to the child's origin traces it to Mary and to the Holy Ghost. None traces it to a man.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Mary was a virgin when she conceived. Luke 1:27 (παρθένος, parthenos, "virgin"), Luke 1:34 ("I know not a man", with ginōskō, "to know", read by Genesis 4:1), and Matthew 1:23 quoting Isaiah 7:14 (ʿalmāh, "young woman"), fixed by Genesis 24:16,43.
2. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, before Mary and Joseph came together, and Joseph did not know her until the birth. Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 (ek pneumatos, "out of the Spirit"), and Matthew 1:25 (eginōsken, "was knowing", imperfect, limited by "till she had brought forth").
3. The child was brought into being by divine power, and the human origin is the woman alone. Luke 1:35 (episkiasei, "will overshadow", read by Exodus 40:35) and Galatians 4:4 (ek gynaikos, "out of a woman"), supported by Genesis 3:15 ("her seed").
4. Joseph's fatherhood is legal and supposed, not generative. Matthew 1:16 (ἧς, hēs, a feminine relative pronoun, after the repeated ἐγέννησεν, egennēsen, "begat"), Luke 3:23 (ὡς ἐνομίζετο, hōs enomizeto, "as was supposed"), and Luke 2:48–49.
5. The royal line fits this: Jeremiah 22:30 read with Matthew 1:11–12 and 1:16 and Luke 1:32 shows the throne promise is not made through Joseph's seed.
6. Therefore Christ had no biological father. He was conceived of the Holy Ghost in Mary, a virgin, and Joseph was his father only by legal standing and in common supposition.

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# Challenger, Round 1: The seed is David's according to the flesh, and the named father is Joseph

**Thesis.** [L4] The KJV's seed rows require a seed out of a man's loins. The narration names one man of David's house beside Mary, and that man is Joseph. The defender's keystone (D6, "no biological father") cuts the oath sworn to David from the only Davidic line the narration supplies. The links beneath D6 rest on words read past what they state, and on a Greek Old Testament reading that is not the KJV.

## Against D6 and D3: the oath requires the loins

**[L1] Acts 2:30:** "God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- **[L2]** The Greek is ek karpou tēs osphyos autou (out of the fruit of his loins), kata sarka (according to the flesh).
- **[L3]** osphys (loins) is the word of Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." That is generation through a man.

**[L1] Romans 1:3:** "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L1] 2 Samuel 7:12:** "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."

**[L1] Psalm 132:11:** "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." The margin reads "Heb. belly."

**[L1] Hebrews 7:14:** "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

**[L1] Luke 2:4:** Joseph went to Bethlehem "because he was of the house and lineage of David."

**[L1] Luke 1:27:** "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David."

**[L1] Luke 1:36 with 1:5:** Mary's "cousin Elisabeth" is "of the daughters of Aaron."

**[L4] The chain:**
- The oath requires fruit of David's loins "according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30, with osphys read by Hebrews 7:10).
- The narration attaches David's house and lineage to Joseph (Luke 1:27; 2:4).
- The one kinswoman it gives Mary is Aaronic (Luke 1:5, 36).
- So D3's "the human origin is the woman alone," joined to D6, routes the flesh through the one person to whom the narration attaches no Davidic line. That leaves "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14) without the line the narration names.

**[L1] Numbers 1:18:** Israel "declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- **[L3]** The register was reckoned by the father's house.
- **[L3]** Ezra 2:62 shows the inverse. Priests "called after their name," the name of the wife's house (2:61), were "as polluted, put from the priesthood."

## Against D3: Galatians 4:4 and Genesis 3:15

**[L3] "Made of a woman" is the text's idiom of mortal birth. It is not a denial of a father:**
- Job 14:1: "Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble."
- Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist."
- John's father is named: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13).

**[L3] "Her seed" (Genesis 3:15) is not unusual. Seed is said of women whose children came by named men:**
- Hagar: "I will multiply thy seed exceedingly" (Genesis 16:10).
- Rebekah: "let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them" (Genesis 24:60).
- [L4] With these two rows (Genesis 16:10; 24:60) and the [L2] zar'ah (her seed) of Genesis 3:15, the defender's claim that seed attributed to a woman marks a manless origin has no footing.

## Against D3: Luke 1:35's verbs

**[L2] eperchomai (to come upon) is the verb of Acts 1:8:** "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me." It is said of the apostles. It names power and empowerment, not begetting.

**[L2] episkiazō (to overshadow) appears in these KJV rows:**
- Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them."
- Acts 5:15: "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."
- Neither denotes generation.

**[L3] The defender's footing for "overshadow" is Exodus 40:35, but the KJV text he quotes does not contain the word.** It reads "the cloud abode thereon." His [L2] reads: "In the Greek Old Testament it is used of the cloud over the tabernacle." A Greek-translation reading is not the Hebrew or Greek of a KJV row. That footing fails.

**[L1] Luke 1:35 says the child "shall be called the Son of God."**

# DEBATE SYNTHESIS

## 1. WHAT HELD AT L1–L2–L3 (no charge in either list contests it)

- **The oath's own vocabulary.** "Fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30), "the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3), "which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12), "of the fruit of thy body" (Psalm 132:11, margin "Heb. belly"), "sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14), "in the loins of his father" (Hebrews 7:10). Neither side disputes the words or the L2 glosses (osphys, sperma, kata sarka). The defender's R3 concedes the glosses themselves: "**They do not say who begat**" — the contest is over entailment, not over the text.
- **Joseph is placed in David's house by the narration.** Luke 1:27 ("a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David"); Luke 2:4 ("of the house and lineage of David"). The defender accepted the placement: "They place Joseph in David's house. They do not say Joseph begat the child."
- **Mary's only named kin are Aaronic.** Luke 1:5 ("of the daughters of Aaron") with Luke 1:36 ("thy cousin Elisabeth"). The defender: "I drop any claim that Mary's own house is stated."
- **At the annunciation Mary had not known a man.** Luke 1:34 read as present indicative — the challenger's own L2: "It states her condition when the angel spoke. It is not a vow." Both sides read it the same way.
- **Joseph is "her husband" and she "thy wife" from the espousal, as legal status.** Matthew 1:19, 1:20; Deuteronomy 22:24 ("his neighbour's wife"). Both sides treat this as status, not as proof of union.
- **The break in Matthew 1:16 is a textual fact.** egennēsen repeated through the list, then the passive egennēthē with feminine hēs at the last link. The challenger accepts the fact: "The passive does not narrate the begetting and says nothing against it."
- **"Son of God" is not a claim of biological divine paternity.** Neither list charges it. The challenger's footing (1 Chronicles 28:6, "I will be his father" said of Solomon; Acts 13:33 at the resurrection; Romans 1:4, "declared... by the resurrection") was not contested, and the defender expressly declined to rest on the title: "I do not rest D3 on the word 'Son' alone."

## 2. CONCESSIONS, NARROWINGS AND CHARGED POINTS

### Defender's links

- **D1 — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** "NARROWED TO: the limb that stands on Luke 1:27, Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:18–25. Isaiah 7:14 corroborates and is not load-bearing." Also: "I do not rest weight on *ʿalmāh* ('young woman') alone"; "I concede the formula does not by itself prove virginity from Isaiah."
- **D2 — CITED-WITH-FOOTING,** on Matthew 1:18, 1:20 (gennēthen, ek pneumatos hagiou, margin "Gr. begotten") and 1:25 (eginōsken), with the Matthew 1:16 egennēthē/hēs break. One limb shed: "Granted: it names the bearer, as Luke 1:13 does for Elisabeth. D2 does not rest on [Luke 1:35]." Scope limited: "I claim only the span up to the birth."
- **D3 — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE, with a self-identified circularity.** "NARROWED TO: Luke 1:34–35 as one question and answer. Galatians 4:4 and Genesis 3:15 are corroboration only." Then: "Galatians 4:4... **Taken alone it excludes nothing about a father**"; "Genesis 3:15, 'her seed,' is matched by Genesis 16:10 and Genesis 24:60. It is not load-bearing and **I withdraw it from the weight**"; "I drop any claim that Luke 1:27 states Mary's Davidic descent." And on the Romans 1:3 route: "I grant the KJV text never states Mary's descent. That is an inference from Romans 1:3, **resting on D3's own premise** that Mary is the sole human source. **It is not independent proof of D3.**"
- **D4 — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** "NARROWED TO: Joseph's fatherhood is 'supposed' in the text and is not the begetting. **I drop Ezra 2:61 as a model for the register**." Also "I concede the passive does not itself narrate the begetting"; "I concede *enomizeto* can have the milder sense 'was wont' (Acts 16:13)."
- **D5 — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** "NARROWED TO: the line fits and corroborates. It does not prove the premise, and D1–D4 do not rest on it." Also "I drop any claim that a register alone meets 'fruit of thy body' in Psalms 132:11"; "I concede Haggai 2:23 sets Zerubbabel as a signet and not on a throne"; "I concede the rule means the LORD could answer his own sentence."
- **D6 — CITED-WITH-FOOTING, but on narrowed supports:** "KEPT, resting on D1, D2 and D4, with D3 narrowed as above."

### Challenger's links

- **C1 (Joseph knew Mary within the espousal) — CITED-WITH-FOOTING,** held through the link round: the seed rows, Genesis 4:1 ("Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived"), the husband/wife status rows, Deuteronomy 22:24, and the "found with child" / "took unto him his wife" / "knew her not till" sequence. The defender's R2 charge against it — "A husband who knew the child was his would have no ground" — is the one the challenger's own list flagged: "supplies a ground the verse does not give."
- **C2 (Joseph alone is placed in David's house; reckoning by the father's house) — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** "**I drop 'only' as a universal** and keep the named rows."
- **C3 (Galatians 4:4 says what Job 14:1 and Matthew 11:11 say) — CITED-WITH-FOOTING, and conceded by the defender** in the words quoted under D3 above.
- **C4 (eperchomai/episkiazō name presence and power, not generation) — CITED-WITH-FOOTING.** Defender: "**I grant the verb means presence**," adding that Luke 1's context supplies the rest.
- **C5 (Isaiah's sign is bounded in Isaiah's own day) — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** "**I drop any claim that the two names are one**," and: "I set no verse against Matthew 1:22–23."
- **C6 (the curse does not carry D5) — NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.** "**I grant that Haggai seats Zerubbabel on no throne.** Jeremiah 22:30... stands as written."

### What the defender's close round answered, and what the format does with it

The close round put its answers in these words: on C1, "A husband who knew her would have no cause to be minded to put her away"; on C4, "the verb alone does not prove generation, but in Luke 1 its context does"; on the seed rows, "a daughter's child is still the fruit of her forefather's loins"; on C2, "Joseph's place in David's house and his legal fatherhood (D4) give the child the legal line." The system's close-round check marks 23 sentences in that round as grading or pressing the challenger's links and **disregards** them as grounds for any grade or count. The challenger's close is structurally last; no round follows it for the defender, so the absence of a further reply is procedural and counts against neither side. No verse the challenger first named in its close is counted — its close rests wholly on rows already pressed.

## 3. DRIFT GUARD VIOLATIONS BY THE CHALLENGER

**None fire.** Tested as claims and as grants/concessions:

- **The union and the named father (the guard's own L4).** The challenger pressed rather than declined it: "Therefore Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal" and, in closing, "On these rows, the child had a biological father, Joseph." No forbidden form appears in its mouth — no "no man," no "without sex" stated as fact, no Holy-Ghost-as-paternity, no flesh routed through Mary alone. It argued *against* the Mary route, noting the defender "conceded that Mary's house is never stated."
- **The Son's title.** Handled as covenant and resurrection: "That title is a covenant title. Acts 13:33 sets 'this day have I begotten thee' at the resurrection," with 1 Chronicles 28:6 and Romans 1:4. No divine-paternity reading asserted; no reverse closure ("a mere man's honorific") either.
- **The genealogies.** The challenger *refused* an invented resolution: "the defender's 'one of them is a different channel' resolves the divergence between the genealogies by a channel neither genealogy states."
- **Verse against verse.** Refused: "I set no verse against Matthew 1:22–23." Isaiah 8's near-referent was filed beside Matthew's "fulfilled," not over it.
- **An excluded apparatus footing.** Refused, not defended: "A Greek-translation reading is not the Hebrew or Greek of a KJV row. That footing fails."
- **Seed, not blood.** No blood-word is used as a lineage verdict; John 1:13's "not of blood" appears only as quoted text about the ek-of-God construction.
- **Its own grants** ("Haggai seats Zerubbabel on no throne"; "the two names are one" dropped; "only" dropped) concede only true points of the text and touch no forbidden category.

## 4. ENGAGEMENT AND WHETHER THE DEFENSE HELD

**The challenger engaged chains as chains.** It built a single load-bearing spine and kept it: the oath's loins (2 Samuel 7:12; Psalm 132:11) → its application to Christ (Acts 2:30; Romans 1:3) → its visibility (Hebrews 7:14) → the loins' meaning (Hebrews 7:10), then attached the reckoning rule (Numbers 1:2, 18; Ezra 2:61–62), then read the timing rows *inside* that spine rather than against it (Matthew 1:18 dates the finding; 1:24 the taking; 1:25 the bounded abstinence; 1 Corinthians 7:5; Genesis 4:1; Deuteronomy 22:24). It exhibited L2 on both sides of the contest (hēs; egennēsen/egennēthē; enomizeto; episkiazō/eperchomai; ʿalmāh/bĕtûlāh; ginomai ek) and conceded where the text was against it — Haggai, the two Isaiah names, the word "only." It did not demand a single stating verse of the defender; it laid its links out to be counted.

**The defense held its thesis but not its footing.** D6 survived, and the defender's method was disciplined — it answered at the link level, marked charges "Noted. Not conceding here. Goes to review," and then actually conceded them. But by the close, four of six links were narrowed and the load-bearing supports were surrendered in its own words: Galatians 4:4 "excludes nothing about a father"; Genesis 3:15 withdrawn "from the weight"; ʿalmāh dropped as proof; Ezra 2:61 dropped as a register model; "the passive does not itself narrate the begetting"; Mary's descent conceded never stated, and the Romans 1:3 route to her admitted to rest on D3's own premise. What remains standing for D6 is Luke 1:27, 1:34, Matthew 1:18–25, the 1:16 formula break, and enomizeto — plus the angel's *gar* in Matthew 1:20.

## 5. MOST VULNERABLE

**On the defender's side, three exposed joints.** (a) The Matthew 1:18 phrase itself: "before they came together, she was found with child" — the whole case requires "found" to date a discovery of a conception that the challenger places earlier, and the defender's strongest remaining move is an inference about Joseph's motive in 1:19, which the challenger had already flagged as a supplied ground. (b) The seed rows are not answered, only denied a referent: "a daughter's child is still the fruit of her forefather's loins" requires a Davidic daughter the defender conceded the text never names, and the defender's own words mark that route as circular. (c) D6 now leans on a passive verb the defender conceded "does not itself narrate the begetting," and on a title the defender declined to load.

**On the challenger's side, three exposed joints.** (a) C1 is an [L4] inference from necessity (loins require seed; seed comes by knowing; the one named Davidic man is the husband) — the text nowhere narrates Joseph knowing Mary, and the reading must distinguish "found with child" from "conceived." That is the single hardest row in the debate and it cuts both ways. (b) C2's Numbers 1:2, 18 is a census rule for Israel's numbering; carrying it to "how the Messiah's Davidic descent is evident" (Hebrews 7:14) is a chain step the challenger asserts more than exhibits, though the defender's retreat from the register model leaves it standing without a competitor. (c) C5 and C6 are narrowed to near-empty: the challenger granted that Haggai seats Zerubbabel on no throne and must rely on the LORD's freedom to answer his own sentence — a true point about the text's God, but not a demonstration.

The tightest collision left on the table is a single pair of rows read two ways: Matthew 1:18–25 as either the exclusion of a begetter or the dating of a discovery, set against Acts 2:30's "fruit of his loins, according to the flesh."

**LINK 6: SUPPORTED**

Footing:
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The KJV margin reads "Gr. begotten".
- [L2] gennaō (to beget) is the verb the genealogy uses of fathers: "Abraham begat Isaac" (Matthew 1:2). Matthew 1:20 names the source of the child's begetting as pneuma hagion (Holy Spirit), not Joseph.
- [L2] Matthew 1:16 breaks the pattern: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The relative pronoun hēs (of whom) is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone. The verb is passive, egennēthē (was born), where the earlier links read egennēsen (begat).
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." [L2] enomizeto (was reckoned) marks a supposition.
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The source named is Mary, with ek sou (out of you).

Chain: the text's begetting verb is used of fathers, and in the one case of this child it gives the Holy Ghost as source and Mary as the one born of. Joseph appears only as "supposed". So he is no begetter.

The pressed verses:
- Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ."
- Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- Hebrews 7:14: "our Lord sprang out of Juda."

None of these names a father. [L2] ginomenou ek spermatos (made out of seed) and anatetalken (has risen up, as a sprout) state descent. They do not say who begat. The oath names David's fruit, and a daughter's child is still the fruit of her forefather's loins. Genesis 3:15 says "her seed". I hold this chain as inference.

Luke 2:4 ("because he was of the house and lineage of David") and Luke 1:27 ("a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David") place Joseph in David's house. They do not say Joseph begat the child.

Genesis 4:1 ("Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived") and Deuteronomy 22:24 ("his neighbour's wife") give the ordinary rule. Matthew 1:20 states the exception.

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** the body of the child is stated to come out of the woman, and the Davidic line reaches him as her seed. I drop any claim that Luke 1:27 states Mary's Davidic descent.

Footing:

Acts 1:8 "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." Exodus 40:35 "the cloud abode thereon." These show the verb for presence and power. In Luke 1:35 the verse continues with "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The "therefore" ties the birth to the coming upon, which no other pressed verse does.

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED.** The premise: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, before the taking that Matthew 1:18 and 1:24 mark.

Footing:

- **[L3] The law already calls a betrothed damsel a wife.** Deuteronomy 22:24: "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife."

  - Romans 1:3 adds *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh") when bodily origin is meant. Matthew 1:20's *ek pneumatos hagiou* ("of the Holy Ghost") carries no *kata sarka*.
  - The *ek* + God construction elsewhere marks covenant origin. 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."

Chain: the seed must come out of a man's loins. The text's means of begetting is knowing. The one husband the text names is Joseph, and he is husband from the espousal. Therefore, at [L4] on these rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

The pressed verses, read inside that chain:
- **Matthew 1:18**, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." This dates the *finding*. Matthew himself sets what "came together" means by what follows: "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24), her coming into his house. 1 Corinthians 7:5, "come together again," shows the verb names married union. That is all I draw from it.
- **Matthew 1:20**, "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The *gar* ("for") grounds the command "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." It gives the reason to take her, not a begetter.
- **Matthew 1:25**, "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." This bounds the abstinence to the time after the taking. "Till" fixes its end.
- **Luke 1:35**, "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." This names the bearer, as Luke 1:13 names Elisabeth the bearer to a named father.

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO:** the text places only Joseph in David's house, and its reckoning runs by the father's house. I drop "only" as a universal and keep the named rows.

Footing:
- **[L1] Reckoning is by the father's house.**
  - Numbers 1:2: "after their families, by the house of their fathers."
  - Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."

  - Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
  - Luke 1:27: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David."
- **[L2] Luke 1:27's grammar.** In Greek, *ex oikou David* ("of the house of David") follows *andri ... Iōsēph* ("a man ... Joseph").
- **[L3] Mary's only stated kin is Aaronic.**
  - Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth."
  - Luke 1:5: "his wife was of the daughters of Aaron."

The defender has dropped any claim that Mary's Davidic descent is stated. So "a daughter's child is the fruit of her forefather's loins" rests on a daughter the text never places in David's house.

The pressed verses:
- **Matthew 1:3**, "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." The begetting verb is Judah's. The mother is named with "of," and the line runs through the father. This verse is my witness.
- **Matthew 1:16**, "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The line Matthew writes ends at Joseph. The passive does not narrate the begetting and says nothing against it.
- **Luke 3:23**, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." [L2] *enomizeto* is the same form as Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made." The verb carries no verdict of its own. It stands beside Mary's own words: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48).
- **Luke 1:32**, "the throne of his father David." The throne comes through the father's house.
- **Genesis 3:15**, "her seed." Genesis 16:10 (Hagar) and Genesis 24:60 (Rebekah) also give women seed. None of these women is of David's house.

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED.** The premise: Galatians 4:4 says what Job 14:1 and Matthew 11:11 say of every man.

Footing:
- **[L1] The verse itself.** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." Both phrases describe condition.
- **[L3] The same words are said of every mortal.**
  - Job 14:1: "Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble."
  - Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist."
- **[L1] John's father is named.** Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- **[L2] The construction.** *ginomenon ek gynaikos* ("made of a woman") names the bearer, as *ginomenou ek spermatos* ("made of the seed") names the seed (Romans 1:3).

Chain: "born of women" is said of John, whose father is named. So the phrase names the mortal bearer and says nothing about a father's absence.

The pressed verses:
- **Luke 1:31**, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." It lacks "bear thee" because it is spoken to the mother. Luke 1:13 is spoken to the father.
- **Luke 1:35**, "born of thee," likewise names the bearer.
- **Matthew 1:20**: see Link 1. *ek* without *kata sarka* marks origin, not paternity.

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED.** The premise: the two verbs name presence and power, not generation.

Footing:
- **[L1] Overshadowing at the transfiguration.** Luke 9:34-35: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them ... And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him." The overshadowing and the title "Son" come together over a grown man, with no generation.
- **[L1] Overshadowing by Peter's shadow.** Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."
- **[L1] The coming upon at Pentecost.** Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." This is the same verb as Luke 1:35, said to the apostles.
