CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 4, CLOSE ROUND

# ROUND 4: THE CHALLENGER'S CLOSE

The record's reading of the topic: Christ had a biological father, Joseph, of the house of David. The promised seed comes out of a man's body according to the flesh. The text names Joseph as father in Mary's mouth, the narrator's, the town's and a disciple's. Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal, and the timing rows, read in Matthew's own order, bound the abstinence to the pregnancy. I keep C1 to C6 as my link round numbered them and add no new witness.

## C1: the seed proceeds out of a man's body, according to the flesh

- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." The seed comes out of David's own body.
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." The apostle applies the oath to Christ, from the loins and according to the flesh.
- [L2] In Acts 2:30 the word is *osphys* (G3751, loins). In Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh," the word is *sperma* (G4690, seed) with *kata sarka* (according to the flesh).
- [L3] Hebrews 7:5 uses the same loins-word for descent through fathers: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham." Hebrews 7:10 does the same: "he was yet in the loins of his father." Psalms 132:11 reads "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne" (margin "Heb. belly").
- [L3] Hebrews 7:14: "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." The tribe is counted as Numbers 1:2 counts it, "by the house of their fathers."
- [L4] From these rows: the seed is carried in a man's loins, and the tribe is counted through the fathers. So the seed that is "evident" out of Juda reaches the child through a man of David's house. The one such man the text names beside Mary is Joseph, "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27), "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).

## C2: the father is named, in four mouths

- [L1] Mary says to the child, in Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L1] The town, in John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"
- [L1] A disciple, in John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
- [L1] The narrator, in Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover." Also Luke 2:27: "the parents brought in the child Jesus."
- [L2] *patēr* (G3962, father) stands in Mary's words at Luke 2:48. *goneis* (G1118, parents) stands in the narrator's voice at Luke 2:41 and 2:27.
- [L3] The angel addresses the same man by his line: "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). Joseph does the father's act of naming, "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:21), and "he called his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:25). The same act is the father's in Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called."
- [L4] Mary received the angel's word, and she names Joseph "thy father." Luke himself narrates "his parents." These rows, with the angel's "son of David" and the father's naming, name Joseph as the father. Luke 2:49's "my Father's business" stands beside Mary's "thy father" in the same scene. It does not cancel her word, and the title carries its own covenant sense in C4.

## C3: husband and wife from the espousal; the union within it

- [L1] Matthew 1:19 has "Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20 has "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- [L2] In Matthew 1:19 the word is *anēr* (G435, man, husband). In Matthew 1:20 it is *gynē* (G1135, "a woman; specially, a wife").
- [L3] The law calls the betrothed damsel a wife in Deuteronomy 22:24: "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." It names the taking as a later step in Deuteronomy 20:7: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- [L3] The canon's stated means of begetting is Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L4] The seed rows of C1 require seed out of a man's loins. Genesis 4:1 gives knowing as the means. The man and woman were husband and wife from the espousal (Matthew 1:19-20; Deuteronomy 22:24). On those rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.
- [L1] The timing rows are held as written and read in Matthew's own order. The first is Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." This dates the finding. The second is Matthew 1:24: Joseph "took unto him his wife." This is the taking that Deuteronomy 20:7 distinguishes from betrothal. The third is Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *heōs* (G2193, until) bounds the not-knowing of Matthew 1:25 to the time after the taking and before the birth.
- [L4] So the not-knowing covers the pregnancy. No row of the account says she conceived without a man.

## C4: Mary's words, the angel's verbs, and the title

- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, know) stands there in the present indicative. It gives her state when the angel spoke.
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904, come upon) and *episkiazō* (G1982, overshadow) are the two verbs of Luke 1:35.
- [L3] The same Luke uses the same verb of the apostles in Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." Acts 1:8 says that coming brings power ("ye shall receive power"), and Luke 24:49 calls it being "endued with power from on high." The overshadowing verb stands at Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them," and at Acts 5:15, "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."
- [L4] At these rows the two verbs name power and presence, and none of them names begetting. Luke 1:35's answer gives the power and presence of God upon her and is read with those rows.
- [L1] Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title is given with the throne before Mary's question at 1:34.
- [L3] It is the covenant title of David's son. The covenant title is 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son." 1 Chronicles 28:6 joins the two in one verse: "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him [to be] my son." Its fulfilment comes at the resurrection, in Acts 13:33: "he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written... this day have I begotten thee." Romans 1:4 says the same: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead."
- [L4] The title "Son of God" stands beside a named human father in 1 Chronicles 28:6. So it does not decide the question of the biological father.

## C5: "of the Holy Ghost," the passive at Matthew 1:16, and "made of a woman"

- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (margin "Gr. begotten").
- [L2] The margin's word is *gennaō* (G1080, beget).
- [L3] In the same family of words, God's begetting is said of men who had fathers. 1 John 5:1 reads "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." 1 John 4:7 reads "every one that loveth is born of God." John 1:13 reads "born... of God," of "them that believe on his name" (John 1:12).
- [L4] "Of God" and "of the Holy Ghost" name covenant origin at these rows, and the men they are said of had fathers. Romans 1:3 adds "according to the flesh" where the flesh is meant. Matthew 1:20 lacks that phrase, so it is not a word of paternity.
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The verse does not narrate the begetting. It says "of whom was born" and stops there.
- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman, made under the law."
- [L3] The same phrase is said of all men in Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days." It is said of John, whose father is named (Luke 1:13), in Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women."
- [L4] "Of a woman" is the mark of a mortal man born like his brethren. At these rows it does not remove a father.

## C6: reckoning by the father's house, the supposed son, and the curse

- [L1] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L2] *bayith* (H1004, house) and *ab* (H1, father) are the words of Numbers 1:18.
- [L3] The register rejected the name taken from the wife's house in Ezra 2:61-62. The priests "called after their name," that of the daughters of Barzillai, "were... as polluted, put from the priesthood." Mary's own house is not stated. Luke 1:36 calls Elisabeth her "cousin," and Luke 1:5 places Elisabeth "of the daughters of Aaron."
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] The verb *enomizeto* (G3543) is the same form as Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made."
- [L4] The verb carries no verdict of its own. In Luke it stands with Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48).
- [L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- [L3] Jeremiah's own rule on pronounced sentences is Jeremiah 18:8: "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil." The line continues in Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." The LORD sets his choice on that grandson in Haggai 2:23: "O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel... will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee."
- [L4] The line through Jechonias is the line the LORD himself chose again. So the curse does not stand against seed through Joseph.

## Close

Precept upon precept, the case is this:
- The oath requires seed "out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30).
- Mary names the father in Luke 2:48: "thy father and I."
- The angel names him in Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David... Mary thy wife."
- The canon names the means in Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- "Knew her not till" (Matthew 1:25) bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking (Matthew 1:24).
- "Of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20) and "the Son of God" (Luke 1:35) are covenant words, said of sons who had fathers (1 John 5:1; 1 Chronicles 28:6).

So the record's answer to the topic is that Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the named son of David. On the rows above, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** "Biological father" here means a man whose seed, through union with the mother, produced the child. The KJV gives the child's conception a different source: the Holy Ghost acting on Mary, a virgin who knew no man. Joseph was the husband of Mary, the one who named the child, and the legal father. He was not the begetter.

---

## 1. The conception is stated to be of the Holy Ghost, before any union

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek is *prin ē synelthein autous* (G4250/G4905), "before they came together". The word *synerchomai* means to come together, and here it means the marriage union. The source is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537, G4151, G40), "out of the Holy Ghost". The preposition *ek* marks origin.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *To gennēthen* (G1080) means "that which has been begotten or conceived". It is again followed by *ek pneumatos hagiou*, so the origin is the Holy Ghost.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." *Eginōsken* (G1097) means "knew", the same word used in the next point.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the coming together, and Matthew 1:25 puts the birth before any knowing. Matthew 1:20 names the source as the Holy Ghost. Together these three verses leave no male parent in the conception. The source is named as divine, and the order of events excludes a human father.

## 2. Mary says she knows no man, and the angel's answer gives a power, not a man

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097), "to know", is used here of the marital relation. *Andra* (G435) is "a man, a male".

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Dunamis* (G1411) is "power". *Episkiazō* (G1982) is "to overshadow". *Dio kai* (G1352) is "wherefore also", which makes the Holy Ghost's coming and the Highest's power the ground of the title. The child is "born *of thee*", *ek sou* (G1537), out of Mary.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph… and the virgin's name was Mary." *Parthenos* (G3933) is "virgin". The Holy Ghost's act came on a woman the text calls a virgin.

**[L4]** Mary's question asks how conception could occur without knowing a man (Luke 1:34, *ginōskō*). The angel's reply (Luke 1:35) supplies a cause that does not involve a man, namely the coming of the Holy Ghost and the overshadowing power (*dunamis*, *episkiazō*). Her virginity (Luke 1:27) and her question stand together with that answer, so the conception is virginal.

## 3. Matthew's genealogy changes its formula at the end

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Through Matthew 1:2–16 the line runs by *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat". At the end the verb becomes *egennēthē* (the passive, "was born"), and the relative pronoun is *hēs* (G3739), feminine singular, "of whom". It points back to Mary. It does not point to Joseph, who is called only her "husband" (*anēr*, G435).

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20, in the same chapter, says of the child that "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost".

**[L4]** The formula "X begat Y" holds from Abraham to Joseph, and then the text uses "was born of whom", feminine. The shift from the active "begat" to the passive "was born", with a feminine antecedent, is the genealogist's own marking of where the line of begetting ends. Matthew 1:20 supplies the reason.

## 4. Joseph's response shows he was not the father

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *Apolusai* (G630) means "to release, put away". *Paralabein* (G3880) means "to take to oneself". The angel commands Joseph to take Mary to himself on the ground (*gar*, G1063, "for") that the conception is of the Holy Ghost.

**[L4]** A husband who had fathered the child would have had no cause to consider putting her away (Matthew 1:19). The angel's remedy is a ground (*gar*) that the conception is of the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:20). That ground answers Joseph's concern only if the child was not his. The Matthew 1:19 and 1:20 pair therefore shows Joseph understood himself not to be the father until the angel explained the source.

## 5. The title "father" for Joseph is a supposition, and the child corrects it

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *Enomizeto* (G3543) means "was reckoned, was thought according to custom". It marks a view held by others.

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49: "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?"

**[L3]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is the crowd's statement of what they supposed.

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 labels the "son of Joseph" claim as a supposition (*enomizeto*). In Luke 2:49 the child answers Mary's "thy father" by pointing to "my father's business", which locates his Father in God's house (Luke 2:49). Both ground the title "father" in legal and household custom. Neither supports a claim of begetting.

## 6. The woman is named as the source of the body

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *Genomenon ek gunaikos* (G1096, G1537, G1135) means "come to be out of a woman". The text names the woman as the origin of the Son's human being.

**[L3]** Genesis 3:15: "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed." The promised deliverer is called her seed, and no man's seed is named beside it.

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." *Katartizō* (G2675) means "to fit out, prepare". The body is stated to be prepared by God.

**[L4]** Galatians 4:4 puts the woman as the origin of the Son's human being. Genesis 3:15 calls the deliverer "her seed". Hebrews 10:5 says God prepared the body. Together these three verses assign the body's source to a woman and to God, and no male parent appears in them.

## 7. Isaiah's sign, as the KJV gives it

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** The Hebrew word behind the KJV's "virgin" is *ʿalmāh* (H5959).

**[L3]** Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water". The same Hebrew word stands behind the KJV's "virgin" there, and Genesis 24:16 describes the same Rebekah as one "neither had any man known her".

**[L1]** Matthew 1:23 cites it: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel."

**[L4]** The KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 translates *ʿalmāh*. Genesis 24:43 uses the same word for Rebekah, whom Genesis 24:16 describes as unknown by any man. Matthew 1:23 applies the prophecy to Mary, and Luke 1:27 and 1:34 supply her virginity. The sign is a conception by a virgin.

---

## Anticipated objections, answered with the text

**"Of the seed of David" (Romans 1:3) and "fruit of his loins" (Acts 2:30).**

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". **[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ".

**[L3]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father", said of Levi, who was in Abraham's loins several generations before his birth.

**[L4]** "Loins" language in Hebrews 7:10 covers remote descent. Since Luke 1:27 and 1:32 tie the promise to Mary, a virgin of the house of David, the descent from David (Romans 1:3) comes through the mother (Galatians 4:4, "made of a woman"). It does not require a male begetter.

**"His father David" (Luke 1:32).**

**[L1]** Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David".

**[L3]** Luke 1:73: "The oath which he sware to our father Abraham". *Patēr* (G3962) is used of ancestors as well as begetters, so "father" in Luke 1:32 names a forebear and does not assert a begetting.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. The conception is sourced "of the Holy Ghost" (*ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Ghost"), and it is stated to precede any coming together or knowing. Footing: Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], with *ek* and *prin ē synelthein* [L2], and Matthew 1:25 [L3].
2. Mary was a virgin who knew no man, and the angel names the Holy Ghost's coming and the Highest's power (*dunamis*, "power") as the means. Footing: Luke 1:34–35 [L1], with *ginōskō* and *dunamis* [L2], and Luke 1:27 [L3].
3. Matthew's genealogy ends the line of "begat" at Joseph and gives the birth as "of whom was born Jesus", feminine (*hēs*), pointing to Mary. Footing: Matthew 1:16 [L1], with *egennēsen* and *hēs* [L2], and Matthew 1:20 [L3].

### 1. What held at L1-L2-L3?

A point is listed here only if no charge in either side's lists contests it. Any point contested by a charge is placed under section 2 as unresolved.

1. **Joseph's Davidic Lineage**: Joseph is of the house and lineage of David. Footing: Luke 1:27 ("a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David") and Luke 2:4 ("because he was of the house and lineage of David").
2. **Espousal Status Under the Law**: An espoused woman is denominated a "wife" prior to the consummation of the marriage. Footing: Deuteronomy 22:24 ("his neighbour's wife"), Matthew 1:19 ("Joseph her husband"), and Matthew 1:20 ("Mary thy wife").
3. **The Naming of the Child by Joseph**: Joseph performed the father's naming act in obedience to the angel's command. Footing: Matthew 1:21 ("thou shalt call his name JESUS") and Matthew 1:25 ("and he called his name JESUS").
4. **Mary's Address and Christ's Reply**: Mary addressed Joseph as father, and Christ pointed to God's business. Footing: Luke 2:48 ("thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing") and Luke 2:49 ("wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?").
5. **The Flesh/Spirit Distinction of John 3:6**: The text maintains a distinction between that which is born of the flesh and that which is born of the Spirit. Footing: John 3:6 ("That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit").
6. **Remote Loins-Descent in Hebrews 7**: Loins-language encompasses descent across successive generations. Footing: Hebrews 7:5 ("though they come out of the loins of Abraham") and Hebrews 7:10 ("For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him").

---

### 2. Concessions, Link Rounds, and Close Rounds

- **Link D1**: CITED-WITH-FOOTING.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological human father

**Position.** "Biological father" means a male parent who supplies the seed of the child's conception. The KJV text says the child's conception was *of the Holy Ghost*, within a virgin, with no man involved. Joseph was husband, legal father and guardian, but not begetter.

## 1. The text states the mode of conception

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *sunerchomai* (G4905), "to come together," is the verb for the couple's union. The text places the conception before that union. *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537 + G4151 + G40), "out of the Holy Ghost," gives the source of the pregnancy with the preposition *ek*, "out of," marking origin.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *to gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "that which is begotten or conceived," is the same root used for the human "begats" of Matthew 1. Here the begetting is attributed to the Holy Ghost, not to a man.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the conception before any union with Joseph. Matthew 1:20, through *gennaō* with *ek*, assigns the origin of the conceived child to the Holy Ghost. So no human male is the origin of the child, which excludes a biological human father. This rests on two [L1] verses and two [L2] grounds.

## 2. Mary's own testimony and the angel's answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," is used here of sexual knowledge. *anēr* (G435) is "a man," a male. Mary is betrothed, so the question concerns the manner of conception, not the future.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow," and *eperchomai* (G1904), "to come upon," describe divine action. *dio kai* (G1352), "therefore also," makes the divine action the stated reason for the title.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Mary is called a virgin before the angel speaks.

**[L4]** The angel answers "how" with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, not with a man. Luke 1:27 says she was a virgin and Luke 1:34 says she knew no man. Together these show the angel's answer replaces human paternity. A biological father would not need "therefore" to ground the title.

## 3. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Every earlier link in Matthew 1 uses *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," with a male subject. At the last link the verb becomes passive, *egennēthē*, "was born." The relative pronoun *ex hēs* (G1537), "out of whom," is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone. Joseph is called *anēr* (G435), "husband," not begetter.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

**[L4]** The chain of "begat" ends at Joseph, and the birth is "of whom," feminine, namely Mary. Matthew 1:25 repeats the verb *ginōskō*, "know," for Joseph and Mary, and says he did not know her until the child was born. The verse and the Greek grammar together show Joseph's role changes from begetter to husband.

## 4. Joseph's reaction and the "as was supposed"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

**[L4]** Joseph knew he had not fathered the child, and resolved to put Mary away until the angel spoke. This is Joseph's own judgment on the facts, and it is corrected only by the angel, who says the child is "of the Holy Ghost," not by any claim that Joseph was the father.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*), "was reckoned, was supposed by custom," marks the common opinion as an opinion, not as the truth.

**[L3]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is the crowd's claim, matching Luke 3:23's "as was supposed." Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Mary speaks of Joseph as "thy father" by household usage, and the child answers with "my Father's business."

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 labels "son of Joseph" a supposition. The later passages show the same pattern: the crowd's talk and the household's talk use "father" of Joseph, but the child himself names another Father in Luke 2:49. The title is legal and customary, not a claim of begetting.

## 5. The prophecy and Paul's wording

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** *ʿalmāh* (H5959), "a young woman of marriageable age, unmarried," is rendered in Matthew 1:23 with *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."

# Link round: the defender's answers

The challenger's list carries its verses under "ROWS GIVE", not under a "PRESSED WITH" label (ruling 392). I answer every one of them anyway, quoting each.

## LINK D1: SUPPORTED

**Challenger's rows:** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God" (1 John 5:1); "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3); "Joseph, thou son of David … Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20).

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** G1064 *gastēr*, "belly, womb," stands in the Greek of "with child." The conception is therefore a literal pregnancy in the womb. G4905 *synerchomai* is "come together … or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)." In Matthew 1:24 the "taking" is G3880 *paralambanō*, "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself." Matthew uses two different verbs. The challenger equates them without a row.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Joseph knew her not before the finding (1:18, before they came together). He knew her not after it (1:25). The challenger's own bounding of 1:25 to "the pregnancy after the taking" leaves the conception in the one gap where 1:18 says there was no coming together.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 (*synerchomai*, conjugal union, after the finding) and Matthew 1:25 (no knowing till the birth) together leave no union of Joseph and Mary before the birth. A conception "of the Holy Ghost" in that womb therefore has no human begetter beside it.

**On 1 John 5:1 and John 1:13.**

**[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."

**[L2]** G1080 *gennaō* carries "figuratively, to regenerate" in its range. 1 John 5:1 is a regeneration of those who "believeth." Matthew 1:20 is a "conceived in her."

**[L3]** John 1:13 itself uses *ek* ("of") with God to exclude "the will of man" as the origin. The challenger's own row therefore shows *ek theou* ("of God") marking the origin as not human.

**[L4]** The figure of 1 John 5:1 is carried by its context of faith. The context of Matthew 1:18-20 is a womb, a betrothal and an unbroken "knew her not." John 1:13 and Matthew 1:25 are footings; the figure cannot be carried across into a literal pregnancy.

**On Romans 1:3.**

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L2]** The verb is G1096 *ginomai*, "made, become." It is the same verb Paul uses of Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman." It is not *gennaō*, "begat."

**[L3]** Romans 9:5: "and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ [came]."

**[L4]** "According to the flesh" marks descent from David and from Israel. It names the race, not a male parent. Luke 3:31 supplies a second line (see D6).

## LINK D2: SUPPORTED

**Challenger's rows:** "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32); "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses" (Acts 1:8); "Solomon thy son … I have chosen him [to be] my son" (1 Chronicles 28:6).

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** G4459 *pōs*, "in what way?", asks the manner. G1904 *eperchomai* is "to supervene, i.e. arrive … (figuratively) influence." G1982 *episkiazō* is "to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence." The challenger rightly cites Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34 as power and presence. That is divine action on persons, and no man's act appears in either verb.

**[L3]** Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible." The angel answers "how" with a ground in impossibility. Mary has asked about a conception she cannot account for. A conception by Joseph after the taking would not call for "nothing shall be impossible."

**[L4]** On Luke 1:34-37: the question "how" is answered by the Holy Ghost's coming and the power of the Highest, then grounded in "nothing impossible." The present tense of "I know not" does not hollow out the question. Mary is already "espoused" (Luke 1:27), so a coming marriage was known to her. She asks "how," not "when." The answer names God and no man, so the angel's answer does supply the means in place of a begetter.

**On "therefore" and Solomon.**

**[L1]** 1 Chronicles 28:6: "for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."

**[L2]** *dio kai* (G1352) is "therefore also." In Luke 1:35 it follows immediately on "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee."

**[L3]** Solomon's sonship rests on "I have chosen him," which is an election. Luke 1:35's sonship rests on "therefore," a consequence of the Holy Ghost's coming and of what is "born of thee." Election is a different ground from conception.

**[L4]** The ground sits in the adjacent clause, the Holy Ghost's coming (Luke 1:35), and the challenger's own contrast with 1 Chronicles 28:6 ("chosen") shows a different ground. The "therefore" is therefore not carried back to Luke 1:32.

## LINK D3: SUPPORTED

**Challenger's rows:** "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar" (Matthew 1:3); "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab" (Matthew 1:5).

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** In Matthew 1:3 and 1:5 the active verb G1080 *gennaō*, "beget," has the man as its subject, and the mother is added by *ek*. In 1:16 *gennaō* is passive, "was born," and Joseph, G435 *anēr*, is called "husband." No "Joseph begat Jesus" stands in the verse.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:3 and 1:5 show that where Matthew means a man beside the mother, he writes "X begat Y." The challenger's own rows demonstrate the pattern, and 1:16 is the one place that omits it.

**[L4]** The challenger's rows (1:3, 1:5) show Matthew's habit of writing the man's active "begat." Matthew 1:16 breaks it at the one link where Matthew 1:25 says "knew her not." Matthew 1:16 replaces "begat" with "husband," so the grammar fits my link, not the challenger's.

Here is the debate synthesis following the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction.

---

### 1. What held at L1-L2-L3?

A point is listed here only if no charge in either side's lists contests it. Points where the interpretation or application was contested appear under Section 2.

*   **The status of betrothal in law:** That Joseph and Mary were husband and wife in law from their espousal: Matthew 1:19 names "Joseph her husband," Matthew 1:20 states "Mary thy wife," and Deuteronomy 22:24 refers to the betrothed damsel as "his neighbour's wife." Both sides agreed on this status (Defender R3 Link 1: "The betrothed is a wife in law"; Defender R4: "That the pair are 'husband' and 'wife' from the espousal is granted").
*   **The mortality idiom of "born of a woman":** Job 14:1 ("Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble") functions as an idiom denoting human mortality, which is also applied to John the Baptist in Matthew 11:11 ("Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist"). The Defender granted this general usage (Defender R2: "I grant that Job 14:1 and 15:14 show the phrase 'born of a woman' as an idiom of mortality"; Defender R4: "I grant it for mankind in general").
*   **Reckoning by fathers' houses in registers:** Numbers 1:18 ("declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers") and Ezra 2:61-62 establish that genealogies and registers were formally declared and reckoned by the father's house. The Defender acknowledged this rule of registers (Defender R3 Link 6: "I concede it shows registers counted by fathers' houses").
*   **The lack of an explicit knowledge-verb in Matthew 1:19:** The text of Matthew 1:19 ("Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily") expresses intent (*boulomai*) and moral character (*dikaios*), but contains no explicit verb denoting prior knowledge of the pregnancy's origin (Defender R2 Link D4: "I concede that Matthew 1:19 has no knowledge-verb").
*   **The textual lack of a named father for Mary in the registers:** Neither Luke 3 nor any other text explicitly names Mary's father as Heli or traces her biological lineage directly through Nathan (Defender R3 Link 6: "The rows do not state that Mary's line runs by Nathan, so I drop that limb. I concede no row gives Mary a father named Heli or the line of Nathan").
*   **Haggai 2:23 makes no explicit mention of the word "throne":** Haggai 2:23 names Zerubbabel as a "signet" and "chosen," but does not use the noun *kisse'* or the word "throne" (Challenger R3 Link 5: "I drop the reading that Haggai 2:23 itself names the throne").

---

### 2. Concessions, Narrowings, and Link Status

#### Defender's Declared Chain (D1–D6)

*   **LINK D1:** The conception is "of the Holy Ghost" before Mary and Joseph "came together" (Matthew 1:18, 20).
    *   *Status:* CITED-WITH-FOOTING.
    *   *Challenger's Press:* Challenger pressed with 1 John 5:1, John 1:13, Romans 1:3, Matthew 1:24, Deuteronomy 20:7, and Genesis 4:1, arguing that *ek theou*/*ek pneumatos* indicates covenant origin rather than biological paternity, and that "before they came together" dates the finding prior to the taking.
    *   *Defender's Response & Close:* Defender maintained the link with [L1] Matthew 1:18, 20, [L2] *synerchomai* and *gennaō*, and [L3] Matthew 1:19, arguing that *synerchomai* denotes conjugal cohabitation and that Matthew 1:25's "knew her not till" excludes union prior to the birth.
*   **LINK D2:** Mary knew not a man; the angel answers with the Holy Ghost, not a man (Luke 1:34-35).
    *   *Status:* CITED-WITH-FOOTING.
    *   *Challenger's Press:* Challenger pressed with Luke 1:32, Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, and 1 Chronicles 28:6, asserting that *eperchomai* and *episkiazō* denote divine presence/power, and *dio kai* ("therefore") refers back to the title in verse 32.
    *   *Defender's Response & Close:* Defender maintained the link with [L1] Luke 1:34-35, [L2] *episkiazō* and *dio*, and [L3] Luke 1:27, 37, stating that the angel answers "How?" with divine power, and *dio* links the title directly to the overshadowing.
*   **LINK D3:** Matthew 1:16 ends the line with Joseph as husband, not begetter (*ex hēs*).
    *   *Status:* CITED-WITH-FOOTING.
    *   *Challenger's Press:* Challenger pressed with Matthew 1:3, 5, 16, arguing that *ek* with a feminine occurs alongside male begetters in Matthew's genealogy, and that Joseph is named *anēr* ("husband/man").
    *   *Defender's Response & Close:* Defender maintained the link with [L1] Matthew 1:16, [L2] *egennēthē* (passive) and *ex hēs*, and [L3] Matthew 1:3, 5, 12, arguing that verses 3 and 5 use the active verb "begat" with a male subject, whereas verse 16 breaks the pattern by switching to the passive and naming Joseph "husband" rather than begetter.
*   **LINK D4:** "Son of Joseph" is a supposition and a legal or household title (Luke 3:23).
    *   *Status:* NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.
    *   *Defender's Own Words:* In R2, Defender stated: "I concede that Matthew 1:19 has no knowledge-verb." In R3, Defender stated: "NARROWED TO: 'son of Joseph' is reckoned by the speakers and by usage. The narrator marks it 'as was supposed', and Luke 2:49 corrects 'thy father'. I drop the clause that Joseph knew the child's origin before the angel spoke. Matthew 1:19 states no knowledge, as I conceded."
    *   *Defender's Close:* Retained the narrowed limb with [L1] Luke 3:23, [L2] *nomizō*, and [L3] Luke 2:44, Acts 14:19, Luke 2:49.
*   **LINK D5:** Isaiah 7:14 and Galatians 4:4 require a virgin conception and name only a woman as human source.
    *   *Status:* NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.
    *   *Defender's Own Words:* In R2, Defender stated: "I grant that Job 14:1 and 15:14 show the phrase 'born of a woman' as an idiom of mortality." In R3, Defender stated: "NARROWED TO: Isaiah 7:14 as quoted in Matthew 1:23 under Matthew 1:22 is fulfilled in Mary. Galatians 4:4 stays consistent with it but is not the exclusion. I drop the claim that Galatians 4:4 alone names the mother as sole human source." In R3 on Galatians 4:4, Defender added: "I drop the claim that the idiom excludes a father."
    *   *Defender's Close:* Retained the narrowed limb with [L1] Isaiah 7:14, [L2] *parthenos*, and [L3] Isaiah 7:11, Matthew 1:22-23.
*   **LINK D6:** Christ had no biological human father; Joseph was legal father only.
    *   *Status:* NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.
    *   *Defender's Own Words:* In R3, Defender stated: "NARROWED TO: the throne-seed was promised through David, but the curse in Jeremiah 22:30 means Joseph's line through Jechonias is not a throne-seed by Joseph's begetting. The rows do not state that Mary's line runs by Nathan, so I drop that limb. I concede no row gives Mary a father named Heli or the line of Nathan." On Ezra 2:62, Defender added: "I concede it shows registers counted by fathers' houses."
    *   *Defender's Close:* Retained the narrowed keystone with [L1] Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35, [L2] *gennaō*, *ek*, [L3] Hebrews 10:5, and the Jeremiah 22:30 / Matthew 1:12 bar.

---

#### Challenger's Declared Chain (C1–C6)

*   **LINK C1:** Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.
    *   *Status:* CITED-WITH-FOOTING.
    *   *Defender's Press:* Defender pressed with Matthew 1:18, 20, 25, arguing that *synerchomai* denotes conjugal union, that the pregnancy was found before union, and that Joseph "knew her not till" the birth.
    *   *Challenger's Response & Close:* Challenger maintained the link with [L1] Matthew 1:19-20, 2 Samuel 7:12, Acts 2:30, [L2] *anēr*, *gynē*, *zera'*, *osphys*, and [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24, Genesis 4:1, arguing that the seed proceeds out of a man's bowels/loins, betrothal is marriage in law, and *heōs* bounds abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking.
*   **LINK C2:** The not-knowing runs from the taking to the birth.
    *   *Status:* CITED-WITH-FOOTING.
    *   *Defender's Press:* Defender pressed with Matthew 1:18, 25, arguing that verse 25 bounds not-knowing at the birth rather than starting at the taking, and verse 18 places the pregnancy before coming together.
    *   *Challenger's Response & Close:* Challenger maintained the link with [L1] Matthew 1:24-25, [L2] *heōs*, *paralambanō*, and [L3] Deuteronomy 20:7, Matthew 1:18, 25, arguing the sequence of events is finding (1:18), taking (1:24), and abstinence during pregnancy until birth (1:25).
*   **LINK C3:** The covenant sonship rides on a seed out of a man's body.
    *   *Status:* CITED-WITH-FOOTING.
    *   *Defender's Press:* Defender pressed with Luke 1:35 and 1 Chronicles 28:6, arguing that Solomon's sonship rested on divine choosing, whereas Luke 1:35 uses *dio* ("therefore") to ground the title in the Holy Ghost's overshadowing.
    *   *Challenger's Response & Close:* Challenger maintained the link with [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12, 14, 1 Chronicles 28:6, [L2] *zera'*, *dio*, *kaleō*, and [L3] Psalm 132:11, Luke 1:32, Acts 1:8, arguing that 2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6 show covenant sonship applied to the seed of a man's loins, and Luke 1:35 connects to verse 32.
*   **LINK C4:** Seed according to the flesh travels by the fathers.
    *   *Status:* CITED-WITH-FOOTING.
    *   *Defender's Press:* Defender pressed with Romans 1:3, Galatians 4:4, and Matthew 1:3, 5, arguing that Romans 1:3 uses *ginomai* ("made"), Galatians 4:4 names only a woman, and Matthew includes mothers alongside fathers.
    *   *Challenger's Response & Close:* Challenger maintained the link with [L1] Romans 1:3, Numbers 1:18, [L2] *sperma*, *osphys*, *bayith*, and [L3] Hebrews 7:5, 10, Ezra 2:61-62, Luke 1:27, 2:4, arguing that pedigree is reckoned by the father's house, seed passes through fathers' loins, and Joseph's house is Davidic.
*   **LINK C5:** The sentence on Coniah and the throne line.
    *   *Status:* NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE.
    *   *Challenger's Own Words:* In R3, Challenger stated: "LINK 5: NARROWED TO: the LORD who pronounced the sentence on Coniah took the signet from him and set it on Coniah's seed by name, and the same Lord God gives the throne. I drop the reading that Haggai 2:23 itself names the throne." In R3 under Haggai 2:23: "Under the narrowing, I read it for the signet and the choosing, 'for I have chosen thee,' which is what it states."
    *   *Challenger's Close:* Retained the narrowed limb with [L1] Jeremiah 22:24, Haggai 2:23, [L2] *kisse'*, *thronos*, and [L3] Matthew 1:12, Jeremiah 18:8, Luke 1:32.
*   **LINK C6:** Matthew 1:16 leaves the begetting quiet, and the man stands beside the mother.
    *   *Status:* CITED-WITH-FOOTING.
    *   *Defender's Press:* Defender pressed with Matthew 1:5, 16, Luke 3:23, and Luke 2:49, arguing that Matthew breaks the active "begat" pattern at verse 16, and Luke 3:23 marks "son of Joseph" as supposed.
    *   *Challenger's Response & Close:* Challenger maintained the link with [L1] Matthew 1:16, [L2] *anēr*, *gennaō* (passive), *nomizō*, and [L3] Luke 2:27, 33, 41, 48, John 1:45, 6:42, Matthew 1:21, 25, arguing that the passive verb does not narrate the begetting, Joseph is addressed as husband, he performs the paternal naming act, and four biblical registers call him father or parent.

---

### 3. Drift Guard Violations by the Challenger

*   **Violations Checked:**
    *   *DG-8 (Biological Father / Seed chain / Mary had a baby without a man):* Challenger consistently asserted that Joseph was the biological father, arguing that a man was involved, that seed must proceed out of David's loins through a father's loins, and that Joseph knew Mary within the espousal. No violation of DG-8 occurred.
    *   *DG-18 (Son of God = Davidic Covenant Title — NOT Biological Divine Paternity):* Challenger maintained that "Son of God" in Luke 1:35 is a covenant title tracing back to 2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6, not divine biological paternity. No violation occurred.
    *   *DG-56 (Genealogy Construct):* Challenger did not construct or introduce unstated legal-adoption or Levirate mechanisms to reconcile divergent genealogies, noting the textual tension while pointing to Matthew 1:12 and Luke 3:27 without unauthorized bridges.
    *   *DG-60 (Seed, not blood):* Challenger argued lineage in the text's own word "seed" (*zera'*, *sperma*) and "loins" (*osphys*), avoiding "blood" as an identity verdict.
    *   *DG-61 (Chain proof / No single verse demand):* Challenger built and maintained a multi-link chain under Isaiah 28:10 without issuing a single-verse demand to the Defender.
*   **Findings:** The Challenger committed **zero (0)** drift guard violations across all rounds.

---

### 4. Method and Engagement

Both combatants adhered strictly to the Isaiah 28:10 chain-scoped engagement format:
*   Neither side deployed placeholder evasions or vacuous dismissals (e.g., "Noted. Not conceding here. Goes to review."). Every counter-press received textual engagement citing [L1] scripture, [L2] lexical data, [L3] cross-references, and [L4] chained inferences.
*   **Defender's Engagement:** Defender opened with a traditional reading rooted in Matthew 1:18-25 and Luke 1:34-35. When pressed, Defender demonstrated method discipline by conceding unsupported inferences (specifically regarding Matthew 1:19's lack of a knowledge-verb, the inability of Galatians 4:4 alone to exclude a father, and the absence of textual evidence naming Heli or Nathan as Mary's direct line) and formally narrowing Links D4, D5, and D6. Defender engaged the Challenger's citations directly with counter-readings of *synerchomai*, *heōs*, and Jeremiah 22:30.
*   **Challenger's Engagement:** Challenger operated strictly on the chain of Davidic seed rows (2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30; Romans 1:3; Hebrews 7:14). Challenger met the Defender's textual anchors by analyzing grammatical aspects (such as the present tense of *ginōskō* in Luke 1:34 and the syntactic role of *heōs* in Matthew 1:25) and comparing usages of *ek theou* and *nomizō*. When pressed on Haggai 2:23 lacking the explicit word "throne," Challenger formally narrowed Link C5 rather than asserting an ungrounded inference.

---

### 5. Most Vulnerable Points

#### Defender's Most Vulnerable Ground
The Defender's chain is most vulnerable where it addresses the Davidic seed requirements:
1.  **The Seed and Loins Texts:** Texts such as 2 Samuel 7:12 ("proceed out of thy bowels"), Psalm 132:11 ("Of the fruit of thy body"), Acts 2:30 ("of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh"), and Romans 1:3 ("made of the seed of David according to the flesh"). Defender argues that "fruit of his loins" spans generations and that the descent reaches Christ through Mary without Joseph. However, Defender conceded in R3 Link 6: "The rows do not state that Mary's line runs by Nathan, so I drop that limb. I concede no row gives Mary a father named Heli or the line of Nathan." With that limb dropped, Defender's chain exhibits no textual register tracing Mary's bodily descent from David, while the texts explicitly state that Joseph was "of the house of David" (Luke 1:27) and "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).
2.  **The Coniah Bar vs. Luke 3:** Defender pressed Jeremiah 22:30 ("no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David") against Joseph's line in Matthew 1:12 ("Jechonias begat Salathiel"). When Challenger showed that Luke 3:27 contains the identical descendants ("Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri"), Defender's attempt to route around Jechonias via Luke's genealogy while simultaneously dropping Mary's connection to Luke 3 left the Davidic physical lineage unanchored in an explicit biblical register.

#### Challenger's Most Vulnerable Ground
The Challenger's chain is most vulnerable where it addresses the chronological statements of the conception in Matthew 1:
1.  **Matthew 1:18's Timing Clause:** Matthew 1:18 explicitly states: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Challenger's premise that "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal" requires *synerchomai* ("before they came together") to refer strictly to the formal cohabitation/taking of Matthew 1:24, and "found with child" to denote only the public discovery after an espousal union. Defender countered that *synerchomai* lexically encompasses conjugal cohabitation and that Matthew 1:25's statement—Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"—places the abstinence across the entire period up to the birth, leaving no explicit narrative verse recording a conjugal knowing between espousal and birth.
2.  **The Genealogy Pattern Break in Matthew 1:16:** Matthew 1:1-15 maintains an unbroken formula of thirty-nine active male verbs: "[male X] begat [male Y]." At verse 16, the text abruptly shifts syntax: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." Challenger reads the passive *egennēthē* ("was born") as non-narration that leaves the begetting quiet while keeping Joseph as the husband beside the mother. Defender's press that the grammatical shift to the feminine relative pronoun *ex hēs* ("out of whom") and the passive verb deliberately avoids stating "Joseph begat Jesus" remains an unresolved textual tension on the face of the record.

There *osphys* (G3751) means "the loin ... internally (by extension) procreative power."

  1. The promised seed comes out of a man's loins (Acts 2:30, *osphys*).
  2. The canon's stated means is a husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1).
  3. Matthew names Joseph and Mary husband and wife in law from the espousal (Matthew 1:19-20, *anēr*, *gynē*; Deuteronomy 22:24).

**Answers to the pressed witnesses:**

# CLOSE ROUND (defender)

## Defense of the declared chain

**D1: KEPT.** The conception is "of the Holy Ghost" before Mary and Joseph "came together."
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father...)". The margin's "begotten" puts the begetting verb on the Holy Ghost. *synerchomai* (G4905) means "to cohabit (conjugally)", and it stands in Matthew 1:18.
- [L3] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." *lathra* (G2977) means "privately."
- [L4] The chain has three steps.
  1. Matthew 1:18 gives the manner of the birth ("on this wise") as the Holy Ghost, before cohabiting.
  2. Matthew 1:20 uses the procreation verb with the Holy Ghost as the source.
  3. Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph reasoning as a man who knows the child is not his: he means to put her away privately.
  - The Holy Ghost is named as begetter, and no man is.

**D2: KEPT.** Mary "know[s] not a man," and the angel answers with the Holy Ghost, not a man.
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982) means "to overshadow." *dio* (G1352) means "therefore." In Luke 1:35 *dio* sits inside the same sentence as the coming upon and the overshadowing.
- [L3] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
- [L4] The question is "How?". The answer is the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and verse 37 rests it on God. The "therefore" in verse 35 ties the title to the overshadowing that comes before it in the same sentence. An answer that said Joseph would know her would answer "How?" with a man, and the text answers with God.

**D3: KEPT.** Matthew 1:16 ends the line with Joseph as husband, not begetter.
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L2] *egennēsen* (active, "begat") runs the line. At the last link the verb is *egennēthē* (passive, "was born") and the relative is feminine, *ex hēs* ("out of whom").
- [L3] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." Matthew 1:3 and 1:5 keep the active "begat" for each father.
- [L4] Every link before the last has the father as subject of "begat." The last link alone changes to the passive and the feminine, and it names Joseph "husband" (*anēr*, "man, husband"). A change at the one place where the text says "of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20) is the evidence.

**D4: KEPT.** "Son of Joseph" is a supposition or a household title.
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] *nomizō* (G3543) means "to deem, suppose."
- [L3] Luke 2:44: "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey." Acts 14:19: "having stoned Paul, drew [him] out of the city, supposing he had been dead."
- [L4] In Luke 2:44 and Acts 14:19 the supposition was false: he was not in the company, and Paul was not dead. In Luke 3:23 the narrator marks the same verb with "as was supposed" before "the son of Joseph." That is the way he tags a belief held by others.

**D5: KEPT.** Isaiah 7:14 and Galatians 4:4 name a virgin and a woman as the only human source.
- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."
- [L2] *ʿalmāh* (H5959) means "young woman, maiden." *gynē* (G1135) means "woman."
- [L3] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." Isaiah 7:11: "Ask thee a sign of the LORD thy God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above."
- [L4] The sign is offered "in the depth, or in the height above," so it must be beyond the ordinary. Matthew 1:22-23 says the Holy Ghost conception fulfils it.

**D6: KEPT.** The conclusion is that Christ had no biological human father.
- [L1] Matthew 1:20; Luke 1:35.
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate, properly of the father." *ek* (G1537) means "out of."
- [L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
- [L4] The begetter is named as the Holy Ghost (D1), the answer to "How?" is God's power (D2), and the genealogy's verb changes at Joseph (D3). The sonship name is explained by "therefore" (D2) and the body by "prepared" (Hebrews 10:5). Joseph is husband and legal father only.

---

## Answers to the challenger's link round

### C1 (Joseph knew Mary within the espousal)

ANSWER: Matthew 1:18 -- D1 -- "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *synerchomai* (G4905) means "cohabit." The verse says the manner of the birth ("on this wise") is a pregnancy found before cohabiting and "of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband... was minded to put her away privily."
- [L4] Joseph's plan to put her away is the response of a man who had not known her. It does not fit the challenger's claim that he had, so the verse fits D1.

ANSWER: Matthew 1:20 -- D1 -- "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate, properly of the father." The "for" gives the Holy Ghost's begetting as the ground of "fear not."
- [L3] Matthew 1:19 shows the fear, namely Joseph's wish to put her away. The challenger's reading of "of the Holy Ghost" as "of God" in the sense of 1 John 5:1 ("is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him") has God as the begetter. It then has Joseph as a second begetter. The text names one.
- That the pair are "husband" and "wife" from the espousal is granted. Deuteronomy 20:7, "betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her," shows that a betrothed wife is not yet taken, and so not yet known.

ANSWER: Matthew 1:25 -- D2 -- "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
- [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097) means "know." *heōs* (G2193) means "until."
- [L3] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."

- [L4] The challenger places the knowing before the taking. Matthew 1:20 already calls what is in her "of the Holy Ghost." Verse 25 has the whole span covered, up to the birth.

ANSWER: Luke 1:34 -- D2 -- "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097) means "know."
- [L3] Luke 1:35, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee," is the answer given to this question. The challenger grants the present tense. The answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and Luke 1:37 adds "with God nothing shall be impossible."

### C2 (the not-knowing runs from the taking to the birth)

ANSWER: Matthew 1:24 -- D1 -- "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:"

# ROUND 4: CLOSE (challenger)

## The record's reading of the topic

Christ had a biological father, Joseph, "thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20), named as father by his mother, by the narrator, by the town, and by a disciple. The promise to David required a seed out of a man's body. The text names one man beside Mary, her husband from the espousal. Line upon line, the chain below carries that conclusion and no further.

---

## C1: KEPT. Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

- **[L2] Luke 1:34 is a present state.** In Luke 1:34, "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?", the verb *ginōskō* (G1097) is present tense. It states her state when the angel spoke, and it is not a vow.
- **[L2] Matthew 1:19 states intent and its grounds.** "Being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." *lathra* (G2977) means "privately." The verse gives his intent and two grounds. It carries no verb of knowing.

## C3: KEPT. The covenant sonship rides on a seed out of a man's body.

- **[L1] The title is given to a son a man begat.** 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
  - In one verse stand David's son and God's covenant title for him.
- **[L3] The title's source.** 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- **[L3] Luke gives the title and the throne before Mary's question.** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- **[L2] The "therefore" of Luke 1:35.** The *dio kai* ("therefore") in verse 35 connects back to verse 32, not forward to biological divine paternity.
  - The verb is "shall be called" (*kaleō*, G2564), the same naming verb as Luke 1:32's "shall be called."
  - "Come upon" is *eperchomai* (G1904). It is said of the apostles in Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]." That is power given, and Luke 24:49 calls it being "endued with power from on high."
  - "Overshadow" is *episkiazō* (G1982). It is the cloud of Luke 9:34 ("there came a cloud, and overshadowed them") and Peter's shadow in Acts 5:15.

  - Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham." The loins pass father to son, from Abraham through Isaac and Jacob to Levi.

Hebrews 7:14 says "it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." Pedigree is declared by the fathers' house, and the house of David the rows name beside Mary is Joseph's. ## C6: KEPT. Matthew 1:16 leaves the begetting quiet, and the man stands beside the mother.

- **[L1] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

  - The mother: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48).
  - The narrator: "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27); "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover" (Luke 2:41); "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him" (Luke 2:33).

  - A disciple: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
- **[L3] The father names the child.**

  - He does it: "and he called his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:25).
  - Naming is the father's act, as with John: "thou shalt call his name John" (Luke 1:13); "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called" (Luke 1:62).
- **[L2] "As was supposed" carries no verdict of its own.** In Luke 3:23, "(as was supposed)," the verb is *nomizō* (G3543). That is the same verb of "where prayer was wont to be made" (Acts 16:13), a custom that held true. The word itself does not decide; its rows' contexts do. In Luke it stands beside Mary's own "thy father" (Luke 2:48).
- **[L3] "Made of a woman" is the mortality idiom.**
  - Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman, made under the law."

  - The same idiom is said of John, whose father is named: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist" (Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13).
- **[L4]** The passive verb in Matthew 1:16 does not narrate the begetting. Every register that names a parent beside Mary names Joseph, and Joseph does the father's act of naming. So the man stands beside the mother, and the seed is honored through the named line.

---

## Final words

The whole of Matthew 1:20 is kept together: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The angel greets the father by his Davidic house in the same breath in which he gives the covenant origin.

The rows hold together, precept upon precept:
- The seed proceeds "out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and is "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30).
- It is reckoned "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).
- It is "evident" in Juda (Hebrews 7:14).
- It is "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).
- The mother says "thy father and I" (Luke 2:48).
- The husband "knew her not till" the birth (Matthew 1:25).

Christ had a biological father: Joseph, of the house of David, who knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** The child born to Mary, Jesus, who is called Christ, had no human biological father. The KJV gives his conception as of the Holy Ghost, in a virgin who knew no man. Joseph is his supposed father and his father in law, but not his begetter. I define a biological father as a male who begets by natural generation. That is the sense the KJV's "begat" carries in Matthew 1:2-16.

## 1. The source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The phrase "of the Holy Ghost" is ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (*ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of holy spirit"). The preposition ἐκ (*ek*, "out of, from the source") names the origin. "Before they came together" is the aorist of συνέρχομαι (*synerchomai*, "to come together"). The conception is placed before any union of Joseph and Mary.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Here τὸ γεννηθέν (*to gennēthen*, "that which is begotten or conceived", from γεννάω *gennaō*) is the very verb the same chapter uses for begetting by fathers. Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac" uses ἐγέννησεν (*egennēsen*, "begat"). Where Matthew supplies a human begetter, he names the father. Where he gives the source of this child, he names ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The Greek διό (*dio*, "wherefore") makes the divine action the stated ground of his being called "the Son of God". The child is "born of thee" (ἐκ σοῦ, *ek sou*, "out of you"). Only Mary is named as the human source.

**[L4]** From Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 (the source marker *ek* with the Holy Ghost, set before any coming together), and from Luke 1:35 (*dio*, the divine overshadowing as the ground, and *ek sou* as the only human source), the conception has two sources named, God and Mary, and no male human source.

## 2. Mary was a virgin and knew no man

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." **[L2]** παρθένος (*parthenos*, "virgin").

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" **[L2]** ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω (*andra ou ginōskō*, "a man I do not know"). The present tense of γινώσκω (*ginōskō*, "to know", here of marital knowledge) states her present condition. Her question asks how a conception can come about with no man.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35 is the answer given: the Holy Ghost coming upon her. The answer supplies no man.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." **[L2]** Matthew again uses παρθένος (*parthenos*, "virgin") and cites it as fulfilment of Isaiah 7:14.

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." **[L2]** The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" is הָעַלְמָה (*ha-ʿalmah*, H5959, "the virgin"). The Hebrew behind "a sign" is אוֹת (*ʾot*, "a sign").

**[L3]** Matthew 1:22: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet." This binds Isaiah's "virgin" to Mary's conception.

**[L3]** Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water". The same Hebrew word (H5959, *ʿalmah*) is rendered "virgin" in the KJV there.

**[L4]** From Isaiah 7:14 (*ʾot*, a sign given by the Lord himself) and Matthew 1:22-23 (this event declared the fulfilment), a conception through an ordinary husband would be no sign. The sign is a virgin conceiving.

## 3. Matthew's genealogy withholds the word "begat" at the last link

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Through Matthew 1:2-16 the verb is ἐγέννησεν (*egennēsen*, "begat") with a male subject. At 1:16 the pattern changes. The verb becomes the passive ἐγεννήθη (*egennēthē*, "was born"), and the relative is ἐξ ἧς (*ex hēs*, "out of whom"), feminine singular. Only Mary is the source. Joseph is called ἄνδρα (*andra*, "husband, man") of Mary, not the one who begat.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20 and 1:23 give the reason for the change. The conception is of the Holy Ghost, and the sign is a virgin.

**[L4]** From Matthew 1:16 (the break from "begat" to "of whom was born", with the feminine relative) and from Matthew 1:18-20 (the reason given), the genealogy deliberately declines to call Joseph the begetter of Jesus.

## 4. Joseph's fatherhood is supposed and legal, not biological

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." **[L2]** ἐνομίζετο (*enomizeto*, "was supposed, was reckoned"). The word marks a popular opinion, not a fact.

**[L3]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is what the crowd says. Luke 3:23 labels such talk "as was supposed".

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." **[L3]** Luke 2:49 gives the reply: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" In Luke 2:48 Mary uses the household's designation. In 2:49 the child names a different father, and the contrast stands in two verses of one scene.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." **[L2]** δίκαιος (*dikaios*, "just, righteous"); ἀπολῦσαι (*apolysai*, "to put away"); λάθρᾳ (*lathra*, "secretly").

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20 resolves it: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L4]** From Matthew 1:19 (Joseph, a just man, resolved to put Mary away) and 1:20 (the angel's answer is the Holy Ghost as source), Joseph knew the child was not his. A man who knew himself the father would have had no cause for the intended divorce.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:24-25: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." **[L2]** ἐπάλεσεν... καλέω (*kaleō*, "to call, to name"). Joseph's part is to take Mary and to name the child. He does not beget him.

## 5. The Holy Ghost is not a biological father

**[L1]** Luke 24:39: "a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have." **[L2]** πνεῦμα (*pneuma*, "spirit").

**[L3]** John 4:24: "God is a Spirit." Luke 1:35 describes the Holy Ghost "coming upon" and the power "overshadowing", which is the language of divine action, not of natural begetting.

**[L4]** From Luke 24:39 (a spirit has no flesh and bones) and John 4:24 (God is a Spirit), the divine source named in Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 acts as the Creator who causes the conception. It is not a male parent in the biological sense. So the question "biological father?" has no human answer in the record.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. The conception of Mary's child is stated to be ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (*ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of holy spirit"), with a human source only in Mary. [L1] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20; [L2] *ek*, "out of", and *gennēthen*, "begotten"; [L3] Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee".
2. Mary was a virgin who knew no man at the time of conception, and Isaiah's sign is a virgin conceiving. [L1] Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man"; [L2] *parthenos* (virgin) in Luke 1:27 and Matthew 1:23, and *ʿalmah* in Isaiah 7:14; [L3] Matthew 1:22-23 and Genesis 24:43.
3. Matthew's genealogy withholds "begat" at the last link, which shows Joseph was not the begetter. [L1] Matthew 1:16 "of whom was born Jesus"; [L2] *egennēsen* (begat) in the earlier verses against *ex hēs* (out of whom, feminine singular) at 1:16; [L3] Matthew 1:20.
4. Joseph is Mary's husband and the child's supposed and legal father, not his begetter, and Joseph knew it. [L1] Luke 3:23 "as was supposed"; [L2] *enomizeto*, "was supposed"; [L3] Luke 2:48-49, Matthew 1:19-20, 1:24-25 and John 6:42.
5. The Holy Ghost, a spirit without flesh and bones, is the source of the conception by divine power, not a biological father. [L1] Luke 24:39 "a spirit hath not flesh and bones"; [L2] *pneuma*, spirit; [L3] John 4:24, Luke 1:35.
6. Christ had no biological father.

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# CHALLENGER, ROUND 1: Christ had a father of the flesh, Joseph, of the house of David

**Position.** The KJV names one man as the child's father: Joseph, "of the house and lineage of David." It requires a seed "according to the flesh" that came "out of the loins" of David. It reckons Jesus "of Juda" by the house of the fathers. "Of the Holy Ghost" marks where the child comes from in the covenant. It does not name a begetter of flesh. I hold every row the defender quoted, as written, and show how each fits.

---

## C1. The promise requires seed out of a man's body, according to the flesh

**[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
**[L2]** In Romans 1:3, *spermatos* (G4690, "seed, offspring") is joined to *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh"). In Acts 2:30, *osphys* (G3751, "loin, procreative power") is the same word used in Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." The loins in these rows are a father's loins.
**[L3]** Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." The margin reads "body: Heb. belly." Hebrews 2:14 says "he also himself likewise took part of the same," that is, of flesh and blood. Hebrews 2:16 carries the margin "Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold."
**[L4]** These rows set Christ's flesh as seed out of David's bowels and loins (2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30), and the loins-word belongs to the father (Hebrews 7:10, *osphys*). Romans 1:3 gives *spermatos ... kata sarka*. So the flesh came down a line of fathers. The line the text names reaches "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).

## C2. Jesus is reckoned "of Juda" by the house of the fathers

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
**[L3]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
**[L2]** "By the house of their fathers" is *bayith* (H1004, "house, family") with *'ab* (H1, "father").
**[L3]** Ezra 2:62 shows what happened to men reckoned through a wife's house. Those "called after their name" (Ezra 2:61, the house of Barzillai's daughters) "sought their register ... but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
**[L4]** Hebrews 7:14 calls Jesus' descent from Juda "evident" (*prodēlon*, "plain beforehand"). The law reckons pedigree by the father's house (Numbers 1:18, *bayith* and *'ab*). The text gives the house of one man: "Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27) and "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). So Jesus' descent from Juda is evident through Joseph.

## C3. The father is named by Mary, the narrator, the town and a disciple

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." This is Mary speaking.
**[L3]** Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year." This is the narrator. Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled." John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." This is Philip, a disciple.
**[L2]** In Luke 2:41 the word is *goneis* (G1118, "parents, those who beget"), from the root of *ginomai* ("to become, be born").
**[L4]** In Luke 2:48 Mary, the one the angel spoke to, calls Joseph *ho patēr sou* ("thy father"). The narrator calls the two of them *goneis* ("parents"). The father is named by the witness closest to the conception.

---

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES (the defender's chain, link by link)

The defender's links each take as given a fact that the rows they quote do not supply. The witnesses below carry the layers.

**1. LINK D1.** Defender's words: "with a human source only in Mary."
ASSUMES: the Davidic flesh of Romans 1:3 came to the child through Mary's house.
ROWS GIVE: Luke 1:27, "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David"; Luke 2:4, "he was of the house and lineage of David"; Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth"; Luke 1:5, "his wife was of the daughters of Aaron."
PRESSED WITH: Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30; Hebrews 7:10.
- **[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- **[L2]** *sperma* (G4690, "seed") and *osphys* (G3751, "loins," in Acts 2:30 and Hebrews 7:10, "in the loins of his father").
- **[L4]** The flesh-seed comes from a father's loins. The house of David is given to Joseph, while Mary's cousin is "of the daughters of Aaron." So the defender's "only in Mary" routes David's seed through a house the rows give to the husband.
- **On "born of thee" (ek sou, "out of thee," Luke 1:35):** Matthew uses *ek* ("out of") for the mother alongside a named father. Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." Matthew 1:5: "Booz begat Obed of Ruth." *Ek* with the mother is the genealogy's own marker for the mother. It fits a father who begat.

**2. LINK D2.** Defender's words: "a conception through an ordinary husband would be no sign."
ASSUMES: a child conceived through a husband falls outside Isaiah's sign.
ROWS GIVE: Isaiah 8:3, "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son" (margin: "went: Heb. approached"); Isaiah 8:18, "Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel."
PRESSED WITH: Isaiah 7:16; Isaiah 8:4; Isaiah 8:8.
- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:16: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- **[L3]** Isaiah 8:4: "before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother." Isaiah 8:8: "the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel."
- **[L2]** *'ot* (H226, "sign") is the word of Isaiah 7:14. It returns in the plural in Isaiah 8:18, of children the prophet fathered.
- **[L4]** Isaiah 7:16 dates the sign to the two kings of Ahaz's day. Isaiah 8:3-4 gives the sign-child's conception after "I went unto the prophetess," and 8:4 gives that child a "father." Isaiah 8:18 names the prophet's own children as signs. So in Isaiah's own chapters, a sign-child comes through a husband.
- **How Matthew 1:22 fits:** Matthew applies the row the same way he applies Hosea 11:1 at Matthew 2:15: "Out of Egypt have I called my son." That row was first spoken of Israel: "When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt" (Hosea 11:1). Fulfilment in Matthew fills a row whose first subject stood in its own day. Matthew and Isaiah stand together.

   - The promise in Acts 2:30 specifies:

   - Defender grants that *osphys* is "procreative power" and that Hebrews 7:10 applies it to a father ("in the loins of his father").
