## THE UNNAMED PRESSES

**ANSWER: 1 Chronicles 3:17 -- D3 --** "And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son,"
- **[L1]** This verse gives Salathiel as Jeconiah's son. It does not say who begat Jesus.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:12 carries that line forward: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." Matthew 1:16 then closes it: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** In Matthew 1:16 the pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular. The verb is *egennēthē* ("was born"), not "begat."
- **[L4]** In Matthew 1:2, 1:3 and 1:12 the line runs "begat ... begat ... begat." At Matthew 1:16 the verb changes and the relative pronoun becomes feminine. Jacob begat Joseph, "the husband of Mary," and Jesus was born "of whom" (Mary). Two layers of text stand under this: the verb change and the feminine pronoun. First Chronicles 3:17 proves that Jeconiah's line continued. It supplies no row where Joseph "begat" Jesus. D3 stands.

**ANSWER: Exodus 2:1 -- D3 --** "And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took [to wife] a daughter of Levi."
- **[L1]** The verse names the taking of a wife.
- **[L2]** The Hebrew behind "took" is *laqach* ("to take"). It names an act of marriage, not a begetting.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:24 uses the same shape of act: Joseph "took unto him his wife." Matthew 1:25 then puts the knowing after the bearing: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L4]** In both verses "took to wife" is one act, and begetting is another. Matthew 1:24-25 separates them in Joseph's own case. Exodus 2:1 does not overturn D3.

**ANSWER: Esther 2:15 -- D3 --** "Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king,"
- **[L1]** The verse keeps her natural father's name, "the daughter of Abihail," and states Mordecai's relation by the word "taken."
- **[L3]** Esther 2:7: "whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter."
- **[L3]** Genesis 48:5 gives the same kind of legal sonship: "Ephraim and Manasseh ... [are] mine."
- **[L3]** Exodus 2:10: "he became her son. And she called his name Moses."
- **[L4]** Scripture marks a son by taking where it means one, and it keeps the natural father's name where it knows him. Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's place in the other way: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." Here *enomizeto* ("was reckoned") states the reckoning of the people. Esther 2:15 shows that sonship can be named without begetting. D3 stands.

---

## THE CHALLENGER'S LINK-ROUND WITNESSES

### C1 (the signet)

**ANSWER: Jeremiah 22:30 -- D3 and D5 --** "for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
- **[L1]** The bar is on "his seed."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:12 and 1:16 place Joseph in the line of Jechonias.
- **[L4]** A son begotten of Joseph would be of that seed. The text that declares the bar places Joseph in that line. A son "of whom" Mary, "begotten of the Holy Ghost," is not Joseph's seed. This fits D1, D3 and D5.
- Haggai 2:23 and Jeremiah 18:8 only lift a bar. A bar lifted is not a begetting stated.

**ANSWER: Haggai 2:23 -- D3 --** "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the LORD of hosts."
- **[L1]** The words are said of Zerubbabel.
- **[L2]** *Bachar* ("to choose") is a verb of choosing.
- **[L4]** Zerubbabel is made "as a signet," and no throne is given. The challenger's own link claims "the lifting of the plucking, not a throne-sitting." That lifting states nothing about who begat Jesus. This leaves D3 unmoved.

**ANSWER: Jeremiah 18:8 -- D3 --** "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them."
- **[L1]** The repenting here is conditioned: "If ... turn from their evil."
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 22:30 is the pronouncement. Haggai 2:23 does not mention Coniah's turning.
- **[L4]** Even if the bar were lifted, the lifting would make a begetting by Joseph possible. It would not say that Joseph begat Jesus. D1 through D4 rest on rows that state the conception.

**ANSWER: Acts 2:30 -- D4 --** "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;"
- **[L1]** The loins are David's.
- **[L3]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."
- **[L2]** *Ginomai* ("to be made") is the one verb in both verses.
- **[L4]** The flesh is David's through "a woman," so the seed of David came by the woman. Acts 2:30 names David's loins and does not name Joseph's. D4 stands.

### C2 (Luke 1:32 and 1:35)

**ANSWER: Luke 1:35 -- D1 --** "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

- **[L4]** The answer to "seeing I know not a man" names God's act and no husband. D1 stands.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:34 -- D2 --** "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L1]** The question is asked in view of Luke 1:27: "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." She was already espoused to a man, and still asks how.

- **[L4]** If conception through her espoused husband were meant, there would be no "how." Her words show that the conception promised was not by him. D2 stands.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:20 -- D1 --** "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [conceived: Gr. begotten]

### C6 (naming)

**ANSWER: Luke 1:13 and 1:62-63 with Matthew 1:21 -- D3 --** "thou shalt call his name John" and "thou shalt call his name JESUS."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:25 says "he called his name JESUS."

- **[L4]** Naming is done by mother, father and adopter alike. It does not mark the begetter. The narrowed link adds nothing to D3's opposition.

### Witnesses of the people

**ANSWER: John 6:42 and Luke 4:22 -- D3 --** "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" And "Is not this Joseph's son?"

- **[L3]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L2]** *Enomizeto* ("was reckoned") marks what was supposed.

**ANSWER: Luke 2:48-49 -- D3 --** "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." And "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

- **[L2]** *Patēr* ("father") is the same word in both verses.
- **[L4]** The child's reply sets the other Father over the business. Mary's phrase is the parent's way of speaking. Luke 3:23 says "as was supposed." D3 stands.

---

## FINAL STATEMENT OF THE CHAIN

- **D1:** Matthew 1:20 says "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Luke 1:35 says "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee ... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Both name the Holy Ghost as source.

- **D4:** Galatians 4:4 says "made of a woman." Romans 1:3 says "of the seed of David according to the flesh." Hebrews 10:5 says "a body hast thou prepared me."
- **D5:** From these four, with Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 and Galatians 4:4, Christ had no biological father. The text names a mother, a husband "as was supposed," and the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception.

# ROUND 4 — CHALLENGER'S CLOSE

My position is the record's reading of the topic: **Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the man the text names, of the house of David.** The seed came out of a man's loins according to the flesh. "Of the Holy Ghost" marks where the child comes from in God's covenant. It does not name a begetter. I keep my links under their link-round numbers, C1 to C6. I press no new witness here.

---

## C1 — THE SEED IS DAVID'S BY THE LOINS, AND THE BAR ON CONIAH'S SEED WAS LIFTED: RESTATED

- **[L1]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." The promise names a body, loins, and flesh.
- **[L2]** *Osphys* (G3751) means "the loin ... internally (by extension) procreative power." *Sarx* (G4561) is flesh, "as the means of kindred." Both words stand in Acts 2:30.
- **[L3]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." *Me'eh* (H4578) is "of men, the seat of generation."
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 22:30: "for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David." The bar was spoken against a seed.
- **[L3]** Haggai 2:23: "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel ... and will make thee as a signet." Jeremiah 22:24 had said of Coniah, "yet would I pluck thee thence."
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 18:8 gives the LORD's own rule for a sentence he has pronounced: "I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them."
- **[L4]** The verses chain in order:
  - Acts 2:30 and 2 Samuel 7:12 require procreative seed out of a man's loins.
  - The signet plucked from Coniah in Jeremiah 22:24 is set again on his grandson in Haggai 2:23. 1 Chronicles 3:17 gives "Salathiel his son," and Matthew 1:12 gives "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel."
  - Jeremiah 18:8 is the LORD's stated rule for repenting of a pronounced evil.
  - So the line through Jechonias to Joseph is a live line for David's seed. It is not a closed one.
- C1 stands as declared.

## C2 — LUKE 1:32 AND 1:35: THE TITLE IS GIVEN WITH THE THRONE, AND THE VERBS ARE POWER AND PRESENCE: RESTATED

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title and the throne are given together, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** The *dio kai* ("therefore also") of verse 35 connects back to verse 32, where the title and the throne were already given. It does not point forward to a begetting of flesh by God.
- **[L2]** *Eperchomai* ("come upon") and *episkiazō* ("overshadow") are the verbs of verse 35.
- **[L3]** The same "come upon" is said of the apostles in Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." Luke 24:49 gives the same event: "until ye be endued with power from on high."
- **[L3]** The same "overshadow" is said of the cloud in Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." It is said of Peter in Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."
- **[L3]** The title has an earlier bearer. 1 Chronicles 28:6 says: "Solomon thy son ... for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." 2 Samuel 7:14 says: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- **[L3]** Psalms 2:7, "this day have I begotten thee," is applied in three places:
  - to the resurrection, Acts 13:33: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again";
  - to the priesthood, Hebrews 5:5: "Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest";
  - beside 2 Samuel 7:14, Hebrews 1:5: "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son."
- **[L4]** The chain:
  - Verse 35's verbs are the empowering and presence words of Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34 and Acts 5:15.
  - Its title is the covenant title already given at verse 32 with "the throne of his father David."
  - That title was carried by Solomon, whom David begat ("Solomon THY son ... MY son," 1 Chronicles 28:6).
  - So "called the Son of God" sits with a father of the flesh. It fits the named line, as Solomon's title did.
- C2 stands as declared.

## C3 — SOLOMON, "HER SEED," AND "MADE OF A WOMAN": RESTATED

- **[L1]** Genesis 4:25: "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel." Eve names Seth her seed. Adam's knowing stands in the same verse.
- **[L2]** *Zera'* (H2233) means "seed; figuratively ... posterity." It is the word of Genesis 3:15, "between thy seed and her seed," and of Genesis 4:25.
- **[L3]** "Born of a woman" is said of men whose fathers stand in the text:
  - Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble."
  - Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named in Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias ... thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- **[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." *Ginomai* (G1096) means "to become (come into being)."
- **[L4]** The chain:
  - The woman's seed (Genesis 4:25) stands with the husband's knowing.
  - "Born of a woman" (Job 14:1; Matthew 11:11) stands with a named father (Luke 1:13).
  - Galatians 4:4's "made of a woman" therefore names the mother as these rows do. It fits a father of the house of David, as Romans 1:3 requires: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- C3 stands as declared.

## C4 — THE HUSBAND'S KNOWING, WITHIN THE ESPOUSAL: RESTATED

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- **[L3]** The law calls the betrothed "his neighbour's wife" in Deuteronomy 22:24. Deuteronomy 20:7 names the later step: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- **[L3]** The canon's stated means of begetting is knowing. Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- **[L2]** In Luke 1:34, "seeing I know not a man," the verb *ginōskō* is present indicative. It states her state when the angel spoke. It is not a vow.
- **[L1]** Matthew sets three steps in order:
  - Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." This dates the finding.
  - Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." This is her coming into his house, the taking of Deuteronomy 20:7.
  - Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." This covers the pregnancy after the taking. The "till" bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy.
- **[L4]** The chain:
  - The seed rows of C1 require seed out of a man's loins.
  - Genesis 4:1 gives knowing as the means of begetting.
  - From the espousal Joseph is "her husband" and Mary is "thy wife" (Matthew 1:19-20; Deuteronomy 22:24).
  - So, at this inference layer, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.
  - The timing rows sit inside this chain. The finding (Matthew 1:18) comes before the taking (Matthew 1:24). The not-knowing of Matthew 1:25 runs from the taking to the birth.
- C4 stands as declared.

## C5 — "EVIDENT THAT OUR LORD SPRANG OUT OF JUDA," BY THE HOUSE OF THE FATHERS: RESTATED

- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
- **[L2]** The words of Hebrews 7:14:
  - *Prodēlos* (G4271) means "plain before all men, i.e. obvious."
  - *Anatellō* (G393) means "to (cause to) arise."
  - *Phylē* (G5443) means "an offshoot."
- **[L3]** The tribe is reckoned in Numbers 1:2, "by the house of their fathers," and in Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." *Yalad* (H3205) there means "specifically, to show lineage ... declare pedigrees." *Ab* (H1) means "father."
- **[L3]** The reverse case is Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed [or, pedigree]." Ezra 2:61-62 says of those "called after their name," the wife's house: "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:10 places the seed in the father: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." Luke 2:4 gives the house: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David."
- **[L4]** The chain:
  - A tribe made plain before all men (Hebrews 7:14) is plain by the reckoning the law gives: the house of the fathers (Numbers 1:2, 18).
  - That reckoning was refused to those counted by the wife's house (Ezra 2:61-62).
  - The one man of Judah's royal house the text names is Joseph (Luke 2:4).
  - So "evident ... out of Juda" fits the father's line.
- C5 stands as declared.

## C6 — NAMING: KEPT AS NARROWED

**NARROWED TO:** naming is the parents' act. In Luke 1 the naming is closed by the father's word, and Matthew gives the naming to Joseph as Luke gives it to Zacharias.

- **[L1]** Luke 1:62-63: "And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called. And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John." Luke 1:60 shows the mother spoke first: "Not [so]; but he shall be called John." The father's writing closed the matter.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "and he called his name JESUS."
- **[L4]** Joseph receives the father's charge, given to him as it was given to Zacharias (Luke 1:13, "thou shalt call his name John"), and he performs it. That fits the named father.

---

## THE WITNESSES OF THE FATHER, KEPT WHOLE

- **[L1]** Four voices name Joseph as father:
  - Mary herself: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48).
  - The narrator: "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27); "Joseph and his mother marvelled" (Luke 2:33); "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41).
  - The town: "Is not this Joseph's son?" (Luke 4:22); "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42).
  - A disciple: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
- **[L2]** In Luke 3:23, "(as was supposed)" is *enomizeto*, from *nomizō* (G3543), "properly, to do by law (usage)." It is the same form as Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." *Patēr* (G3962), "a father," is Mary's word in Luke 2:48.
- **[L4]** The word in Luke 3:23 is the custom word of Acts 16:13 and carries no verdict of its own. It stands beside Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48) and the narrator's "parents" (Luke 2:27, 41). So Luke's own pages name Joseph father in the narrator's voice and in Mary's.
- Matthew 1:16, "of whom was born Jesus," does not narrate the begetting. Matthew 1:3 shows the mother named with "of" beside a father who begat: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." The chorus above fills what that one verse leaves quiet. It is held whole, not set against the rest.

---

## FINAL WORDS

Precept upon precept, the text gives one chain:

1. The seed is David's, "which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12), "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30), "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).
2. The tribe is "evident" (Hebrews 7:14), reckoned "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).
3. The father is named by Mary, by the narrator, by the town and by a disciple (Luke 2:48; Luke 2:33; John 6:42; John 1:45).
4. The angel addresses him "Joseph, thou son of David," commands him to "take unto thee Mary thy wife," and grounds the command: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). That is the covenant origin of a son God claims, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14), and gives "the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32).
5. The Holy Ghost "come upon" and the Highest "overshadow" are the power of Acts 1:8 and the presence of Luke 9:34.
6. "Made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) is said as "born of women" is said of John, whose father is named (Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13).

So the record's reading stands at the inference layer, footed on these rows: **Christ had a biological father, Joseph, of the house and lineage of David (Luke 2:4). Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25).**

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost. Joseph was her husband and the child's guardian, but he was not the one who begat him. No man was his biological father. [L4, resting on the verses below]

## 1. Matthew's genealogy changes its verb at Joseph

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren". Every father in the line is named with the active verb "begat".

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] The verb behind both "begat" and "was born" is gennaō (G1080, to beget; in the passive, to be born). In Matthew 1:16 the active "begat" (egennēsen) stops at Joseph. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary", not the one who begat Jesus. The next verb is the passive egennēthē, "was born". The relative "of whom" is the Greek hēs (feminine singular, "of her"), so the birth is traced to Mary alone.

[L3] Matthew 1:2 shows the pattern the line follows until Joseph. In Matthew 1:16 the pattern is deliberately not continued.

[L4] Matthew keeps "A begat B" through the whole line and then, at Joseph, switches to the passive and a feminine relative. So he is denying that Joseph begat Jesus. This rests on the verb (L2) and the broken pattern (L1, L3).

## 2. The source of the conception is stated: the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] "Of" is ek (G1537, out of, from as source). "Of the Holy Ghost" is ek pneumatos hagiou, "out of the Holy Spirit". "That which is conceived" is gennēthen, the same root verb (G1080) that Matthew 1:2 uses for a father's begetting. Matthew 1:20 therefore gives as the source of the begetting the Holy Ghost, in the place where a human father would stand.

[L3] Matthew 1:18 says this was "before they came together". Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". In Matthew 1:25 "knew" is ginōskō (G1097), used here of marital relations, and "till" is heōs (G2193, until).

[L4] The conception was found before the couple came together (Matthew 1:18), and its stated source is the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:20, ek). Joseph's relations with Mary are placed after the birth (Matthew 1:25). Therefore Joseph is excluded as the begetter.

## 3. Mary and the angel, in Luke

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph". [L2] "Virgin" is parthenos (G3933, a virgin).

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L2] "Know" is ginōskō (G1097) and "man" is anēr (G435, a man, a husband).

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] "Overshadow" is episkiazō (G1982, to cast a shadow over). "Therefore" is dio (G1352, wherefore). The reason he is called the Son of God is the Holy Ghost's action upon Mary.

[L4] Mary asks how it can be, "seeing I know not a man" (Luke 1:34), and the angel answers with the Holy Ghost's coming and the power of the Highest (Luke 1:35). That answer names the means, and it is not a man. It rests on Luke 1:34 (L1) and the sense of episkiazō (L2).

## 4. Joseph's fatherhood is described as supposed

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] "Supposed" is enomizeto, from nomizō (G3543, to think, to deem by custom or opinion).

[L3] Pre-emptive answer on the passages that call Joseph "father". Luke 2:48 has Mary say, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". Luke 2:49 gives the reply: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" The child answers with a different Father, in the house where Mary had spoken of Joseph. John 6:42 reports what "they said": "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" That is the crowd's opinion, and it is the same "supposed" of Luke 3:23.

[L4] Luke 3:23 marks the "son of Joseph" label as opinion (L2, nomizō). Luke 2:49 gives the child's own different answer (L1, L3). So the "father" language is legal and household usage, and it does not state who begat him.

## 5. The prophecy and the body prepared

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." [L2] The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" is ha'almah (H5959, the maiden, rendered "virgin" in this verse).

[L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son". [L2] Matthew's word is parthenos (G3933, a virgin).

[L3] Hebrews 10:5: "but a body hast thou prepared me". [L2] "Body" is sōma (G4983, a body), and "prepared" is katartizō (G2675, to fit, to make ready).

[L4] Matthew 1:23 applies Isaiah 7:14 to the birth of Jesus (L1, L3). Hebrews 10:5 says the body was prepared (L2, L3), which fits the Holy Ghost's work in Luke 1:35 and not a man's begetting.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew breaks his "begat" line at Joseph: Matthew 1:2 and 1:16 [L1]; gennaō (G1080) in the active "begat" ending at Joseph, then the passive egennēthē with the feminine hēs ("of whom", of Mary) [L2]; so Joseph is not named as the begetter of Jesus.
2. The conceiving is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost": Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1]; ek (G1537, out of, as source) with gennēthen (G1080, conceived) [L2]; Matthew 1:25 puts "knew her not" until the birth [L3].
3. Mary and the angel put no man as the cause: Luke 1:34 and 1:35 [L1]; ginōskō (G1097) and episkiazō (G1982, to overshadow) [L2]; Luke 1:27 "a virgin" [L3].
4. The "son of Joseph" and "father" language is opinion or household usage: Luke 3:23 "as was supposed" [L1]; nomizō (G3543, to deem) [L2]; Luke 2:48-49 and John 6:42 [L3].
5. Prophecy and the prepared body fit a virgin conception: Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23 [L1]; ha'almah (H5959) and parthenos (G3933) [L2]; Hebrews 10:5 "a body hast thou prepared me" [L3].
6. Christ had no human biological father: Matthew 1:16 and 1:20, and Luke 1:35 [L1]; gennaō (G1080) with ek (G1537) and episkiazō (G1982) [L2]; Luke 1:34 and Luke 3:23 [L3].

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# CHALLENGE: The seed of David came by the father's loins, and Joseph is the named father

**Position.** The child was "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). The text names the father who carried that seed: Joseph, "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). "Of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" name the child's covenant origin and title. They do not name the begetter of the flesh. [L4, footed below]

---

## PRESS ON D1: "of whom" is Matthew's mother-marker, and it stands beside begetting fathers

[L1] Matthew 1:3: "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar". This verse names a father and a mother together.

[L1] Matthew 1:5: "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth". This verse does the same twice.

[L1] Matthew 1:6: "David the king begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Urias". The pattern holds at David himself.

# ROUND 2: ANSWER TO THE PRESSES (revised)

I grant what the rows give. Joseph is "her husband" (Matthew 1:19) and the child's guardian. Luke 2:4 names Joseph as "of the house and lineage of David". "Seed of David" and "fruit of his loins" are said of Christ. The question is how that descent reaches him.

## D1: the verb and its object

[L1] Matthew 1:3: "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar". Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus".

[L2] I grant the challenger's point on ek (G1537, out of). It marks the mother at Matthew 1:3, 5 and 6, so the feminine relative in 1:16 does not by itself remove Joseph. Gennaō (G1080) is "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". The active "begat" is the father's verb.

[L3] Matthew 1:3, 5 and 6 always give the child as the object of "begat": Judas begat Phares, Booz begat Obed, David begat Solomon. Matthew 1:16 gives "begat" the object "Joseph". Jesus is not its object. He is the subject of the passive "was born", and the one the birth is "of" is Mary.

[L4] Matthew keeps the father's verb with the child as its object through every generation. At Jesus he drops it and gives the passive with Mary alone. This rests on Matthew 1:3, 5, 6 and 16 (L1, L3) and the father/mother senses of G1080 (L2).

**Naming does not mean begetting.**
- [L1] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS". Mary is also told to name him.
- [L3] Genesis 29:32: "Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben". Luke 1:60: "his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John". Isaiah 7:14, margin: "thou, O virgin, shalt call".
- [L4] Mothers name children, and so does a guardian who is told to. Joseph's naming in Matthew 1:21 and 1:25 therefore fits a guardian's act as well as a begetter's (L1, L3).

**"Son of David".** [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife". [L4] The verse states Joseph's own descent and gives it in the same sentence as the command to take Mary, with the reason that follows: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". The descent from David is said of Joseph. The conception is said to be of the Holy Ghost (L1). So the verse shows how the child entered David's house through the husband's taking of Mary (Matthew 1:24).

## D2: the angel's "for" and the timing rows

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". The margin reads "conceived: Gr. begotten".

[L2] The word is gennaō (G1080), the father's verb. The reason (gar, for) Joseph need not fear is that what is begotten in her is ek (G1537, out of) the Holy Ghost.

[L3] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband... was minded to put her away privily". The word is apolyō (G630, to dismiss or divorce). Matthew 1:20 says "while he thought on these things", with enthymeomai (G1760, to ponder).

[L4] Joseph's reaction was to put her away (L1, L3). A reason that quiets that fear is a begetter other than himself. If Joseph were the begetter, the "for" clause would give him nothing to answer his fear. Matthew 1:20's "for" stands on this ground (L1, L2).

**The birth verbs.**
- [L1] John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God".
- [L2] Gennaō in the figurative sense is "to regenerate" (G1080).
- [L3] John 3:6: "that which is born of the Spirit is spirit". 1 John 5:1: "is born of God".
- [L4] "Born of God" in John 1:13 is set against "of blood" and "the will of man". It is the second birth of believers, and each of them had a first birth by a father (L1, L2, L3). Matthew 1:20 puts God's source on the one conception, in her womb (L1). The challenger's rows compare two births in one person with one conception.

**Timing.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost".
- [L2] Synerchomai (G4905) in the lexicon includes "cohabit (conjugally)".
- [L3] Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". [L1] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived".
- [L4] Genesis 4:1 gives "knew... and she conceived" as one pair. Matthew 1:18 gives "before they came together... found with child of the Holy Ghost", and Matthew 1:25 gives "knew her not till she had brought forth". Her being found with child comes before the coming together, and the not-knowing runs to the birth. The conception is attributed to the Holy Ghost (L1, L2, L3).

## D3: Luke 1:35

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God".

[L2] I grant that eperchomai (G1904) and episkiazō (G1982) are used elsewhere of power and presence (Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34). Dio (G1352, wherefore) and the result clause tie "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" to those two verbs.

[L3] Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". Luke 1:35: "shall be born of thee". The angel to Zacharias says "bear thee a son", with the husband in the sentence. The angel to Mary says "of thee", with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest in the sentence.

[L4] The question was "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" (Luke 1:34, L1, with ginōskō G1097, know). The reply gives the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest as the cause of the birth "of thee" (L1, L2). That is the stated means. Elisabeth's sign (Luke 1:36) is a conception "in her old age" in one "who was called barren" (L1), and it answers age and barrenness. Mary's question was "seeing I know not a man", so her sign answers a different matter (L1).

**The throne.** [L1] Luke 1:32: "the throne of his father David". [L4] David is "father" here across the generations, so "father" in Luke 1:32 carries the forefather's sense, which my D6 answer below uses (L1, with Hebrews 7:10 at L3).

## D4: "supposed"

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".

[L2] The word is nomizō (G3543). I grant it can mean "wont", as in Acts 16:13.

[L3] Luke 2:44: "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey". Acts 14:19: "supposing he had been dead". The challenger cited Luke 2:44, and the supposing there proved mistaken. In Acts 14:19 it was also mistaken.

[L4] Luke's own uses of "supposing" in 2:44 and Acts 14:19 are of beliefs that turned out wrong (L1, L3). In Luke 3:23 the parenthesis stands at the one place where "son of Joseph" would otherwise be stated flat, so it carries the same sense.

**Luke 2:33.** [L1] Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled". The narrator names Joseph by name and attaches "his" to the mother. Luke 2:27 and 2:41 give "parents", which is goneus (G1118, parents of a household). Mary's "thy father" (2:48) is her address. The child answers in the same exchange with "my Father's business" (2:49), and so names a different Father (L1, L3).

**The covenant pattern.** [L3] 2 Samuel 7:14 says "I will be his father" of Solomon, who proceeded "out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12). Hebrews 1:5 puts the same words to Christ: "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?" [L4] The 2 Samuel row joins two fathers because Solomon had a human begetter. Hebrews 1:5 applies only the second half of that pairing, "I will be to him a Father", to Christ (L1, L3).

## D5: Hebrews 10:5

[L1] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me". The margin reads "or, thou hast fitted me".

[L2] Katartizō (G2675) is "to fit, make ready". Its subject is God.

[L3] Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same", meaning the flesh of the children.

[L4] I concede D5 is a fit only. Hebrews 10:5 gives God as the preparer of the body, and Hebrews 2:14 gives true flesh (L1, L3). Together they corroborate D1 to D3, and I rest nothing on D5 alone. Isaiah 7:14 stands on its own words: "a virgin shall conceive" (L1), applied in Matthew 1:23 as "a virgin shall be with child" (L3) with parthenos (G3933, a virgin) (L2). Isaiah 8:3 speaks of "the prophetess", and her child is named "Mahershalalhashbaz", a different child from Immanuel (L1, L3).

## D6: the seed, the loins, and Hebrews 7:14

**What "seed" and "loins" carry.**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:10: "he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him".
- [L3] Hebrews 7:9: "Levi... payed tithes in Abraham". The loins that carried Levi were Abraham's, his forefather's, three generations back.
- [L3] Genesis 35:11: "kings shall come out of thy loins". This is said to Jacob of a line of descendants.
- [L2] Osphys (G3751) is the loin. Sperma (G4690) is "seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring". Zera' (H2233) is seed.
- [L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed". The woman has "seed".
- [L4] "Loins of his father" in Hebrews 7:10 spans generations (L1, L3). "Seed" is a woman's offspring in Genesis 3:15 (L3) and "offspring" in G4690 (L2). Romans 1:3, Acts 2:30 and 2 Timothy 2:8 each state descent "of the seed of David", and a mother's seed fits those words as Genesis 3:15 shows. Romans 1:3 says "made" (ginomai, G1096, come into being) and not "begotten" (L1, L2).

### 1. What Held at L1–L2–L3 (Uncontested Floor)

The following points were quoted and maintained across all rounds without being charged or contested by either side:

- **Espousal and House:** In Luke 1:27, Mary was espoused to Joseph, a man "of the house of David," and is designated a "virgin" (*parthenos*, G3933). In Luke 2:4, Joseph went up to Bethlehem "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
- **Mary’s Kinship:** In Luke 1:36, Elisabeth is named Mary’s "cousin" (*syngenis*, G4773), and in Luke 1:5, Elisabeth was "of the daughters of Aaron."
- **Marital Status in Law:** In Matthew 1:19, Joseph is named "her husband"; in Matthew 1:20, the angel addresses Mary as "thy wife"; and in Deuteronomy 22:24, a betrothed woman is called "his neighbour's wife."
- **Naming Commands and Acts:** In Luke 1:31, Mary is told "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." In Matthew 1:21, Joseph is commanded "thou shalt call his name JESUS," and in Matthew 1:25, Joseph "called his name JESUS." In Luke 1:13, Zacharias is told "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John," and in Luke 1:62, "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called." In Genesis 29:32, Leah "bare a son, and she called his name Reuben."
- **Mary’s State at the Annunciation:** In Luke 1:34, Mary asks, "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" where "know" is present indicative (*ou ginōskō*, G1097).
- **Narrator and Parental Vocabulary:** In Luke 2:27 and Luke 2:41, the narrator uses "parents" (*goneus*, G1118). In Luke 2:33, the narrator writes "Joseph and his mother." In Luke 2:48, Mary speaks directly: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." In Luke 2:49, the child answers: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
- **Empowerment and Presence Lexicon:** The verbs in Luke 1:35—*eperchomai* (G1904, "come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "overshadow")—are the identical Greek verbs used for power coming upon the apostles in Acts 1:8 ("power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you") and for the cloud over the disciples in Luke 9:34 ("there came a cloud, and overshadowed them").
- **Davidic Seed and Loins Texts:** In Romans 1:3, Christ was "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." In Acts 2:30, God swore "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." In Psalm 132:11, the promise is "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." In 2 Samuel 7:12, the seed shall "proceed out of thy bowels." In Hebrews 7:10, Levi "was yet in the loins of his father."
- **Shared Flesh and Abrahamic Seed:** In Hebrews 2:14, Christ "also himself likewise took part of the same"; in Hebrews 2:16, "he took on him the seed of Abraham"; and in Hebrews 2:17, "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren."
- **Genealogy Framing:** In Matthew 1:1, the line is headed "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham." In Matthew 1:17, "from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations."
- **New Testament Applications of Psalm 2:7:** The declaration "Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee" is quoted at the resurrection in Acts 13:33 ("in that he hath raised up Jesus again"), at the priesthood in Hebrews 5:5, and paired with 2 Samuel 7:14 in Hebrews 1:5.

### 3. Drift Guard Examination (Challenger Only)

The Challenger’s submissions, concessions, and grants were evaluated against the active framework drift guards:

- **DG-8 (Biological Father: Joseph Named):** The Challenger maintained that Joseph is the named biological Davidic father, arguing the Davidic seed chain from 2 Samuel 7:12, Psalm 132:11, Acts 2:30, and Romans 1:3. The Challenger held Mary's words in Luke 2:48 ("thy father and I"), identified Joseph and Mary as husband and wife from espousal (Matthew 1:19–20; Deuteronomy 22:24), and argued that Joseph knew Mary within the espousal based on Genesis 4:1 and Matthew 1:24–25. The Challenger did not suggest Mary had a baby without a man, did not route the seed through Mary alone, and did not adopt the purged genealogy construct (DG-56).
- **DG-18 (Son of God = Covenant Title):** The Challenger maintained that "of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" represent covenant origin, empowerment, and title rather than biological paternity. When citing Psalm 2:7, the Challenger correctly exhibited its three New Testament occurrences: Acts 13:33 (resurrection), Hebrews 5:5 (priesthood), and Hebrews 1:5 (paired with 2 Samuel 7:14).
- **DG-60 (Seed, Not Blood):** The Challenger consistently argued lineage in the text’s word, *seed* (*zera'*, *sperma*), counted by covenant, rather than constructing bloodline arguments. Canonical occurrences of "blood" were cited strictly within the text of John 1:13 and Hebrews 2:14.

**Result:** Zero drift guard violations committed by the Challenger.

### 4. Method and Engagement

Neither side utilized evasive placeholders (e.g., *"Noted. Not conceding here. Goes to review"*). Both combatants maintained strict method by grounding arguments in textual citations ([L1]), lexical parsing ([L2]), and scriptural cross-references ([L3]).

- **Challenger Engagement:** The Challenger pressed the Defender’s opening positions on a chain-level basis. Against the passive verb in Matthew 1:16, the Challenger introduced the mother-markers of Matthew 1:3, 1:5, and 1:6 (*ek* with feminine nouns) alongside the Davidic heading (1:1) and generation count (1:17). Against the divine paternity reading of Matthew 1:20, the Challenger compared *ek* with God in 1 John 5:1 and John 1:13, contrasted spirit and flesh using John 3:6 and Romans 1:3, and analyzed the covenant address in 1 Chronicles 28:6. In response to Defender presses, the Challenger narrowed C3 and C4 to match the precise covenant-address and legal-reckoning patterns.
- **Defender Defense:** The Defender engaged directly with every press rather than evading. The Defender granted that *ek* marks mothers in Matthew 1:3, 1:5, and 1:6, but distinguished Matthew 1:16 on the basis that the active verb *egennēsen* ceases at Joseph and does not take Jesus as its direct grammatical object. When pressed on the timing of Matthew 1:18, the Defender pointed to *synerchomai* ("before they came together") and Joseph's intent to put Mary away privily (Matthew 1:19) as evidence of non-paternity. When pressed on pedigree law and Ezra 2:61, the Defender acknowledged that Ezra 2:62 disqualified those priests and dropped that support line. The Defender systematically narrowed D2, D4, D5, and D6 to isolate and defend the core proposition that the Holy Ghost is the sole stated source of the conception.

---

### 5. Textual Tension and Structural Vulnerabilities

Without asserting a verdict, the debate leaves each position facing distinct textual pressures:

#### Defender Vulnerability
- **The Physical Seed Chain:** Scripture repeatedly defines the Davidic lineage through physical procreative terms: 2 Samuel 7:12 specifies seed that shall "proceed out of thy bowels"; Psalm 132:11 specifies the "fruit of thy body"; Acts 2:30 states "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh"; and Romans 1:3 states Christ was "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." 
- **The Father's Line in Pedigree:** Numbers 1:18 establishes that pedigrees are declared "by the house of their fathers," and Luke 2:4 explicitly places Joseph in the "house and lineage of David." The text nowhere explicitly states Mary's lineage or house, while Luke 1:36 associates her with Elisabeth, who was "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5). Having dropped Ezra 2:61, the Defender’s position rests on an inference [L4] that the physical Davidic seed reached Christ through Mary alone, a transmission mechanism not explicitly narrated in the text.

#### Challenger Vulnerability
- **The Non-Narrated Union:** The Challenger’s position that Joseph knew Mary within the espousal requires inserting marital relations prior to Matthew 1:18, a detail the text does not record.
- **The Explicit Timing and Reaction Rows:** Matthew 1:18 explicitly states that "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." If Joseph had already known Mary as his wife, Matthew 1:19 records that Joseph, "being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily"—a reaction the Defender argued is inconsistent with a husband conscious of his own paternity. Furthermore, Matthew 1:25 states that Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son," and in Luke 1:34 Mary states, "seeing I know not a man," requiring the Challenger to interpret "till" (*heōs*) as an abstinence bounded strictly to the post-taking pregnancy and Mary's statement as strictly present tense.

### D1: Matthew breaks his "begat" line at Joseph (answers C1)

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:16 -- D1 -- "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."**
- [L1] The active "begat" has Jacob as its subject and Joseph as its object. Joseph is then named "the husband of Mary" (anēr, G435, "a man, husband"). The one born stands under the passive "was born."
- [L2] The relative "of whom" is hēs, feminine singular, so it points back to Mary and not to Joseph. The verb is gennaō (G1080), "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)." It is active in the father's sense through Jacob and passive in the mother's sense for the one born.
- [L3] Matthew 1:3: "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." Matthew 1:6: "David the king begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Urias." In both, the father is the subject of an active "begat" whose object is the child, and the woman's "of" follows. In 1:16 the child is under the passive "was born," with the woman alone.
- [L4] The challenger's parallel with 1:3 and 1:6 breaks on the verses' own wording. There the father's "begat" takes the child as object and the woman is added. In 1:16 the father-verb ends on Joseph and the woman alone carries the child. This stands on [L1] 1:16 and 1:3 and [L2] hēs.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:2 -- D1 -- "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;"**
- [L1] The formula is "[father] begat [son]," and the one begotten becomes the next subject.
- [L3] Matthew 1:16 follows the formula up to "Jacob begat Joseph." Then it changes to "of whom was born Jesus."
- [L4] The verse itself shows the formula carried to Joseph and then changed to the passive with the woman. That change is the break D1 names. It stands on [L1] 1:2 and 1:16 and [L3] the pattern of 1:3 and 1:6.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:17 (with Matthew 1:1 and 1:18) -- D1 -- "from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ [are] fourteen generations."**

### D2: The conceiving is "of the Holy Ghost" (answers C2)

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:18 -- D2 -- "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."**

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological human father

**Position.** The standard reading is that Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost without a man's seed. Joseph was his legal and supposed father, not his begetter. I stand on the interlocking text, not on any single word.

## 1. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at the last link

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Every earlier link uses ἐγέννησεν (egennēsen, "begat", the father's act of generating). At the end the verb becomes passive, ἐγεννήθη (egennēthē, "was born"). The relative pronoun ἧς (hēs, "of whom") is feminine singular, so it can refer only to Mary and not to Joseph. Joseph is called ἀνήρ (anēr, "husband"), not the one who begat.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary." The same persons are described as virgin and espoused.

**[L4]** Matthew keeps the rhythm of "begat" through sixteen verses and breaks it exactly where Jesus enters. That break rests on the feminine ἧς (Matthew 1:16, [L2]) and on the virgin of Luke 1:27 ([L3]). The text is saying that Jesus came from Mary and was not begotten by Joseph.

## 2. The conception is attributed to the Holy Ghost, and Mary denies any man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** In Matthew 1:18, ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (ek pneumatos hagiou) means "out of Spirit holy", naming the source. In Matthew 1:20, τὸ γεννηθέν (to gennēthen) means "that which is begotten or conceived". The same root gennaō is the verb of generation, here with the Spirit as the source.

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" **[L2]** ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω (andra ou ginōskō) means "I know not a man". It is present tense, a statement of her present state.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** ἐπισκιάσει (episkiasei) means "will overshadow". It is a verb of divine presence and power, not of union. **[L2]** The connector διό (dio, "therefore") makes the divine action the stated reason for the title.

**[L3]** John 4:24: "God is a Spirit". God's fatherhood here is not a carnal, human generation. Hebrews 10:5 says: "a body hast thou prepared me". **[L2]** κατηρτίσω (katērtisō) means "thou hast fitted out or prepared", an act of provision, not of seed.

**[L4]** Mary's question (Luke 1:34, [L1]) and the angel's answer, which names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest and no man (Luke 1:35, [L1]), exclude a human begetter. The Greek of Matthew 1:20 ([L2]) fixes the source of the begetting as the Spirit.

## 3. Joseph's fatherhood is only supposed or legal

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". **[L2]** νομιζόμενος (nomizomenos) means "being thought or reckoned". Luke himself marks the relation as a belief held by others, not a fact.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." **[L2]** ἐγίνωσκεν (eginōsken) means "he was knowing", an imperfect that describes continued non-relation. ἕως οὗ (heōs hou) means "until which", marking the limit of that state at the birth.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just man... was minded to put her away privily." Joseph acts as a man who knows the child is not his.

**[L3]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is the crowd's belief, the very thing Luke 3:23 marks as "supposed".

**[L3]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Mary uses the household word, and Jesus corrects the referent to his Father.

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 ([L1]) with νομιζόμενος ([L2]) shows that Scripture itself labels Joseph's fatherhood a supposition. Matthew 1:19 and 1:25 ([L3] and [L1]) give the reason: Joseph did not beget. Luke 2:48-49 ([L3]) shows both uses side by side.

## 4. Prophecy and the seed of the woman

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." **[L2]** עַלְמָה (ʿalmāh) means "a young woman of marriageable age". It is used of Rebekah, **[L3]** Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water", and Genesis 24:16 describes her as one whom "neither had any man known her". **[L1]** Matthew 1:23 quotes Isaiah: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child". **[L2]** The Greek is παρθένος (parthenos), "virgin", which fixes the sense by the inspired quotation.

**[L1]** Genesis 3:15: "thy seed and her seed". **[L2]** זֶרַע (zeraʿ) means "seed", and here it is assigned to the woman. **[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman". **[L2]** γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός (genomenon ek gynaikos) means "coming to be out of a woman", and no man is named.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:12 names Jechonias in Joseph's line, and Jeremiah 22:30 says: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David". **[L4]** Joseph's line carried that sentence. Luke 1:32 says "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David", and Romans 1:3 says "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". Together they leave the Davidic descent to run through Mary and not by Joseph's begetting.

## Anticipated objection

If the challenger says "Father" in Luke 2:49 means God begat him as a man begets, I answer with the chain. The act is "overshadow" and "prepared", not union (Luke 1:35 and Hebrews 10:5, [L1]). God is a Spirit (John 4:24, [L3]). So God's fatherhood is by the Holy Ghost's act and is not human biological generation.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Matthew 1:16 breaks the "begat" pattern of Matthew 1:2: the Greek verb passes from ἐγέννησεν ("begat") to ἐγεννήθη ("was born") with the feminine ἧς ("of whom"), and Luke 1:27 ([L3]) names Mary a virgin, so Jesus is traced to Mary and not to Joseph's begetting.
2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:18, 1:20, ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου, "out of Spirit holy"), and Mary says "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34, ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω), so no man was the source.
3. Joseph's fatherhood is only supposed: Luke 3:23 νομιζόμενος ("being thought") and Matthew 1:25 ἐγίνωσκεν ("he was knowing") with Matthew 1:19 show him as husband and guardian but not begetter.
4. The text matches the prophecy of the virgin and the woman's seed: Isaiah 7:14 עַלְמָה with Matthew 1:23 παρθένος ("virgin"), Genesis 3:15 "her seed", and Galatians 4:4 γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός ("coming to be out of a woman").
5. Christ had no biological human father: he was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, Joseph was only his supposed and legal father, and God's fatherhood is by the Spirit's overshadowing, not by human generation.

# Challenge: the seed of David according to the flesh came by the named father

**Position.** The defender's chain rests on four [L4] steps. Each turns a verse that does not narrate the begetting into a statement that "excludes a human begetter." Against that stand rows that do state the child's flesh: it is David's seed, "according to the flesh," out of "loins" and "bowels." The text names one man of the house of David beside Mary, and it names him "thy father." I take the links in order and aim at the keystone, D5.

---

## Against LINK D5 (the keystone): the flesh is stated, and it is a man's

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;"
**[L2]** The Greek is *ek spermatos Dauid kata sarka*. *Sperma* means "seed, offspring." *Kata sarka* means "according to the flesh." Paul states the child's bodily origin as David's seed.
**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;"
**[L2]** *Osphys* means "loins." It is the same word Hebrews uses for descent from a father: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham" (Hebrews 7:5) and "he was yet in the loins of his father" (Hebrews 7:10).
**[L3]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne" [margin: "Heb. belly"]. 1 Kings 8:19: "thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins."
**[L4]** The promise is a seed out of a man's loins and bowels (2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30, *osphys*). The fulfilment is "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3, *kata sarka*). From those two footings, the child's flesh is stated as David's by bodily descent, which is the contrary of "no biological human father."

**Whose loins?** Only one person beside Mary is named of David's house.
**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
**[L3]** Mary's own kin, where the text names it, is priestly. Luke 1:36 calls Elisabeth "thy cousin," and Luke 1:5 says Elisabeth was "of the daughters of Aaron."
**[L3]** Descent is reckoned by the father's house. Numbers 1:18 says they "declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Ezra 2:59 says those who "could not shew their father's house, and their seed [margin: or, pedigree]" could not prove they were of Israel.
**[L4]** Hebrews 7:14 says it is "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." The tribe is counted "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18). The one Davidic man named is Joseph (Luke 2:4). So the evident descent runs by the named father, and the defender's route "through Mary" has no stated lineage behind it.

---

## Against LINK D1: Matthew 1:16 does not narrate the begetting

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
**[L2]** I grant the defender's grammar. *Egennēthē* ("was born") is passive, and *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine. The verb names the birth from the mother. It is the act Luke 2:7 narrates: "she brought forth her firstborn son."
**[L3]** The same Gospel then has the angel address the husband by his Davidic line: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). Joseph is also given the father's act of naming: "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:21), done at 1:25, "he called his name JESUS."
**[L3]** Naming is the father's act in Luke as well: "thou shalt call his name John" (Luke 1:13); "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called" (Luke 1:62).
**[L4]** The passive with *hēs* says what Mary did, which is to bear (Luke 2:7). The surrounding rows give Joseph the son-of-David address and the father's naming (Matthew 1:20-21; Luke 1:62). Read with them, the change of verb records the birth from the mother. It does not state that the begetter was absent. The defender's sentence, "was not begotten by Joseph," is drawn from the verb's silence, not from its words.

---

## Against LINK D2: "of the Holy Ghost" and "come upon" are covenant and empowering language

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *Ek* means "out of, from." Where *ek* takes God as its object of men born, the origin is covenant, not paternity:
- **[L3]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- **[L3]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
**[L2]** *Andra ou ginōskō* is present indicative, "I know not a man." The defender agrees it is "a statement of her present state." It describes her state at the announcement. It does not describe the months that follow.
**[L4]** The defender's verbs are empowerment (*eperchomai*, Acts 1:8) and presence (*episkiazō*, Luke 9:34). Mary's words are present-state (*ginōskō*, Luke 1:34). So D2's step "exclude a human begetter" rests on no verb of exclusion. It infers from presence-verbs what they do not state.

But two verses earlier Luke's narration says "Joseph and his mother knew not [of it]" (Luke 2:43) and "his parents" (Luke 2:41). The covenant Father of 1 Chronicles 28:6 and the father of the house stand together in that verse. Neither cancels the other.

**On Matthew 1:19.**
**[L1]** "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
**[L2]** The Greek is *dikaios ōn, mē thelōn... eboulēthē lathra apolysai autēn*: "being just, not willing... he purposed to release her secretly." It gives an intent and two grounds. It has no verb of knowing.

**[L1]** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
**[L2]** *Heōs hou* means "until which." The defender agrees it marks "the limit of that state at the birth."

**[L4] The union, as the rows give it.** Four footings:
- They were husband and wife from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19); "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). The law calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- The canon's stated means of begetting is knowing: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1).
- The seed is required out of a man's loins (Acts 2:30).

From these I infer that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and that the child is of his loins. The defender's "Joseph acts as a man who knows the child is not his" puts a verb of knowing into Matthew 1:19 that the Greek does not carry.

---

## Against LINK D4: the sign, the woman's seed, and the curse

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son" [margin: "or, thou, O virgin, shalt call"].
**[L2]** The word is *ʿalmāh* (H5959), "young woman": 7 verses. The defender concedes "a young woman of marriageable age." *Bethulah* (H1330) is not used here.
**[L3]** The sign is bounded in Isaiah's own day: "before the child shall know to refuse the evil... the land... shall be forsaken" (Isaiah 7:16). Isaiah 8:3-4 follows, and "O Immanuel" appears in 8:8.

I hold Matthew 1:23 as written: "a virgin shall be with child." *Parthenos* ("virgin") is the word Luke 1:27 uses of Mary "espoused to a man... Joseph." It names her state at the espousal and announcement, the same state as Luke 1:34's present tense. It does not narrate the begetting.

**[L1]** Genesis 3:15: "her seed."
**[L3]** Seed is said of a woman in the offspring sense elsewhere: Hagar, "I will multiply thy seed" (Genesis 16:10); Rebekah, "let thy seed possess the gate" (Genesis 24:60). Both bore by husbands.

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman."
**[L3]** "Born of a woman" is the mortality idiom: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days" (Job 14:1). The Lord says of John: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist" (Matthew 11:11), and John's father is named (Luke 1:13).

1. **C1.** The child's flesh is David's seed out of a man's loins: Romans 1:3 (*kata sarka*), Acts 2:30 (*osphys*), and 2 Samuel 7:12.
2. **C2.** The Davidic man named is Joseph, and descent is reckoned by the father's house: Luke 1:27; 2:4; Numbers 1:18; Hebrews 7:14.
3. **C3.** The text names Joseph father in Mary's mouth, the narrator's, the town's and a disciple's: Luke 2:48; 2:41; John 6:42; John 1:45.
4. **C4.** "Of the Holy Ghost," "come upon" and "overshadow" are covenant origin, empowering and presence (John 1:13; Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34). "Son of God" is the covenant title (1 Chronicles 28:6; Acts 13:33).
5. **C5.** Therefore Christ had a biological father, Joseph, who knew Mary his wife within the espousal (Matthew 1:19-20; Genesis 4:1; Matthew 1:25).

---

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES (the defender's)

**1. LINK D5:** "Christ had no biological human father: he was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, Joseph was only his supposed and legal father."
- **Charge:** This conclusion stands against stated rows.

  - Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" [L1]. *Kata sarka* means "according to the flesh" [L2].

rows.synthesis:
# SYNTHESIS

## 1. What stands uncontested at L1–L2–L3

A point appears here only where neither side's charge list contests it.

- **Matthew 1:16's verb form.** [L1] "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." The challenger granted the grammar outright: "I grant the defender's grammar. *Egennēthē* ('was born') is passive, and *hēs* ('of whom') is feminine." Both sides agree the passive names the mother's act, which the challenger ties to Luke 2:7, "she brought forth her firstborn son." What the change does to the question of the begetter is contested (see §2).
- **Joseph is named of David's house.** [L1] Luke 1:27, "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David"; Luke 2:4, "because he was of the house and lineage of David." The defender: "I grant that these rows name Joseph's house."
- **A betrothed woman is a wife in law.** [L1] Deuteronomy 22:24, "his neighbour's wife"; Matthew 1:20, "Mary thy wife." The defender: "I grant that a betrothed woman is called a wife."
- **Taking is a distinct step from betrothal.** [L1] Matthew 1:24, "and took unto him his wife"; Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her." The defender: "I grant that taking and betrothal are distinct steps."
- **The Luke 1:35 verbs are not begetting verbs.** [L2] *eperchomai* / *episkiazō*. The defender: "I grant that the verb is not a begetting verb"; "I grant that overshadowing is presence and not union."
- **νομίζω carries no verdict of falsehood.** [L1] Luke 3:23, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." The defender: "I grant that the verb names what is held by custom or opinion and does not carry a verdict of falsehood."
- **Luke 1:34 is Mary's state when the angel spoke.** The defender: "I grant that this is her state when the angel spoke."
- **The narrator uses *goneus*, "parents," of Joseph and Mary together.** [L1] Luke 2:27, "when the parents brought in the child Jesus"; Luke 2:41, "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year." The defender: "I grant the narrator uses 'parents' of Joseph and Mary together."
- **Luke's register is Joseph's and the divergence is unexplained.** The defender: "I grant that Luke writes Joseph's line and that the text does not explain the divergence." The challenger: "That divergence is real, and the text does not explain it."
- **The title sits on a begotten son, and "begotten" is applied at the resurrection.** [L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6, "Solomon thy son … I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father"; Acts 13:33, "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee." The defender: "I grant 1 Chronicles 28:6 is a parallel for a title"; and earlier, "Acts 13:33 … is applied to the resurrection."
- **"Her seed" is also said of women whose husbands begat.** [L1] Genesis 16:10, "I will multiply thy seed exceedingly"; Genesis 24:60, "let thy seed possess the gate." The defender: "I grant that 'seed' … is said of Hagar (Genesis 16:10) and Rebekah (Genesis 24:60)."

## 2. Concessions, narrowings, and contested footings — both link rounds and both close rounds

**Defender's links**

| Link | Status | The side's own words |
|---|---|---|
| D1 (Matt 1:16 break) | NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE | "Matthew 1:16 does not write 'Joseph begat Jesus.' It alone does not close the question, and D2 carries the rest." |
| D2 (conception "of the Holy Ghost") | CITED-WITH-FOOTING, contested | R3 "LINK 2: SUPPORTED"; R4 "D2: KEPT." Pressed by Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, John 1:13; answer: "That is the exclusion. It rests on the answer given to the question asked, not on the verbs alone." |
| D3, premise 5 ("supposed") | NARROWED-BY-ITS-OWN-SIDE | "I drop the claim that *nomizō* itself proves the supposition false." |
| D3, premise 6 (Joseph's intent) | CITED-WITH-FOOTING, with a limb CONCEDED | "I CONCEDE the Matthew 1:25 limb of D3. The imperfect and *heōs* (G2193, 'until') do not by themselves prove that Joseph never knew her before the pregnancy. I do not rest on them." |
| D4 (virgin sign / "through Mary") | NARROWED twice and one limb CONCEDED | R3: "I drop the claim that Luke 3 is Mary's genealogy or that any verse states Mary's tribe." R4: "I keep Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 only as consistent with the chain. I do not claim they prove it"; "I CONCEDE that Galatians 4:4 does not exclude a father." |
| D5 (keystone) | CITED-WITH-FOOTING, two limbs CONCEDED out of its footing | "I CONCEDE that this is about believers (*gennaō* figuratively, 'to regenerate,' G1080), who also had a flesh-birth (John 3:6). D5 does not rest on it"; "1 John 5:1 … Conceded in the same way." Also: "So Acts 2:30 states that the descent is David's, not which step carried it. The text is silent on the channel, and I do not fill it"; "It nowhere states Mary's tribe." |

**Challenger's links**

| Link | Status | The side's own words |
|---|---|---|
| C1/LINK 1 (Luke's list runs from Joseph, no woman in any link) | CITED-WITH-FOOTING, kept | "The defender granted that the verb 'does not carry a verdict of falsehood.' The words qualify the reckoning. They do not insert a woman into the list, which still runs from Joseph." |
| LINK 2 (a Mary-line is a construct) | CITED-WITH-FOOTING; the opposing claim was dropped by the defender in its own words | "To turn one of them into Mary's line is a construct, not a reading," against the defender's "I drop the claim that Luke 3 is Mary's genealogy." |
| LINK 3 (loins are fathers' loins) | CITED-WITH-FOOTING, contested | "A line that runs past the patriarch's own days is still out of loins at every step (Hebrews 7:5 with Matthew 1:2)," against the defender's "It does not state that every step is a father's." |
| LINK 4 (Joseph knew Mary within the espousal) | CITED-WITH-FOOTING, contested | "Matthew sets the coming together by the taking that follows (Matthew 1:24; Deuteronomy 20:7)," against the defender's "*Synerchomai* … is glossed 'to convene … or (specially), cohabit (conjugally).'" |
| LINK 5 (*gennaō* with God beside a flesh father) | CITED-WITH-FOOTING; John 1:13 / 1 John 5:1 limb conceded by the defender, Matthew 1:20 limb contested | The defender: "Conceded in the same way"; then "But in 1:20 the word is *gennaō* in the passive (margin 'begotten,' G1080), and the 'for' makes it the ground of 'fear not.'" |
| LINK 6 (the narrator's "parents") | CITED-WITH-FOOTING; fact granted, inference contested | The defender: "I grant the narrator uses 'parents' of Joseph and Mary together. It names the household, not the begetter." |

The challenger's own grants in its link round: "I grant the defender's grammar" (Matthew 1:16), and, of its own witness on Mary's kin, "Exodus 6:23 shows Aaron married into Judah. It gives Mary no tribe at all."

**Close rounds.** The defender's close round answers every one of the six pressed premises by naming the witness and quoting it — Matthew 1:6 and Luke 1:13 against D1; Luke 1:34–35, Matthew 1:18, 1:20, Deuteronomy 22:24 against D2; Luke 3:23, John 6:42, Luke 2:27, 2:41, 2:33, 2:43, 2:48, 2:49, Matthew 1:19, 1:24, 1:25 against D3; Genesis 3:15, Galatians 4:4, Job 14:1, Matthew 11:11, Genesis 16:10, 24:60 against D4; Acts 2:30, Romans 1:3, Hebrews 7:5, 2 Samuel 7:12, Genesis 4:1, John 1:13, 1 John 5:1, John 3:6, 3:4, 1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 16:13 against D5 — and drops the enumerated limbs above in its own words. The challenger's close round names no book, chapter and verse that its earlier rounds had not named, so nothing in it is outside the count; it keeps its six links under their numbers with L1 + L2 + L3 footing on each. The challenger's close is structurally last in this format; the defender has no round after it, and that procedural silence is not a concession by either side and is charged to neither.

## 3. Drift-guard test — the challenger's seat only

**Filed:** *DG-18, rule addition on Psalm 2:7* — "never quote Psalm 2:7 without its three NT occasions." The seat quotes the Psalm's words through Acts 13:33, "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee," in R1 and again in the close ("The record applies 'begotten' to the resurrection (Acts 13:33; Romans 1:4)"), and names neither Hebrews 5:5 nor Hebrews 1:5 in either place. The use made of the row is the guard's own reading — resurrection, not conception — so the breach is citation-form, not doctrinal. Filed as stated.

**Tested and clear:**
- **DG-8, both directions.** No forbidden "no human father" / "without Joseph" / "routed through Mary alone" language is asserted or granted by this seat; the guard's own held ground is stated: "the chain stands: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins."
- **DG-8 on Matthew 1:16's passive.** The seat's words match the guard's: "It names her state at the espousal and announcement"; "It does not state that the begetter was absent."
- **DG-8 / DG-18 on "of the Holy Ghost" and the title.** Origin-marker, not paternity: "'Of God' names origin at John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1, of men who each also had a flesh-father"; and on the title, "1 Chronicles 28:6 shows that the two fatherhoods stand together in one verse without displacing each other."
- **DG-56.** The divergence is held open, no construct supplied: "That divergence is real, and the text does not explain it."
- **DG-59.** Verse-against-verse is refused: "To set the two verses against each other is the defender's own inference; neither verse states it."
- **DG-60.** Lineage argued in the text's word, seed — *sperma*, *zeraʿ*, *osphys*, "out of the loins of Abraham" — with no blood-referent asserted as a who-belongs verdict; the single *haima* gloss at LINK 5 is a lexicon note on John 1:13's own word.
- **DG-49 (adjacent).** The Hebrew/Greek of Isaiah 7:14 is handled at L1–L2 with the KJV margin ("or, thou, O virgin, shalt call") and no external apparatus is invoked: "I hold Matthew 1:23 as written: 'a virgin shall be with child.'"

## 4. How the challenger engaged, and the defense's method

The challenger engaged chains as chains. It answered the defender's five declared links by number in R1 and again in R2, it declared six links of its own, and every one of the six carries an [L1] quotation with an [L2] gloss and at least one [L3] cross-reference — the form the framework requires, not a single-verse demand. It named the disputed steps as floating and pressed each with rows (e.g. "the row gives an intent and two grounds, and no verb of knowing"), and it refused a construct rather than building one.

The defense answered each pressed premise twice, witness by witness, in its link round and again in its close round, and it dropped limbs in its own words rather than restating them (Matthew 1:25; *nomizō*; Luke 3 as Mary's line; Galatians 4:4's exclusionary force; John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1 as footing for D5). It also stated the limits of its own case — "I state plainly what the text does not say. It nowhere states Mary's tribe"; "The text is silent on the channel, and I do not fill it." No placeholder sentence of the "Noted. Not conceding here. Goes to review." form appears anywhere in this transcript, on either seat; no link on either side was left as a bare characterisation without footing.

## 5. Most vulnerable — where the two lists stand furthest apart

No verdict is delivered here; these are the junctions the record itself leaves contested, each quoted.

1. **The channel of the Davidic descent.** Defender: "So Acts 2:30 states that the descent is David's, not which step carried it. The text is silent on the channel, and I do not fill it." Challenger: "The oath names the seed by David's procreative power, his loins, 'according to the flesh' (Acts 2:30, G3751). Hebrews 7:10 uses that loins-word only of a father: 'the loins of his father.'" No row on either list was withdrawn on this point by the side that holds it.
2. **The nature of Matthew 1:20's *ek pneumatos hagiou*.** Defender: "the word is *gennaō* in the passive (margin 'begotten,' G1080), and the 'for' makes it the ground of 'fear not.'" Challenger: "'Of God' names origin at John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1, of men who each also had a flesh-father."
3. **The timing of *synerchomai* in Matthew 1:18.** Defender: "*Synerchomai* (G4905) is glossed 'to convene … or (specially), cohabit (conjugally).' The finding is dated before the cohabiting." Challenger: "The verse dates the finding before the taking. The knowing I hold is within the espousal, before the taking, so the finding before the taking agrees with it."
4. **The scope of "loins."** Defender: "Hebrews 7:10 shows the word naming a descendant as having been in an ancestor's procreative power. It does not state that every step is a father's." Challenger: "Wherever the canon uses this word for descent, the loins are a father's."
5. **The weight the defender's close assigns its own case.** Its own words: "D5 is kept as the conclusion, with John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1 conceded as outside its footing," and "D2 is kept as the load-bearing link." Against that stands the challenger's closing sentence: "Seed out of loins cannot stand where no man is involved."

--- ORACLE_DEBATE_V1 CONFIRMATION ---
(A review of the single judge's second opinion, which was HELD. The debate's verdict is the panel's.)
**BRIEF CONFIRMATION.** Accurate where it quotes, with three seams left showing. The §2 tables and §5 junctions each reduce to words the rounds actually carry — D1's own narrowing ("Matthew 1:16 does not write 'Joseph begat Jesus'"), the conceded Matthew 1:25 limb, the dropped Luke 3/Mary's-line claim, the retire-and-restate under K-C, and the challenger's grants at Matthew 1:16 (*egennēthē* passive, *hēs* feminine) — and §1's common ground ([L1] Matthew 1:16; Luke 1:27, 2:4 on Joseph's house; Deuteronomy 22:24 "his neighbour's wife") is granted on both seats. Uncarried tensions: (i) §3 runs the drift test on the challenger's seat **only**, while the second opinion's own terminal chain is the defender's D5, "Christ had no biological human father … conceived by the Holy Ghost," plus its narrowed "through-woman" D4 with Mary's tribe admittedly unstated — the exact direction the framework closes: "of the Holy Ghost" is held as covenant-origin/anointing, not paternity, and no NT row applies *gennaō* to the flesh in Mary as God's begetting (Acts 13:33; Hebrews 5:5; Hebrews 1:5), so the seat cannot be "tested and clear" on one side while the other side's keystone asserts the closed direction; (ii) the second opinion's body contradicts its score line — one challenger link graded BROKEN and one premise UNEXHIBITED beside k=0, w=0, "conceded links: 0" — and the audit's v18 note (conceded item stated, never tagged) is not answered by keeping the stated value; (iii) D5 vs C3 is "UNDERDETERMINED" in the collision points and "STANDS" in the collision map. New: nothing doctrinal enters the paper — only the §3 guard-application note and the DG-18 citation-form filing are additions, and that filing, standing alone with no corresponding test of the defender's seat, is itself asymmetric under the rule that the guards cut both ways.
