DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 4, CLOSE ROUND

## CLOSE ROUND: DEFENDER

I keep D1 to D5 as declared, with no renumbering and no new links. I answer the challenger's blocks C1 to C6 and each witness pressed in them.

### D1: Mary conceived before any union with Joseph or any man

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:18 -- D1 --** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." (C2, P2.1)
- [L1] The verse puts the finding of the child before the coming together.
- [L2] *synerchomai* (G4905) means "to convene... or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)."
- [L3] Matthew 1:20 uses a different verb for the house-taking: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." *Paralambanō* (G3880) means "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself." Matthew 1:24 repeats the act: "and took unto him his wife."
- [L4] The challenger makes the coming together equal to the house-taking, but the text has two verbs for two acts. One verb carries the conjugal sense in its gloss, and the other is the taking near. Matthew 1:18 therefore dates the conception before the conjugal coming together. The challenger's placing of Joseph's knowing "before the finding" has no verse behind it.

**ANSWER: Deuteronomy 20:7 -- D1 --** "And what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" (C2, P2.1)
- [L1] The verse says "betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". It marks the betrothed man as one who has not yet taken her.
- [L3] Matthew 1:18 says "before they came together" and Matthew 1:24 says "took unto him his wife".
- [L4] Deuteronomy 20:7 puts betrothal before the taking, and Matthew 1:18 puts the finding before the coming together. This matches D1's order. It does not place a knowing inside the espousal.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:25 -- D1 --** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." (C2, P2.3)
- [L1] The knowing is withheld until the birth.
- [L2] *ginōskō* is the verb of Genesis 4:1.
- [L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain". There the knowing precedes the conceiving. Matthew 1:25 gives the knowing as withheld until after the bringing forth.
- [L4] Matthew 1:18 gives the finding with child as already true, and Matthew 1:25 gives no knowing until the birth. The conception lies between those two, and no knowing stands there to cause it. The challenger's knowing "within the espousal" is a gap that Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 together close.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:34 -- D1 --** "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" (C2, P2.4)
- [L1] Mary gives her not knowing a man as the ground of her "How".
- [L2] *andra* (G435) means "a man", and *ginōskō* is in the present tense.
- [L3] Luke 1:27 puts the espousal in the same scene: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph".
- [L4] The text sets Mary's espousal (1:27) beside her "How" (1:34). Her espousal to Joseph did not answer her own question, so she asks. The angel's reply gives a different means (1:35), and Luke 1:37 adds "For with God nothing shall be impossible."

### D2: The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:20 -- D2 --** "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [margin: Gr. begotten] (C3)
- [L1] The reason given is a "for": the thing begotten in her is "of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)." *Ek* (G1537) is "out of", the source.
- [L3] John 1:13 sets "of God" against the other sources: "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." 1 John 5:1 uses the same "born of God" for believers.
- [L4] *Gennaō* is the begetting word, and it is placed "in her" with the Holy Ghost as the "out of". The challenger grants that Matthew 1:18 names the source at the finding. Scripture's own use of "of God" opposes it to "the will of man" (John 1:13). Matthew 1:20 therefore gives the Holy Ghost as the source of this begetting.

**ANSWER: Romans 1:3 -- D2 --** "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh". (C1, C3)
- [L1] Romans 1:3 gives the seed of David "according to the flesh."
- [L2] *ginomai* (G1096) means "to become", and it is the verb of Galatians 4:4.
- [L3] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman". Romans 1:4 gives the second clause: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness". Matthew 1:16 gives Joseph his title: "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus".
- [L4] The same verb *ginomai* carries "made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) and "made of the seed of David" (Romans 1:3). The flesh of David's seed is therefore come through the woman, and Romans 1:4 gives the holy origin in its own clause. What Romans 1:3 states is the line, "the seed of David", and the verse that speaks of Joseph, Matthew 1:16, states him as "the husband of Mary". Acts 2:30 gives "the fruit of his loins", where "his" is David's.

**ANSWER: Acts 2:30 -- D2 --** "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne". (C1, C2)
- [L1] The loins are David's.
- [L2] *osphys* (G3751) means "the loin." Hebrews 7:10 uses the same word for Levi "in the loins of his father".
- [L3] Luke 1:32 gives the throne by God's gift: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- [L4] Acts 2:30 and Hebrews 7:10 speak of the ancestor's loins, David's and Abraham's. The challenger's step from these to Joseph's loins is the challenger's own addition to what those verses say.

**ANSWER: Hebrews 7:14 -- D2 --** "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda". (C1, P1.1)
- [L1] The verse states that the tribe is Juda.
- [L3] Romans 1:3 says "made of the seed of David according to the flesh", and Galatians 4:4 says "made of a woman".
- [L4] Hebrews 7:14 states the tribe. Romans 1:3 with Galatians 4:4 supplies the route, through the woman by *ginomai*. The tribe is evident without a register of fathers, and Hebrews 7:16 ("Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life") sets the priesthood outside the fleshly rule. The challenger grants that Hebrews 7:16 governs the office.

**ANSWER: Numbers 1:18 -- D2 --** "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers". (C1)
- [L1] The verse is a census rule for the congregation's polls.
- [L2] *bayith* (H1004) means "house, especially family".
- [L3] Exodus 2:10 says "he became her son", and Esther 2:7 says "took for his own daughter". In both, a house receives by taking.
- [L4] Numbers 1:18 sets a census rule for the people at large. Luke 2:5 enrols "Mary his espoused wife, being great with child" into Joseph's household, and Matthew 1:20 and 1:25 give Joseph the taking and the naming. Joseph's house receives the child by taking and naming, as Exodus 2:10 and Esther 2:7 show for other households.

**ANSWER: Ezra 2:59 -- D2 --** "but they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel". (C1, P1.3)
- [L1] The verse is about men who could not show their pedigree.
- [L3] Ezra 2:61 says "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name", and Ezra 2:62 says "These sought their register". A line could be called after the mother's father.
- [L4] Ezra 2:59-62 concerns the priests' register, and Ezra 2:61 shows a name carried by the wife's house. It gives no ground for making Joseph's seed the source of Jesus.

**ANSWER: Luke 2:4 -- D2 --** "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)". (C1, P1.4)
- [L1] The verse names Joseph's own house and lineage.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20 addresses him as "thou son of David" at the moment the child is given into his house.
- [L4] Luke 2:4 gives Joseph's lineage and the reason for the going up. Matthew 1:21 and 1:25 give the naming ("thou shalt call his name JESUS"; "he called his name JESUS"). Joseph's naming places the child in his house by the same pattern as Exodus 2:10. That is placing by naming, and it is not begetting.

**ANSWER: 2 Samuel 7:12 -- D2 --** "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom." (C1, P1.2)
- [L1] The verse is the promise to David about his seed.
- [L2] *qereb* (H7130) means "the nearest part... bowels".
- [L3] Luke 1:32 says "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David", and Acts 2:30 says "of the fruit of his loins".
- [L4] The promise runs to David's body as the ancestral source. Romans 1:3 (the same verb as Galatians 4:4) carries it through the woman. The giving in Luke 1:32 belongs to the Lord God. The promise is therefore kept without a begotten-by-Joseph link.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:35 -- D2 --** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." (C3, P3.1; C4, P4.3)
- [L1] The "therefore" stands in the same verse, directly after the coming upon and the overshadowing.
- [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904) means "to come upon", and *episkiazō* (G1982) means "to overshadow".
- [L3] Luke 1:32 says "shall be called the Son of the Highest". Acts 1:8 says "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you", Luke 9:34 says "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them", and Acts 5:15 says "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them".
- [L4] The "therefore also" in v.35 follows the two verbs of v.35. The object of those verbs is Mary: "come upon thee", "overshadow thee". The child is called "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The challenger says the "therefore" runs back to v.32, but v.35's own words tie the Sonship to the coming upon and the overshadowing, in the woman. The *kai* ("also") adds this ground to the title given in v.32. In Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34 and Acts 5:15 the verbs rest on disciples, a cloud and the sick, and no child is conceived. Only in Luke 1:35 do they fall on the one of whom "that holy thing" is born.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:19 -- D2 --** "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." (C2, P2.2)
- [L1] Joseph is minded to put her away, and the verb is *apolyō*.
- [L2] *apolyō* (G630) means "to free fully... or (specially) divorce... put (send) away". *Paradeigmatizō* (G3856) means "expose to infamy", *boulomai* (G1014) means "minded", and *lathra* (G2977) means "privily".
- [L3] Matthew 1:20 gives the answer: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." *Phobeō* (G5399) means "be afraid".
- [L4] The challenger says the ground is public infamy. The angel's answer to Joseph's purpose is "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". It is a "for" of source, and it removes the reason for putting away. A husband who knew himself the father would need no source-clause to remove his fear of taking her. Matthew 1:19 and 1:20 together show that the angel answers the question of origin.

**ANSWER: Deuteronomy 22:23 -- D2 --** "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband, and a man find her in the city, and lie with her;" (C2, P2.2)
- [L1] The verse's "a man" who finds and lies with her is a man other than the husband.
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24 gives the penalty: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife".
- [L4] The challenger uses these verses for the public's reading of another man's act. Matthew 1:20 answers with a source, "of the Holy Ghost", and gives no verdict about the public. These verses do not carry "Joseph knew Mary".

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:24 -- D2 --** "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" (C2)
- [L1] Joseph took her after the angel's word.
- [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880) means "receive near, associate with oneself".
- [L3] Matthew 1:25 follows: "And knew her not till she had brought forth".
- [L4] The taking after the dream, followed by the knowing withheld, puts the angel's source-word ahead of Joseph's own act, and the next verse holds his knowing back until the birth.

### D3: Joseph was the husband and supposed father, not the begetter

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:16 -- D3 --** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." (C3, P3.2)
- [L1] The active "begat" reaches Joseph, and then the clause turns to "of whom was born".
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is "properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother." *Anēr* (G435) means "husband".
- [L3] Matthew 1:2 ("Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob") shows the pattern. Matthew 1:3 ("Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar") shows the mother added after the father's active verb.
- [L4] In Matthew 1:2-3 the father takes the active verb ("begat") and the mother is added with "of". In 1:16 the active verb is Jacob's, and Joseph takes the title "husband of Mary". The child is then given by the passive and the woman. The challenger grants that the passive is the bearing, and the verb "begat" is spoken of Jacob at 1:16 and is not put on Joseph.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:3 -- D3 --** "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar". (C3, P3.2)
- [L1] Judas has the active verb, and Thamar is added with "of".
- [L3] Matthew 1:16 gives Jesus the passive "of whom was born".
- [L4] The father's active verb is present at 1:3 and absent for Jesus at 1:16. That difference is the one D3 states.

**ANSWER: Luke 3:23 -- D3 --** "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". (C4, P4.2)
- [L1] The words "as was supposed" stand inside the filiation.
- [L2] *nomizō* (G3543) means "to do by law (usage)... suppose, be wont."
- [L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" Luke 4:22: "Is not this Joseph's son?"
- [L4] The challenger cites Acts 16:13 ("where prayer was wont to be made") as a custom with a real fact behind it. There the custom is a general practice stated of a place. In Luke 3:23 the same word sits in parentheses against "son of Joseph", marking the filiation as the held view. John 6:42 and Luke 4:22 show the people holding it, and in John 6:42 it stands against the child's own "I came down from heaven."

**C5 (kept): the child of the sign has a father to cry to.**
- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]"
- [L1] Isaiah 7:16: "before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- [L2] Isaiah 8:3 carries the margin "went: Heb. approached." The Hebrew is *qarab*, to come near.
- [L3] Isaiah 8:3-4: "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son ... before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother." Isaiah 8:8 addresses "O Immanuel" in Isaiah's own day.
- [L4] The sign is bounded by the same measure in Isaiah's day (7:16; 8:4). That measure is a child who knows to cry "My father." Matthew 1:22-23 fulfils it in a virgin espoused to Joseph (Luke 1:27).

**C6 (kept): Galatians 4:4 and Genesis 3:15 fit a named father.**
- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
- [L2] *Gynē* (G1135, "a woman; specially, a wife"). *Zera'* (H2233, "seed") stands in Genesis 3:15, "her seed," and in Genesis 4:25.
- [L3] Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman." Matthew 11:11: "born of women ... John the Baptist." Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son." Genesis 4:25: "Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son ... another seed."
- [L4] "Of a woman" is said of men whose fathers are named (G30), and Eve's "seed" is Adam's son. So these rows name the mother, and they fit the father whom Luke 2:48 and John 6:42 name: "Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know."

---

## Final words

The text gives a seed "which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30). It counts the tribe "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18) and makes Juda "evident" (Hebrews 7:14). It names one man of David's house in the birth: "Joseph, thou son of David ... Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20).

Mary calls him "thy father" (Luke 2:48). The town says "the son of Joseph" (John 6:42), and Philip says "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).

The Holy Ghost is the covenant origin of the promised Son, who receives "the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32). The flesh is David's seed through Joseph, David's son. Precept upon precept, Christ had a biological father, and his name is Joseph.

# OPENING: Jesus had no biological human father

**Thesis [L4].** Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, without a man's seed. Joseph was his legal, reputed father and not his biological one. Each section below carries its footing.

---

## 1. The conception is said to be "of the Holy Ghost", before any coming together

- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *sunerchomai* (G4905, "to come together", used here for the union of husband and wife) stands in this verse. The pregnancy is dated *before* that union. *Ek pneumatos hagiou* means "out of the Holy Spirit", and *ek* gives the source of the conception.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The angel repeats the source in the same terms, *ek pneumatos estin hagiou*.
- [L4] The text gives two sources for one conception, Mary's womb and the Holy Ghost. It places that conception before any union with Joseph. The chain runs from Matthew 1:18 (timing, "before they came together") through the *ek* of Matthew 1:20 (source) to the conclusion that no man's seed was the source.

## 2. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L2] *egennēsen* (from *gennaō*, G1080, "to beget") is the verb used for each father in the list. At Joseph it changes to *egennēthē ex hēs*, "was born out of whom". The relative pronoun *hēs* is feminine singular, so it can only point to Mary. Joseph is "the husband of Mary" (*ton andra Marias*), not the one who begat.
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". This is the pattern the verb sets, and it is not repeated at Joseph.
- [L4] The "begat" chain runs unbroken until Joseph. There the verb shifts to the passive and the relative becomes feminine. From Matthew 1:2 (the pattern) and the feminine *hēs* of Matthew 1:16 (the break), the writer is shown withholding "begat" from the last link.

## 3. Mary was a virgin, and Mary herself says she had known no man

- [L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."
- [L2] *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") stands in Luke 1:27 and again in Matthew 1:23.
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know", here carnal knowledge) with *andra* (G435, "a man", male) means she has had no relations with any male.
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *dio kai* ("therefore also") makes the answer a cause: the Holy Ghost coming upon her is the reason the child is called the Son of God. *Episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow") names the divine action.
- [L4] Mary asks how, since she knows no man. The angel gives a cause that is not a man. From Luke 1:34 (no man) and the *dio kai* of Luke 1:35 (the cause is divine), no man supplied the seed.

## 4. Joseph's own conduct and the angel's correction

- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man... was minded to put her away privily."
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- [L4] Joseph, the husband, answers the pregnancy by planning to put her away. A husband who knew himself to be the source would have had no such plan. The angel's remedy is to name another source ("of the Holy Ghost"), not to reassure him that the child is his own.
- [L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The verb *eginōsken* (G1097) is "knew". Both verses fit the conception being a divine act.

## 5. The text itself calls Joseph's fatherhood a supposition

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] *enomizeto* (from *nomizō*, G3543, "to reckon, to hold by custom") means "was reckoned". The writer marks the sonship as a view held by others, not as fact.
- [L3] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Jesus answers Mary's words in Luke 2:48 ("Thy father and I have sought thee") by naming a different Father.
- [L4] Luke 2:48 and John 6:42 use "father" and "son of Joseph" in the common speech of the people. Luke 3:23 (supposed) and Luke 2:49 (the answer) show how the text itself reads that speech.

## 6. The prophetic and bodily frame confirms it

- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
- [L2] *almah* (H5959, "virgin") is the word behind the KJV's "virgin".
- [L3] Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water". This is the same Hebrew word, used of Rebekah. Genesis 24:16 describes her as "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
- [L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son... God with us." Matthew quotes Isaiah as fulfilled in this birth.
- [L1] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
- [L2] *katartizō* (G2675, "to fit out, to prepare") means the body was prepared by God.
- [L3] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." The woman is named as the source and no man is named alongside her.
- [L4] Isaiah 7:14 (virgin conceives) and Matthew 1:23 (the fulfilment) agree with Hebrews 10:5 (a prepared body) and Galatians 4:4 (made of a woman). Together they give a conception from a woman and God, with no man's seed.

## Anticipated pressing

**Romans 1:3** [L1]: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." [L2] *ginomai* (G1096, "to become, to be made") is used here, not *gennaō* ("beget"). [L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb", and Luke 1:32 gives "the throne of his father David" to the child. [L4] The descent is real through the mother and legal through Joseph, who is addressed as "thou son of David" in Matthew 1:20. Neither carries the child's seed from a man.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost" and came before Joseph and Mary came together. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:20 ("is of the Holy Ghost"); [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* ("out of the Holy Spirit", source) and *sunerchomai* (G4905, "come together"); the chain is source plus timing, so no man's seed.
2. Matthew 1:16 withholds "begat" from Joseph and uses a feminine "of whom" for Mary. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16; [L2] *egennēsen* (G1080, "begat") against *ex hēs* (feminine, "out of whom"); [L3] Matthew 1:2 sets the pattern the break departs from.
3. Mary was a virgin who had known no man, and the angel's answer gives a divine cause. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34 and Luke 1:35; [L2] *ginōskō* with *andra* ("know a man") and *dio kai* ("therefore also", cause); [L3] Luke 1:27, *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin").
4. Joseph's fatherhood is reputed, not biological. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23 ("as was supposed"); [L2] *enomizeto* (G3543, "reckoned"); [L3] Luke 2:49 ("my Father's business") and Matthew 1:19.
5. Prophecy and the prepared body agree with a conception by a woman and God alone. Footing: [L1] Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23; [L2] *almah* (H5959, "virgin") and *katartizō* (G2675, "prepare"); [L3] Genesis 24:43, Hebrews 10:5, Galatians 4:4.
6. Jesus had no biological human father. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek* (source) and *egennēthē ex hēs* (feminine); [L3] Matthew 1:16 and Luke 3:23; the chain is that the conception came from Mary by the Holy Ghost, without a man's seed.

- **[L3]** The angel names Joseph's hindrance as fear (*phobeō*, G5399, "to be alarmed"): "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20).

**[L4]** The infamy Joseph would spare her is the public's reading of a pregnancy found before the taking (1:18). That exposure comes from the timing that was seen. Joseph's mind yielded to that outward consideration (*boulomai*), and the angel answered the fear (1:20). The angel then put on him the father's act, "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (1:21), which Joseph did (1:25). That is the act "his father" performs in Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called." It fits the link: a just husband sparing his wife public infamy over a pregnancy found before the taking is the plan Matthew 1:19 states.

## 5. The angel's "therefore" (LINK D3): it grounds the title of verse 32, and the sign beside it has a named father

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:"
- **[L2]** The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, and away from any reading of divine paternity of the flesh. It grounds the title given in verse 32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" (Luke 1:34).
- **[L2]** What v.35 grounds is a calling, *klēthēsetai* (*kaleō*, G2564, "to call"). Its object is "that holy thing" (*hagios*, G40, "sacred... consecrated").
- **[L3]** The title's own canon:
  - 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son... for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
  - 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- The defender says Solomon's ground was "choice" and Jesus' ground was conception. The New Testament puts the title's begetting-word at three occasions:
  - Psalm 2:7: "Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee. [the decree: or, for a decree]."

**[L4]** The "therefore" grounds a calling and a consecrated title (Luke 1:32, 35). The canon places the title's "begotten" at the resurrection and the priesthood (Acts 13:33; Hebrews 5:5), and in the house of David's son (1 Chronicles 28:6; Hebrews 1:5). The angel's own sign joins God's power with a husband's fatherhood (Luke 1:13, 36). So the cause in Luke 1:35 fits "the throne of his father David."

## 6. Matthew 1:16 and "on this wise" (LINK D2)

- **[L2]** At Matthew 1:25, "brought forth" is *tiktō* (G5088). Its gloss is "to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth)." The mother's word in Matthew's account is a word of producing from seed.

rows.synthesis:
### 1. What held at L1–L2–L3?

Points where no charge in either side's lists contested the citation, wording, or layer status:

- **Matthew 1:2**: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren." Both sides acknowledge this pattern of the verb *gennaō* (G1080) through the genealogy.
- **Matthew 1:16**: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." Both sides acknowledge the shift to the passive *egennēthē* with the feminine singular relative pronoun *ex hēs* ("of whom"), and that Joseph is designated "the husband of Mary."
- **Romans 1:3**: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Both sides acknowledge *sperma* (G4690, "seed") and *kata sarka* (*sarx*, G4561, "according to the flesh").
- **Galatians 4:4**: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." Both sides accept that the Son was "made of a woman" using the verb *ginomai* (G1096).
- **Hebrews 7:5, 10**: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham" and "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Both sides acknowledge that *osphys* (G3751, "loin") is used across generations and is paired with *patēr* (G3962, "father").
- **Luke 1:27 and Luke 2:4**: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary" and "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)." Both sides acknowledge that Joseph is explicitly named as being of the house and lineage of David.
- **Numbers 1:2, 18**: "by the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their polls" and "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Both sides acknowledge that pedigree registration under Moses is reckoned by the fathers' house.
- **Ezra 2:61–62**: Priests' children who "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name" sought their register, "but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood." Both sides acknowledge that reckoning by a wife's name resulted in removal from the priesthood register.
- **Genesis 4:1**: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." Both sides acknowledge this as the canonical statement of conception following a husband knowing his wife.
- **Deuteronomy 22:23–24**: The law terms a betrothed damsel both "a virgin" and "his neighbour's wife." Both sides acknowledge that betrothal carries the title "wife" prior to cohabitation.
- **Luke 2:48–49**: Mary says, "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing," and Jesus answers, "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Both sides acknowledge that Mary addresses Joseph as "thy father" and that Jesus speaks of His Father.
- **Luke 3:23**: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli." Both sides acknowledge that the verb *nomizō* (G3543) appears here in the form *enomizeto*, rendered "as was supposed," and that the same verb appears in Acts 16:13 ("where prayer was wont to be made").
- **Luke 1:32**: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." Both sides acknowledge that this promise precedes Mary's question in Luke 1:34.

#### Unresolved Competing Chains

##### 1. The Route of David's Seed and Hebrews 7:14 Tribal Evidence
- **Defender's Position:** Christ is "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3) through Mary, fulfilling "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30), because "loins" can span remote generations as shown in Hebrews 7:5 ("though they come out of the loins of Abraham"). Galatians 4:4 ("made of a woman") identifies the maternal human source, while the legal reckoning in the register comes through Joseph's house (Luke 2:4).
- **Challenger's Position:** Pedigree must be declared "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18). Hebrews 7:10 specifies "he was yet in the loins of his father," showing seed descending step by step through fathers. Those reckoned after a mother's house were "as polluted, put from the priesthood" (Ezra 2:62). Therefore, for the Lord's tribe to be "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14), the seed proceeded through Joseph, whose Davidic lineage is explicitly stated in Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4, and Matthew 1:16.

##### 2. The Timing of Matthew 1:18, 20, 24, 25 and Genesis 4:1
- **Defender's Position:** Matthew 1:18 states "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." *Sunerchomai* (G4905) carries the sense of conjugal cohabitation, placing the conception prior to any sexual union. Mary confirms this in Luke 1:34: "seeing I know not a man." Matthew 1:25 states Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son," bounding the abstinence through the birth and leaving no span for a union.
- **Challenger's Position:** The finding occurred "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18), where "came together" is answered by Matthew 1:24, "and took unto him his wife" (*paralambanō*, receiving her into his home). They were already legally husband and wife ("Joseph her husband," 1:19; "Mary thy wife," 1:20; Deuteronomy 22:24). The canon's established means of conception is "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1). Matthew 1:25 ("knew her not till") bounds abstinence to the gestation following the taking; hence Joseph knew Mary within the espousal prior to the public finding.

##### 3. The Sense of "Of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20) and "Son of God" (Luke 1:35)
- **Defender's Position:** Matthew 1:20 margin renders "conceived" as *gennaō* ("begotten"), which with *ek pneumatos hagiou* assigns the begetting of the child in the womb to the Holy Ghost as source. In Luke 1:35, the Holy Ghost coming upon Mary and the power of the Highest overshadowing her provides the causal ground (*dio kai*, "therefore also") for why "that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **Challenger's Position:** *Gennaō ek theou* ("begotten of God") is said of living believers who have natural fathers (1 John 5:1). John 3:6 distinguishes: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." Romans 1:3–4 assigns the flesh to the seed of David and the divine sonship to the Spirit of holiness declared by the resurrection. "Son of God" is a Davidic covenant title (2 Samuel 7:14; 1 Chronicles 28:6; Psalm 2:7; Acts 13:33). The angel's verbs (*eperchomai*, *episkiazō*) designate divine empowerment and presence (Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34), not biological paternity of flesh.

##### 4. The Change of Verb in Matthew 1:16 and Luke 3:23's Parenthesis
- **Defender's Position:** Matthew 1:16 breaks the continuous chain of active *egennēsen* ("begat") that began at Matthew 1:2, deliberately shifting to the passive *egennēthē ex hēs* ("was born of whom"), withholding the verb "begat" from Joseph. Luke 3:23 qualifies Joseph's relation as "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph," with *enomizeto* indicating a reputed reckoning by onlookers.
- **Challenger's Position:** The feminine passive in Matthew 1:16 names the mother's bearing, matching phrases like "born of a woman" (Job 14:1; Galatians 4:4; Matthew 11:11) used of men who possess biological fathers. In Luke 3:23, *nomizō* carries the sense of legal usage and custom (as in Acts 16:13), pointing to formal pedigree reckoning by the father's house. Both the narrator and Mary explicitly use parental terms: "his parents" (Luke 2:27, 41) and "thy father and I" (Luke 2:48).

##### 5. Isaiah 7:14, 8:3–4 and Matthew 1:23
- **Defender's Position:** Isaiah 7:14 gives a miraculous sign (*'ot*): "a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." Matthew 1:23 applies this directly to Christ's birth using *parthenos* (G3933). Isaiah 8:3 describes a different woman ("the prophetess"), an ordinary conception ("approached"), and a differently named child (Mahershalalhashbaz).
- **Challenger's Position:** Isaiah 7:14 is bounded in Ahaz's immediate day by 7:16 ("before the child shall know to refuse the evil... the land... shall be forsaken of both her kings"), which parallels the bound in Isaiah 8:4 ("before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother") following a natural conception (8:3). Matthew 1:22–23's fulfillment citation applies an earlier historical type to Christ (analogous to Matthew 2:15 quoting Hosea 11:1), which does not eliminate the natural order of human generation.

### 5. Most Vulnerable Points

#### Defender's Most Vulnerable Ground
- **The Tribal Lineage Mechanism:** Defender asserts that Davidic seed was transmitted according to the flesh through Mary ("the woman is the channel through which David's seed reached him" [CR2]), while conceding that "The registers do carry tribes by fathers' houses, and Luke 2:4 places Joseph in David's house, so the reckoned tribe is secure through the household" [CR4]. Under the biblical floor cited, Numbers 1:18 establishes that pedigrees are declared "by the house of their fathers," Ezra 2:62 records that those reckoned after a woman's house were "as polluted, put from the priesthood," and the New Testament text explicitly attaches the house of David to Joseph (Luke 1:27: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David"; Luke 2:4: "he was of the house and lineage of David"), leaving Mary's own tribal register unstated in the text.
- **The Extent of the Espousal Span:** Defender argues that "no span remains in which Joseph could have known her and begotten the child" [CR2] based on Matthew 1:18 ("before they came together") and Matthew 1:25 ("knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"). However, Defender concedes that Deuteronomy 22:23–24 names a betrothed woman "wife" while yet a virgin, and that Matthew 1:25's *heōs* ("till") "bounds the abstaining to the pregnancy after the taking" [CR4], creating tension with the assertion that the espousal itself could accommodate no union prior to the finding.

#### Challenger's Most Vulnerable Ground
- **The Direct Text of Matthew 1:18:** The text states: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Challenger's premise that "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is the fruit of his loins" [CR3] requires *sunerchomai* ("came together") to refer exclusively to the formal home-taking of Matthew 1:24 (*paralambanō*) rather than marital relations, despite *sunerchomai* carrying the recognized lexical sense of conjugal union.
- **The Grammatical Shift at Matthew 1:16:** Throughout Matthew 1:2–16, the genealogy uses the active transitive verb *egennēsen* ("begat") thirty-nine times from father to son. At verse 16, the text alters this syntax: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." Challenger's argument that this passive construction (*egennēthē ex hēs*) merely denotes the mother-side bearing while Joseph remained the begetter rests on comparative inference (Job 14:1; Galatians 4:4) rather than an explicit active begetting verb connecting Joseph to Jesus in the text.

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

The footing is Luke 1:34, with Matthew 1:25 and Matthew 1:18 beside it.

- **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is the verb of Matthew 1:25 "knew her not". It is also the verb of Genesis 4:1 "Adam knew Eve".
- **[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". Luke 1:27 names Mary "a virgin espoused". The conception is still future at the angel's word, and Mary says she knows no man at that time, inside the espousal.
- **[L4]** At the moment the espousal stands, Mary says "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34). The conception is then put on "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee" (Luke 1:35). So the espousal supplies no span of union. This rests on Luke 1:34 and Luke 1:31, not on *synerchomai* alone.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:

- **Matthew 1:18**, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost". I grant that *heuriskō* ("to find") dates the finding before the coming together. The verse gives the source of the child at the finding: "of the Holy Ghost". The child is already in her before the taking of Matthew 1:24.
- **Matthew 1:24**, "and took unto him his wife". I grant that *paralambanō* ("to receive near, associate with oneself") and *synerchomai* ("cohabit (conjugally)") share the sense of association. If the coming together is the taking, the child of Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her", was already conceived before it.
- **Matthew 1:19**, "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man]... was minded to put her away privily". *Anēr* (G435, "a man... husband") names the title. *Apolyō* (G630, "to free fully... divorce") names the plan. Both stand at the finding of the child. The angel's answer to that plan gives a reason: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20).
- **Matthew 1:20**, "Mary thy wife". *Gynē* (G1135, "a woman; specially, a wife") names her title. The reason clause that follows names the source of the child.
- **Deuteronomy 22:24**, "his neighbour's wife". I grant the betrothed is called a wife. Deuteronomy 22:23 calls the same betrothed "a damsel [that is] a virgin... betrothed unto an husband". The law gives the title "husband" and the word "virgin" in one verse. So the title does not supply a union.
- **Matthew 1:25**, "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". *Heōs* (G2193, "until") carries "knew her not" up to the bringing forth. That covers the whole time to the birth, the espousal included.
- **Genesis 4:1**, "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". I grant that this is Adam's way of begetting. Matthew 1:25 uses the same verb of Joseph, "knew her not", up to the birth.
- **2 Samuel 7:12**, "which shall proceed out of thy bowels". *Yatsa* (H3318, "to go out") and *qereb* (H7130, "inward part") name seed going out of David. Hebrews 7:5 shows "they come out of the loins of Abraham" across generations. Luke 1:32 says "his father David", and *patēr* (G3962) is "near or more remote". The promise fits a descendant of David.

---

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

The footing is Matthew 1:2 and Matthew 1:16, with Matthew 1:20.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". The pattern is "begat".
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". The verb changes at the last link. The name given to Joseph is "husband of Mary", *anēr* (G435, "man... husband").
- **[L2]** *Gennaō* (G1080) is "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". The passive with the feminine "of whom" names Mary as the one of whom he was born.
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:2 sets "begat" as the pattern. Matthew 1:16 turns to the passive with the woman as source. That change is stated in the verses themselves.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:

- **Matthew 1:20**, "Joseph, thou son of David... that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]". The title "son of David" is the address that opens the charge to take his wife. The reason clause names the source of "that which is conceived [begotten] in her": the *pneuma* (G4151, "spirit") that is *hagios* (G40, "sacred, consecrated").
- **Matthew 1:21**, "thou shalt call his name JESUS". Luke 1:31 says "shalt call his name JESUS" to Mary. Isaiah 8:3 says "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz" to the prophet. Naming is told to Mary and to Isaiah. It does not mark fathering.
- **Matthew 1:25**, "and he called his name JESUS". Joseph does what he was told, and his act in this verse is the calling of the name. *Tiktō* (G5088) is "to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth)". The gloss names the producer as "a mother", and the subject of "brought forth" in Matthew 1:25 is Mary, "her firstborn son". The verse gives Joseph the verb "called" and gives the bringing forth to her.
- **Matthew 11:11**, **Job 14:1** and **Luke 2:7**. I grant that "born of women" and "brought forth" are said of men with fathers. The link does not rest on those phrases. It rests on the change of verb at Matthew 1:16.
- **Luke 1:62**, "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called". I grant that this verse names a father. It names Zacharias as John's father, as Luke 1:13 does.

---

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

The footing is Luke 1:34 and Luke 1:35.

- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** *Eperchomai* (G1904, "to come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "to cast a shade upon") are the verbs that precede "therefore". They stand in the answer to Luke 1:34.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The "how" asks about the conceiving of Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". Luke 1:35 answers that question.
- **[L4]** The "therefore also" follows the two causes in its own verse. Those causes answer a question about conceiving. So the cause of the child is divine. The link gives no human man as source.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:

- **Luke 1:32**, "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". I grant that the title is given here before the question. Luke 1:35 gives a ground for the title in the same row that carries "born of thee". "His father David" is *patēr* "near or more remote".
- **1 Chronicles 28:6**, "for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". The named ground there is "I have chosen". The named ground in Luke 1:35 is the Holy Ghost coming upon her and the power overshadowing her.
- **2 Samuel 7:14** and **Hebrews 1:5**. I grant that "I will be his father" is a covenant formula said of David's seed. Luke 1:35 adds a cause on the mother.
- **Acts 13:33**, **Hebrews 5:5** and **Romans 1:4**. I grant the sonship is applied at the resurrection ("declared [to be]... by the resurrection", margin "determined"). A thing declared is declared of one already so. Luke 1:35 gives the title before birth, "shall be called".
- **Acts 1:8**, "the Holy Ghost is come upon you", and **Luke 9:34**, "overshadowed them". I grant that these name power and presence. In Luke 1:35 the same verbs are set on Mary in answer to "I know not a man".
- **Luke 1:36**, "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age", with **Luke 1:13**, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". I grant that Elisabeth's wonder has a named husband. Her case is a sign set beside Mary's, as the word "also" says. Mary's own words are "I know not a man", and the answer names the Holy Ghost.

---

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED**

The footing is Luke 3:23 and Luke 2:48-49.

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli".
- **[L2]** *Hōs* (G5613, "in that manner, according as") makes "supposed" a manner of reckoning. By the challenger's own gloss, *nomizō* is "to do by law (usage)". The ground named is law and usage, not begetting.
- **[L3]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The next verse answers "thy father" with "my Father's".
- **[L4]** Luke sets the sonship in parentheses as a reckoning. The child sets his Father against "thy father" in the very next verse. So the view held by others is not the writer's statement of fact.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:

- **Acts 16:13**, "where prayer was wont to be made". I grant that this is a true custom. A custom is reckoned by usage, and that is the sense I hold for Luke 3:23.
- **Luke 2:27, 2:41**, "the parents", "his parents". I grant the narrator's word "parents". It is the household's legal reckoning. Luke 2:33 and 2:43 give "Joseph and his mother". The narrator attaches the relation word to Mary, and Joseph is named by name.
- **Luke 2:48**, "thy father and I". *Patēr* (G3962) is "near or more remote". The next verse answers it with "my Father's business".
- **John 6:42**, "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" These are the townspeople's own words. The same people go on, "how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?"
- **John 1:45** and **Luke 4:22**, "the son of Joseph", "Is not this Joseph's son?" These are reports and questions in the speakers' mouths.
- **Heli.** *Huios* (G5207) is "immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship". The "[the son]" before Heli is supplied in italic. Matthew 1:16 names Joseph's begetter: "Jacob begat Joseph". So Luke 3:23 does not fix Heli as Joseph's begetter.

---

**LINK 5: SUPPORTED**

The footing is Isaiah 7:14 and Isaiah 8:3, with Matthew 1:23.

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
- **[L2]** *'Ot* (H226) is "a signal... evidence... token". *'Almah* (H5959) is "a lass... damsel, maid, virgin".
- **[L3]** Genesis 24:43 prints "the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]". Genesis 24:16 says of the same damsel, "a virgin, neither had any man known her". Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son".
- **[L4]** The KJV prints "virgin" at Isaiah 7:14 and for the damsel of Genesis 24:43. Matthew 1:23 gives the verse to this birth. The two together carry a conception from a woman and God.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:

- **Isaiah 7:16** and **8:4**. I grant that these share a bound in Isaiah's day. A sign has a near frame, and the lexicon the challenger names calls Immanuel "a type name". A type is a pattern for what it points to.
- **Isaiah 8:3**, "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son... Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz". The LORD names that child Mahershalalhashbaz. Isaiah 7:14 names its child Immanuel, and the mother there is "a virgin".
- **Isaiah 8:8**, "thy land, O Immanuel". It addresses Immanuel as owner of Judah's land. That fits "the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32).
- **Proverbs 30:19**, "the way of a man with a maid". I grant that the KJV prints "maid" there. It prints "virgin" at Isaiah 7:14 and Genesis 24:43, where verse 16 says "neither had any man known her".
- **Hebrews 2:14, 2:17** and **1 Corinthians 15:38**. I grant that "took part of the same" and "made like unto [his] brethren" name a body of flesh and blood. Hebrews 2:16 names "the seed of Abraham", which came to him by the woman (Galatians 4:4). "To every seed his own body" and "a body hast thou prepared me" (Hebrews 10:5) name the preparer. In Hebrews 10:5 the preparer is God, "thou hast prepared me".

---

**LINK 6: SUPPORTED**

The footing is Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30, with Luke 1:35 and Galatians 4:4.

- **[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee".

# CLOSE ROUND: THE DEFENDER

Chain numbering stays D1 to D6 as declared. The challenger's blocks stay C1 to C6. Every witness the challenger pressed in its link round is answered below by reference and quotation.

---

## ANSWERS TO THE WITNESSES

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:18 -- D1 --** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *Sunerchomai* (G4905, "to come together... specially, cohabit (conjugally)") stands in this verse. *Heuriskō* (G2147, "to find") dates the finding as already past at the moment the verse speaks.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The child is already conceived when the angel speaks to Joseph.
- [L4] The challenger (C2) dates the knowing of Genesis 4:1 "before the finding, within the espousal." Matthew 1:18 puts the finding "before they came together." *Sunerchomai* carries the conjugal sense. A knowing before the finding is therefore a coming together before the finding, and the verse sets the opposite order. The challenger's own timing row defeats the challenger's link. The verse's source phrase, "of the Holy Ghost," stands at the finding. D1 stands.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:24 -- D1 --** "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:"
- [L2] *Paralambanō* (G3880, "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself") names Joseph's receiving of Mary into his house.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L4] The taking is commanded at 1:20 with a reason given: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The conception is already in her when the taking is commanded, and the stated ground of the taking is its source. The sequence is the finding (1:18), the command with the source named (1:20), then the taking (1:24). The stated ground of the taking is the Holy Ghost, so the order puts the receiving of Mary after the conception. D1 stands.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:25 -- D1 --** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
- [L2] *Heōs* (G2193, "until") bounds the clause. *Tiktō* (G5088, "to produce... as a mother") is the verb of her bringing forth.
- [L3] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man]... was minded to put her away privily."
- [L4] The challenger (C2) bounds the abstaining to the pregnancy after the taking. I grant that bound. At 1:19 Joseph, called "her husband," is "minded to put her away" (*apolyō*, G630, "to divorce"), and at 1:20 the cure given him is the source, "of the Holy Ghost." The answer the angel gives the troubled husband is the Holy Ghost, which meets his trouble at its cause. D1 stands.

**ANSWER: Deuteronomy 22:24 -- D1 --** "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife"
- [L1] Deuteronomy 22:23: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband."
- [L2] *Bethulah* (H1330, "a virgin") and *'ishshah* (H802, "wife") are both applied to the betrothed in the same law.
- [L4] The challenger granted that "a title alone is not an act." The law names the betrothed "wife" while she is still a "virgin." Matthew 1:19 and 1:20 ("Joseph her husband," "Mary thy wife") therefore carry the same espousal title, which is a betrothal title. D1 stands.

**ANSWER: 1 John 5:1 -- D1 --** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him."
- [L2] *Gennaō* (G1080) is "to procreate... figuratively, to regenerate." In 1 John 5:1 it has believers as its object.
- [L3] John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- [L4] In 1 John 5:1 the verb is figurative regeneration of persons who already believe, and so already exist. In Matthew 1:20 its object is "that which is conceived in her," a thing in a womb (Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb"). A conceived thing has no earlier existence for the figure to refer to. The same verb with the same "of" names source, and here the source is "the Holy Ghost." John 3:6 contrasts "born of the flesh" with "born of the Spirit." Matthew 1:20 states the second source for the child: "is of the Holy Ghost." D1 stands.

**ANSWER: John 3:6 -- D1 --** "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- [L2] *Gennaō* (G1080) stands in both halves of the verse, so the verb takes either source.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20, margin "begotten": "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L4] The challenger places Matthew 1:20 on the spirit side of John 3:6. Then the source of that which is begotten in her is the Holy Ghost. Matthew 1:20 states that source in its own words, "is of the Holy Ghost," and gives it as the reason for taking Mary. The challenger's own placement therefore supports D1.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:16 -- D2 --** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L2] *Egennēsen* (G1080, "begat") governs every earlier clause of the line. *Gennaō* returns here as a passive with the feminine relative "of whom" (*ex hēs*, "out of whom, feminine"), whose antecedent is Mary. *Tiktō* (G5088, "as a mother") is the mother's verb in Luke 2:7.
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren."
- [L4] The challenger (C1, C5) reads "Jacob begat Joseph" as the last begat-step carrying the tribe to Joseph. I grant that step. Jesus is the next link in the line, and for him the active "begat" gives way to the passive "was born" of the woman alone. Joseph's title at that point is "the husband of Mary." The break from the pattern of 1:2 to 1:16 is in the verse's words. D2 stands.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:34 -- D3 --** "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is in the present tense: her state at the angel's word.
- [L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son."
- [L4] The challenger (C2) grants her present state and places the conceiving after it, within the espousal. Her question asks how conceiving is to be, and she gives her own ground: "seeing I know not a man." Joseph was already "espoused" at 1:27, so a coming knowledge from him was within her view when she asked. The angel's answer takes up her ground and gives a cause of a different kind: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee" (1:35). D3 stands.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:35 -- D3 --** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *Eperchomai* (G1904, "to come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "to cast a shade upon") are the verbs of the two causes. *Dio kai* ("therefore also") draws a consequence from them. *Hagios* (G40, "sacred") names the thing.
- [L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L4] The challenger (C3, C4) grants that these two causes act on Mary and grounds a title only. But the thing that "shall be called the Son of God" is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The clause after "therefore" names the child as born of her, the one on whom the causes act. The causes answer the "how" of conceiving that her question set, and the title follows from that origin. D3 stands.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:32 -- D3 --** "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:"
- [L2] *Kaleō* (G2564, "to call") is the verb here and in 1:35.
- [L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
- [L4] The challenger reasons that the title is given at 1:32 before the question at 1:34, so 1:35 only adds a calling. But 1:32 is spoken to Mary and calls David "his father." Hebrews 7:10 uses "his father" for a remote forefather (the challenger's own step-by-step reading at C1 grants this). So "father" in Luke 1:32 reaches an ancestor, and it is no proof of a begetter in the household. The title in 1:32 is a promise. The "therefore also" of 1:35 attaches that promise to the cause. D3 stands.

**ANSWER: 1 Chronicles 28:6 -- D3 --** "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- [L2] *Bachar* (H977, "to choose") is the verb of the adoptive ground there. In Luke 1:35 the ground is *eperchomai* (G1904, "to come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "to cast a shade upon"), acts upon the mother.
- [L3] 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- [L4] 1 Chronicles 28:6 sets a chosen sonship beside "Solomon thy son," where David's fatherhood is named in the same verse. In Luke 1:35 the verse names causes acting on the mother and a thing "born of thee," and the sonship follows from those. The two rows rest on different grounds: choosing in one, coming upon and overshadowing in the other. D3 stands.

**ANSWER: Psalms 2:7 -- D3 --** "Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee."
- [L3] Acts 13:33: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again." Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead." Hebrews 5:5: "Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee."
- [L4] Romans 1:4 uses "declared" (margin "determined"). The resurrection declares a sonship already held. Luke 1:35 gives that sonship before birth, to "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The psalm applied at the resurrection adds a second declaration over the first. D3 stands.

**ANSWER: Acts 1:8 -- D3 --** "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me"
- [L2] *Eperchomai* (G1904, "to come upon") is the verb of Luke 1:35.
- [L3] Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee."
- [L4] In Acts 1:8 the Holy Ghost comes upon persons already born, and the result stated is "power" and witness. In Luke 1:35 the result of the coming is stated as "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The two verses share a verb and differ in result. Luke 9:34 shows the cloud acting on disciples, and the result there is fear. Luke 1:35 names a born child as the outcome. D3 stands.

**ANSWER: Matthew 1:21 -- D4 --** "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins."
- [L2] *Kaleō* (G2564, "to call") is given to Joseph here and to Mary at Luke 1:31.
- [L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS."
- [L4] The challenger (C5) grants that the name is told to both parents. A deed given to both parents cannot mark one as the begetter. Matthew 1:21 gives the bearing to her, "she shall bring forth," and the naming to him, "thou shalt call." The reputed-father office in D4 consists of just that naming and household care. D4 stands.

**ANSWER: Luke 1:13 and Luke 1:62 -- D4 --** "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." / "And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called."
- [L2] *Kaleō* (G2564) is the naming verb in both.
- [L3] Luke 1:5: "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron, and her name [was] Elisabeth." Luke 1:36: "she hath also conceived a son in her old age."

At Luke 1:62 the naming office is called the father's. At Luke 3:23 the office the household gives Joseph is the reputed one: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." The two texts share the office of naming, and Luke 3:23 qualifies Joseph's sonship with "as was supposed." D4 stands.

**ANSWER: Luke 2:48 -- D4 --** "Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L2] *Nomizō* (G3543, "to reckon") is the verb in Luke 3:23's "as was supposed."

Luke 3:23 qualifies Joseph's sonship as "supposed," and John 6:42 records what the people "know." Mary's word names the man in the household who bore a father's office. D4 stands.

- [L3] Numbers 1:2: "after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names, every male by their polls." Luke 2:4: "he was of the house and lineage of David."

- [L2] *Yada'* (H3045, "to know") is the verb of the ordinary conception.

- [L2] The margin of 8:3 reads "approached" (*qarab*). *'Almah* (H5959, "virgin") stands at Isaiah 7:14 and names the woman there. In 8:3 the woman is "the prophetess," who is approached by the prophet.

In Matthew 2:15 the application to Hosea 11:1 also fits an event the child actually underwent. By the same pattern Matthew 1:23 fits a virgin actually found with child. D5 stands.

D1 and D6 stand.

Hebrews 2:14 says he "took part of the same" flesh and blood, with the verb *metechō* (G3348, "to partake"). The text gives the flesh through the woman and God's sending. D6 stands.

## THE CHAIN, KEPT

**D1: KEPT.** The conception was "of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:18, 1:20) and the finding came "before they came together" (*sunerchomai*, G4905, conjugal coming together). The challenger's knowing "before the finding" contradicts the verse's own "before." The source for "begotten of" is given at 1 John 5:1 as regeneration of persons, against "that which is conceived in her."

Precept upon precept, the rows interlock and none is set against another.

So the record holds at [L4], footed on these rows: Christ had a biological father. Joseph, of the house and lineage of David, is the named father, and the child is "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Jesus had no human biological father

**Terms.** By "biological father" I mean the male whose begetting is the source of the child's conception. The KJV answer is that Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no man as source. God is called his Father by that conception, but not as a body begetting by seed. [L4, built on the verses below]

## 1. The source of the conception is stated as the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537 *ek*, "out of", marking source or origin; *pneuma*, "spirit"; *hagios*, "holy"). The child's origin is *out of* the Holy Ghost.

[L3] Matthew 1:20 repeats the source in the angel's words to Joseph: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The same *ek* stands here, and the verb *gennaō* (G1080, "to beget, to bring forth") appears in the passive: that which is *begotten* in her is out of the Holy Ghost.

[L4] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 each name the Holy Ghost as the source with *ek*. Matthew 1:18 places this "before they came together", so the conception precedes any union of Mary and Joseph. These two rows place the origin of the conception in the Holy Ghost and before Joseph.

## 2. Matthew's genealogy changes its grammar at Joseph

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob."

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] In the chain *egennēsen* (from G1080, "begat", active, a man as subject) runs from verse 2 to Jacob. At the last link the line does not say Joseph begat. It says *ex hēs* ("of whom", a *feminine* singular relative pronoun, so "of her") *egennēthē* (passive, "was born"). The pronoun points to Mary alone. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary" (*anēr*, G435, "husband, man").

[L4] The verb that carries every earlier father-to-son link is dropped at Joseph, and the origin is traced to Mary by a feminine pronoun. The genealogy is built on the begetting formula and then breaks it at the one place where the formula would make Joseph the father.

## 3. Mary's question and the angel's answer

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is used here of a woman's knowledge of a man in marriage. Mary says she has not known a man.

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] *Episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow") describes the power of the Highest covering Mary. The word "therefore" (*dio*) joins the conception to the title Son of God.

[L3] Luke 1:27 first fixes Mary's state: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary." The word is *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin").

[L4] Luke 1:27 says virgin, Luke 1:34 says "I know not a man", and Luke 1:35 says the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, so the answer to "How shall this be?" is an act of God and not a union with a man. The answer given is not "a man shall come". It names the Holy Ghost, and Luke 1:35 ties the child's sonship to that act by "therefore".

## 4. Joseph's response and his act of naming

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

[L4] Joseph, called "a just man", plans to put her away when he finds her with child. That is the course of a man who knows the child is not his, and the angel's reassurance answers exactly that fear. This rests on Matthew 1:19, where *dikaios* (G1342, "just, righteous") is applied to Joseph, and on Matthew 1:20, where the cause is given as the Holy Ghost and not another man.

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

[L2] *Ginōskō* again, the same verb as Luke 1:34, "knew her not" until the birth.

[L4] Joseph's non-union with Mary until the birth, shown by the Matthew 1:25 *ginōskō*, together with the Holy Ghost as source in Matthew 1:20, keeps Joseph out of the begetting. He names the child JESUS (Matthew 1:21, "thou shalt call his name JESUS") and so takes him as his own by legal act, not by begetting.

## 5. Scripture itself marks Joseph's fatherhood as supposed

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

[L2] *Enomizeto* (from *nomizō*, G3543, "to suppose, to hold by custom") marks it as the popular belief, not the fact.

[L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"

[L3] Luke 2:48 has Mary say "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing", and Luke 2:49 has Jesus answer: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

[L4] John 6:42 records the crowd's assumption, and Luke 3:23 qualifies it with "as was supposed". In Luke 2:48–49 Mary's "thy father" is met by Jesus' "my Father's business". Luke 3:23 and Luke 2:49 together show Luke correcting the popular belief and fixing the child's Father elsewhere.

## 6. The prophecy: "virgin", and God's fatherhood is not bodily

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

[L1] Matthew 1:23 quotes it: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."

[L2] The KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 stands on H5959 *ʿalmâ*. In Genesis 24:43 the KJV uses the same word for Rebekah: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water". Genesis 24:16 describes her: "a virgin, neither had any man known her" (*bethulah*, H1330, "virgin").

[L3] John 4:24 says, "God is a Spirit", and Luke 24:39 says, "a spirit hath not flesh and bones."

[L4] Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23 together name a virgin who conceives, and Genesis 24:43 with 24:16 shows the word *ʿalmâ* used of a woman no man had known. John 4:24 and Luke 24:39 show that God the Spirit has no flesh and bones, so his fatherhood of Jesus is by creative power in Luke 1:35, "the power of the Highest", and not by bodily seed. Jesus therefore has no human biological father.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. The conception of Jesus is stated to come from the Holy Ghost, before Mary and Joseph came together. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost", and [L1] Matthew 1:20; [L2] *ek* (G1537, "out of") marks the source in both verses.
2. Matthew's genealogy drops the "begat" formula at Joseph and traces Jesus' birth to Mary alone. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:2, "Abraham begat Isaac", with Matthew 1:16, "of whom was born Jesus"; [L2] *hēs* (feminine "of whom") with the passive *egennēthē* ("was born").
3. Mary, a virgin who had not known a man, is told the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest will cause the conception. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34 and Luke 1:35; [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow"); [L3] Luke 1:27, "a virgin".
4. Joseph did not know Mary until the birth, and his fatherhood is by naming and taking, not by begetting. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:25, "knew her not till she had brought forth"; [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know"); [L3] Matthew 1:19 and Matthew 1:21.
5. Scripture marks Joseph's fatherhood as supposed and sets another Father over Jesus. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23, "as was supposed"; [L2] *enomizeto* (G3543, "was supposed"); [L3] Luke 2:48–49.
6. Jesus had no human biological father; his Father is God, by the Holy Ghost's act and not by bodily seed. Footing: [L1] Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23, "a virgin shall be with child"; [L2] H5959 *ʿalmâ* (rendered "virgin") with Genesis 24:43 and 24:16; [L3] John 4:24, "God is a Spirit", and Luke 24:39.

# CHALLENGE: The seed of David according to the flesh, out of the loins of Joseph

**Terms.** By "biological father" I mean the man whose seed comes out of his loins into the child's flesh. The defender's definition, "the male whose begetting is the source," has nothing to argue with. My case is that the KJV names that man, Joseph of the house of David. The rows that join the Holy Ghost to the conception use the language of covenant origin, presence and power. They do not use the language of seed.

## MY CHAIN

**C1. The promise requires flesh seed out of a man's loins.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." The seed comes out of David's own body.

**The question:** how is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" when pedigrees run "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18)?

**Answer: by Joseph's house, through the father's act of naming, which is a legal father and not a begetting one.**

- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."

- [L4] Numbers 1:18 reckons by the father's house. Matthew 1:20 puts Joseph in David's house, and Matthew 1:21, 25 give the naming to Joseph. So the house in which the child is entered is Joseph's, by the father's act of naming.

- **[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- **[L3]** John 1:12 names who these are: "to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name." 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) is used with *ek* (G1537, "out of") in both rows.
- **[L4]** John 1:12-13 and 1 John 5:1 say "born of God" of believers, every one of whom has a father who begat him. So *ek* with God names covenant birth.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20 joins that marker to the father in one breath: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived [margin: Gr. begotten] in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L3]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- **[L4]** The flesh of "the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3) is born of flesh. What is "of the Holy Ghost" is the covenant origin, and the angel gives it as the reason (*gar*, "for") the son of David should take his wife.

## 7. Luke 1:35's "therefore"

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- **[L2]** *kaleō* (G2564, "to call") stands as "shall be called" in Luke 1:32 and again in Luke 1:35.
- The *dio kai* ("therefore") in Luke 1:35 connects back to Luke 1:32, not forward to biological divine paternity. The title and "the throne of his father David" are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.
- **[L3]** The title's source is 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- **[L3]** Psalm 2:7, "Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee," is applied in three places:
  - the resurrection, Acts 13:33: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again";
  - the priesthood, Hebrews 5:5: "to be made an high priest";
  - beside 2 Samuel 7:14, Hebrews 1:5: "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son."
- **[L4]** The same verb, "shall be called," carries the title in Luke 1:32 and 1:35. 1 Chronicles 28:6 shows that title on a son whom David begat. So the "therefore" gathers the covenant title already given.

## 8. Isaiah 7:11's sign

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:12: "But Ahaz said, I will not ask, neither will I tempt the LORD." Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign."
- **[L2]** *'ôth* (H226), in the served lexicon: "a signal... evidence, etc.; mark, miracle, (en-) sign, token."
- **[L3]** Isaiah 8:18: "Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel."
- **[L4]** The sign "in the depth, or in the height above" (Isaiah 7:11) is the one Ahaz refused at Isaiah 7:12. The sign of Isaiah 7:14 is the one the Lord gave instead. Isaiah 8:18 calls the prophet's children, conceived by approach (Isaiah 8:3, margin "Heb. approached"), "signs and... wonders."
- **[L3]** Matthew's "fulfilled" (Matthew 1:22) follows the same pattern as Matthew 2:15, "Out of Egypt have I called my son," which applies Hosea 11:1: "When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt." Both rows stand: the first in its own day, the second as the fulfilment.

## 9. Luke 3:23's "as was supposed"

- **[L1]** Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made."
- **[L2]** *nomizō* (G3543): "properly, to do by law (usage)."
- **[L3]** Acts 16:16: "as we went to prayer." The place held by usage was a real place, and they went to it.
- **[L4]** Luke 3:23 names the reckoning by law and usage. It stands with Luke's own narration:
  - "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27);
  - "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41);
  - Mary's "thy father and I" (Luke 2:48).
- "My Father's business" (Luke 2:49) carries the covenant title of 1 Chronicles 28:6, and it stands beside Mary's "thy father."

## 10. The naming answer to Hebrews 7:14 confirms my keystone

- **[L1]** Luke 1:62-63: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called... His name is John."
- **[L3]** Ezra 2:61-62: the priest "called after their name," of his wife's house, "sought their register... but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- **[L4]** In Luke 1:62-63 the father who names is the father who begat. In Ezra 2:62 a name reckoned through the wife's house does not hold. So the evident springing out of Juda (Hebrews 7:14) stands on the father's house, and that father is Joseph, "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).
- Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is the seed of David, out of Joseph's loins.
